articleTitle: Demonstrating 300 GHz Wireless Backhaul Links – The ThoR Approach
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This contribution presents the key achievements of the Horizon 2020 EU-Japan project ThoR (“TeraHertz end-to-end wireless systems supporting ultra-high data Rate applications”). Results of the hardware demonstration of 300 GHz backhaul links, the antenna characterisation, the software simulation and the automatic planning will be presented.

articleTitle: Development of Kilowatt THz Gyrotrons for Pulsed Dynamic Nuclear Polarization - Cavity Design Code Phaedra -
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A significant effort has recently been initiated at ETHZ for the development of high frequency, high power, frequency-agile gyrotrons for DNP-NMR spectroscopy. In this context an in house cavity interaction code is under development. In this paper, some details on the development of the new cavity code and the preliminary results will be presented.

articleTitle: Maximum A-Posteriori Probability (MAP) Terahertz Parameter Extraction for Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We developed a maximum a-posteriori probability-based terahertz parameter extraction method to obtain tissue characteristics of paraffin-embedded murine pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma samples. This estimation algorithm can produce conservative estimates of tissue parameters without resorting to frequency-domain analysis. We report well-resolved and statistically significant differences in tumor tissue regions as compared to their healthy counterparts using our parameters extraction algorithm. We propose to use the index of refraction and the absorption as imaging biomarker parameters for biological tissue characterization.

articleTitle: THz optical properties of different 3D printing polymer materials in relation to FTIR, Raman, and XPS evaluation techniques
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The recent fast development of terahertz technology finds applications in many technological aspects used in security, medicine, biology, telecommunication, astronomy, and many others. Each of them requires individual optical components made of well-performing materials adapted to the particular application. This work examines the optical properties of different polymer materials used in 3D printing techniques examined and verified by the terahertz time-domain spectroscopy. Moreover, composite materials significantly influence on polymer base optical and mechanical performance.

articleTitle: 3D-Printed Waveguide for 220 GHz - 325 GHz Band
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A 1-inch-long waveguide for 220-325 GHz was fabricated using our UV-curable-resin type 3D printer, RECILS and electroless plating. The waveguide, with a cross section of 860 μm × 430 μm and UG387/UM flanges at both ends, exhibits insertion loss comparable to that of commercially available metal waveguides. This technology can be used for integrated fabrication of 3D waveguides, such as bandpass filters, directional couplers, and phased arrays, with a high resolution (20-30 μm).

articleTitle: High-bandwidth FMCW THz Imaging in the 499-733 GHz Range for Defect Detection in Glass Fiber Reinforced Thermoplastics
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this research non-destructive testing technology based on 3D-THz imaging system has been implemented to detect defects in glass fiber reinforced thermoplastics (GFRT) composite materials and determine the position of the defect in depth. The 3D THz images have been generated based on frequency modulation continuous wave (FMCW) technology covering the frequency range from 499 to 733 GHz. The presented experimental results demonstrate that the 3D THz-FMCW imaging system can detect a consolidation defect with a difference in thickness around $400 \mu \mathrm{m}$ successfully.

articleTitle: Advances in Terahertz Instrumentation and Technology for Cancer Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: There is an increasing demand for diagnostic techniques capable of label-free, noninvasive and early detection of cancer. In this work, an overview of the technological advancements in the terahertz (THz) technology towards miniaturized and optimized compact THz systems is presented. We focus on THz radiation generation and detection, THz techniques and their biomedical applications for cancer detection. The scope for future studies is envisaged by identifying challenges associated with THz technology and proposing the integration of THz systems with artificial intelligence (AI), internet-of-things (IoT), cloud computing, big data analytics etc. for more sophisticated systems.

articleTitle: High Spectral Resolution Airborne Microwave Sounder (HiSRAMS)
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A high spectral resolution airborne microwave sounder has been developed by Omnisys Instruments in collaboration with the National Research Council Canada (NRC) and McGill University from a European Space Agency (ESA) funding. Two single sideband radiometers have been designed with different operating frequency range, 50 – 58 GHz and 176.3 – 184.3 GHz, observing the H and V polarizations. Each unit is composed of two heterodyne receivers combined with 2 polyphase digital Fast Fourier Transform spectrometers with 5 GHz bandwidth, with up to 16384 channels. The microwave sounder presents system noise temperatures below 250K and 850 K for the 54 GHz band and 183 GHz band, respectively. The two units have been installed onboard the NRC Convair-580 research aircraft for high spectral resolution remote sensing of the atmosphere

articleTitle: High Sensitivity THz Photomultiplier Tubes
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We demonstrate the detection of THz-to-IR frequencies using lightwave-driven cold field electron emission form a metasurface. Combined with classical photo-multiplier tube technology, a novel detector-class with high sensitivity and nanosecond response time is realised. A live imaging device is made by utilising a phosphor screen in combination with a multi-channel plate. This detector and its modifications promise to have great potential in both scientific and industrial applications.

articleTitle: UTC-PD-Integrated HEMT for Optical-to-MMW/THz Carrier Frequency Down-Conversion: Scaling Rule of Conversion Gain on UTC-PD Mesa Size
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We experimentally investigate the scaling rule of the conversion gain on UTC-PD mesa size of the UTC-PD-integrated HEMT for optical to MMW/THz frequency down-conversion. We showed that the conversion gain monotonically increases as the mesa size is reduced, due to the suppression of the in-plane diffusion of photogenerated electrons in the absorption layer.

articleTitle: Tests and Qualification of the European 1 MW, 170 GHz CW Gyrotron in an ITER relevant configuration at SPC
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: After an initial testing period at the Karlsruhe Institute of Technology, the upgraded EU 1 MW, 170 GHz continuous wave (CW) industrial prototype gyrotron (TH1509U) for Electron Cyclotron Resonance Heating and Current Drive (ECRH&CD) in ITER has been transferred to the Swiss Plasma Center (SPC) to be tested in an ITER relevant configuration, to reach the performance level required by Fusion for Energy (F4E) to qualify it for the ITER project, and to increase the pulse length to very long pulses.

articleTitle: Development of Terahertz walk-through body scanner using 300 GHz FMCW radar
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A high-throughput imaging scanner for walkthrough security gates has been developed by combining a 275-305 GHz single transceiver and a high-speed scanner. This body scanner successfully visualizes concealed objects carried by pedestrians walking at 4 km hr<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>.

articleTitle: Demonstration of a Broadband Quasi-Optical Power Distribution and Beam-Steering with Transmit Lens Arrays at 550 GHz
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A novel transmit lens array is proposed to provide broadband quasi-optical power distribution and beam-steering capabilities for array architectures in future submillimeter-wave heterodyne instruments. The transmit array is composed of a double array layer of lens antenna elements with high aperture efficiency. To enable broadband and low loss quasi-optical (QO) power distribution, the transmit lens array is coupled with a high aperture efficiency single lens antenna. The high aperture efficiency is achieved by using a recently introduced multi-mode leaky wave feed. The top lens array can be used to achieve beam-steering capabilities when fed coherently and mechanically translated using a piezo-motor. In this contribution, we present the development of a prototype based on a transmit lens array of 7 elements at 450-650 GHz with measurements showing a good agreement with simulations. This prototype demonstrates a quasi-optical power coupling efficiency of nearly 60%. Moreover it also shows beam-steering of a 36dBi directivity beam to few discrete angles up to +/-25 degrees with less than 2dB scan loss.

articleTitle: Carrierless I-Q Mixing for Terahertz Communications
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate the transmission of a carrierless quadrature amplitude-modulated signals at a data rate up to 64 Gbit/s using a 253 GHz photonics-based terahertz communications system with optical intensity modulation, 10-km single mode liber transmission and terahertz envelope detection.

articleTitle: Ultra-high Gain Transmitarray Antenna for Wireless Backhauling at 280 GHz
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: An ultra-high gain transmitarray antenna for point-to-point backhaul links at 280 GHz is presented here. The proposed array exhibits a 3-bit phase resolution, comprising only three metal layers and no metallized vias. Thanks to a dedicated synthesis procedure, the unit-cells achieve very low losses, full phase coverage and are compatible with a standard printed circuit board process. A 140×140-element transmitarray is numerically optimized and experimentally characterized, using a 10 dBi horn as a feed. A peak gain of 44.5 dBi with 52.3% aperture efficiency and 0.9° half-power beamwidth are reported at the center frequency.

articleTitle: Impedance measurements in La0.7Sr0.3MnO3 thin films for uncooled THz bolometers
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present preliminary results on the fabrication and impedance measurement of loads made of $La_{0.7}Sr_{0.3}MnO_{3}$ (LSMO) thin films on SrTiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> buffered high resistivity silicon substrates. These loads will be used in uncooled mm-wave and THz bolometers based on LSMO.

articleTitle: 0.5 THz Wave based on Two Wavelength Difference Beat with Self-Injected Diode Lasers
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We demonstrate two wavelength difference (TWD) frequency generation in the millimeter wave region based on self-injection locking of two inexpensive semiconductor diode lasers with the help of corresponding Stokes waves generated from a fiber Brillouin cavity. Such a self-injection scheme dramatically enhances performance metrics including greatly reduced phase noise and superior stability of the stimulated Brillouin scattered Stokes lasers, and in turn, of the associated TWD beat frequency, all in while culminating in a relatively inexpensive setup. Our results show ultralow phase noise levels roughly around −114 dBc/Hz and −120 dBc/Hz at Fourier frequencies of 10 kHz and 100 kHz, respectively.

articleTitle: Broadband and efficient terahertz beam scanning using a 3D-printed Risley prism
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present a Risley prism beam-scanning system for terahertz waves. The scanning system consists of two 3Dprinted prisms made of cyclic olefin copolymer (COC), which is a low loss material at terahertz frequencies. The two prisms are mounted in a custom-fabricated, motorised holder to rotate the two prisms independently with high precision. A maximum beam deflection angle of 10.5 ° is demonstrated experimentally over a frequency range of 220 GHz to 330 GHz, with an average transmission efficiency of 81.5%.

articleTitle: Broadband liquid sensing of sealed microfluidic channel using mm-wave dielectric rod waveguide
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A sealed microfludic channel is situated close to a mm-wave dielectric waveguide in order to determine the impact of evanescent interaction with the liquid in broadband. A water-filled channel is observed reduce transmission by up to 53 dB, and to cause >10 dB loss over an 86% relative bandwidth. This indicates compatibility with biomedical applications for which aqueous solutions are commonly deployed, and the use of sealed liquid volumes reduces the risk of handling infectious substances.

articleTitle: Comparison of non-destructive examination methods for wax-resin lining of paintings on canvas
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Wax-resin lining, a kind of additional support for oil painting on canvas, was frequently applied in the 20th century and has preserved many artworks till today. Some of them, however, have issues to be examined when considering the further conservation. For the examination of wax-resin lining, which was reproduced so as to partly delaminate from the painting, three types of non-destructive inspection methods were applied and compared. The results of the experimental examination using them proved how certain methods were effective not only to locate delamination of lining, but also to observe its state.

articleTitle: Noise analysis, noise reduction and covariance estimation for Time domain Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Time domain spectroscopy is now 30 year old and spread more and more along many fields of analytical sciences. The specificity of this technique reads in its name: measurements are not done in the frequency domain using a dispersive element, but in the time domain. One of the consequences is that the data processing is specific as well and shows both complexity and opportunities. In this conference, we will present a thorough noise analysis as well as a method to reduce it in order to take the full benefit of the dynamic range in the case of relatively strong signals.

articleTitle: Low phase noise 300 GHz generation from laser diodes injection-locked to a dissipative Kerr soliton microcomb
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We investigate injection-locking low cost laser diodes (LD's) to a dissipative Kerr soliton (DKS) frequency comb. The locked LD's improve the optical signal to noise of the comb teeth by over 35 dBm/nm while maintaining the low phase noise and frequency stability of the microcomb repetition rate. The resulting laser lines can be photomixed down to produce precision THz radiation.

articleTitle: MIMO Design of 12x64 Element Polarization Sensitive SiGe Array for 3D In-line Detection of Defects at 220-260 GHz
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Non-destructive testing of glass fiber-reinforced composites in mass production requires suitable in-line testing methods that allow single part inspection for quality assurance. We show a design for a MIMO array whose high number of elements can accelerate the measurement process and enables inline capable 3D imaging systems. The MIMO array achieves a lateral resolution of 1mm and provides for the first time a polarization selective arrangement to better detect defects as deviations in the periodic structures of composite materials. Furthermore, the design of the high frequency PCBs for the installation of the SiGe receivers is shown as a first step on the way to a 3D imaging system.

articleTitle: E-band Traveling Wave Tube for High Data Rate Wireless Links
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: E-band (71 – 76 GHz and 81 – 86 GHz) is already used for point to point links with a few Gigabit/second data rate. Front-ends are powered by solid state amplifiers with about 2 – 3 W output power. This output power values limit range and spectral efficiency and have to be compensated by high gain antennas. The availability of tens of Watt would allow higher spectral efficiency and long range, and the use of lower gain antennas for multibeam and area coverage. This paper reports the design and the initial fabrication of the first ever E-band Traveling Wave Tube (TWT) based on the double corrugated waveguide. A test short interaction structure TWT is in assembly phase as proof of concept with about 2 W output power. The final TWT is designed to provide about 70 W power and about 40 dB gain.

articleTitle: Diffraction-Limited Imaging Demonstration using a Silicon Integrated Array at Terahertz Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this contribution we will present the diffraction-limited imaging capabilities of a focal plane array (FPA) of antenna-coupled direct-detectors at submillimeter wavelengths. The FPA prototype is a tightly sampled, 12-pixel array that was developed in a 22 nm CMOS technology and it covers a band from 200 GHz to 600 GHz. A quasi-optical (QO) setup was developed to actively illuminate this FPA in order to perform imaging with $\gt$ 40 dB SNR. The resulting images will be the first that have diffraction-limited angular resolution at these wavelengths, which demonstrates that this FPA design can be very attractive for future passive THz imaging applications.

articleTitle: On-Chip Terahertz Sensor Based on Low-Loss Coplanar Strip Lines for the Analysis of Microscale Two-dimensional Materials
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this study, a low-loss on-chip Terahertz (THz) sensor for future analysis of microscale two-dimensional (2D) materials has been investigated. The sensor is fabricated with the coplanar strip (CPS) lines patterned on a low permittivity polymer substrate that offers a wide usable THz bandwidth as well as controlled and efficient access to small samples combined with mechanical robustness. The applied THz signal is highly confined within the CPS transmission lines and recorded via time-resolved photo-conductive (PC) sampling. The architecture includes a separable sample carrier film integrated with the sensor, designed to probe very small 2D material sections with high sensitivity to electronic material properties.

articleTitle: Dielectric Rod Waveguide-based Radio-Frequency interconnect operating from 55 GHz to 340 GHz
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present a novel concept for high-frequency interconnects based on dielectric rod waveguide structures, which show a broadband operating frequency range. The low cut-off frequency is set at 50 GHz by design, while the upper limit extends beyond 340 GHz. An experimental demonstration is presented to validate the concept. The presented RF interconnect approach covers several rectangular waveguide bands with potential to be extended to terahertz range.

articleTitle: Core-Shell Leaky-Wave Lens Antenna for 150GHz Fly’s Eye Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This work presents a novel lens antenna architecture based on a core-shell lens design with a leaky-wave in-packaged antenna at 150GHz. An electrically small core lens made of dense dielectric material is used to enhance the radiation of the in-packaged antenna. A low-loss dielectric shell lens with electrically large dimensions is then added to provide high directivity. A microstrip feeding network for connection to a 150GHz chipset is then also discussed. The proposed lens antenna provides good quality patterns with aperture efficiencies above 80% over a bandwidth of 20%.

articleTitle: Chip-Scalable, Graphene-Based Terahertz Thermoelectric Photodetectors
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We report room temperature terahertz detection in large-area single layer graphene (SLG) grown by chemical vapor deposition (CVD), integrated in antenna-coupled field effect transistors. We employ different dielectric thin layers as substrate termination (SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>,Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>) and different layers as top encapsulation (HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> or large-area CVD-grown hexagonal boron nitride), to investigate the effect of the surrounding layers on SLG thermoelectric properties underpinning photodetection. With these scalable architectures, response times ~5 ns and noise equivalent powers ~1 nWHz<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1/2</sup> are achieved under zero-bias operation.

articleTitle: Fast Terahertz 3D Super-Resolution Surface Reconstruction by Variational Model from Limited Low-Resolution Sampling
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Integrating with the signal processing, inverse Radon transform, and the variational model, the framework at least saving 83% data acquisition time for fast, smooth three-dimensional (3D) reconstruction from the limited dataset is elucidated in the field of terahertz imaging applications. In hot pursuit, under the viewpoint of discrete geometry, the quantifiable comparison for 3D surfaces by computing the standard deviation of mean curvatures is also proposed to show the reconstructed effectiveness from less input with gaps.

articleTitle: Status and First Operation of Gyrotron Teststand FULGOR at KIT
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: FULGOR, the new KIT gyrotron teststand for megawatt-class gyrotrons, will be presented. Results of initial experiments using a 1.5 MW 140 GHz short pulse pre-prototype gyrotron will be discussed.

articleTitle: Terahertz Image Reconstruction using Compressive Sensing
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The major limitation of the conventional terahertz (THz) imaging system based on a single-pixel detector is the high image acquisition time inhibiting its real-time applications. Alternatively, to reduce the image acquisition time, compressive sensing has been widely explored, wherein a reduced number of imaging points are employed to reconstruct the image. However, this technique, being extremely sensitive to the selection and ordering of the imaging masks, demands a well-formulated and efficient reconstruction algorithm. In the present work, the authors have extensively investigated the reconstruction of the THz images using a total variation minimization algorithm for different compression rates, imaging masks and optimization parameters.

articleTitle: A Waveguide Based Terahertz Variable Attenuator
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A variable attenuator is a critical component at microwave and terahertz frequencies to adjust the signal path loss-gain settings in the system. This facilitates designers and engineers to determine the optimum performance of their measurement systems and instruments. Attenuators, both fixed and tunable, are readily available at microwave frequencies however at submillimeter-wave and terahertz frequencies, design and fabrication are very challenging because such components need to be integrated with compact metal waveguide packaged sub-systems and instruments. In this work, we demonstrate a novel waveguide based variable attenuator at WR1.5 band (500-750 GHz) using a metal coated silicon slab. A piezo electric motor is used to control the position of the slab on the path of the incoming electromagnetic signal to achieve variable attenuation. The amount of attenuation is determined by the volume of silicon slab inside the waveguide and the absorption coefficient of the metal coating.

articleTitle: An Improved Reflection Head for THz-TDS Measurements
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present a novel reflection head for THz-TDS applications. Compared to the state of the art, it offers improved imaging properties, minimal optical losses and preserves the polarization state of the THz radiation. These advantages for non-destructive testing (NDT) are disclosed and first results are presented.

articleTitle: Mitigating the Nonlinearity of Radio-over-Fiber Terahertz Systems
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate a highly-precise equalization technique based on a Volterra nonlinear filter for highly nonlinear terahertz communications systems. The technique is demonstrated with a 253 GHz photonics-based terahertz system with 10-km radio-over-fiber link.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluations of Airport Runway Foreign Object Detection System Using a 96 GHz Millimeter-Wave Radar System Based on International Standard
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The airport runway Foreign Object Debris (FOD) detection system allows small objects, which could potentially damage aircraft, to be automatically detected. We have been developing an FOD detection system based on the optically-connected 96 GHz distributed-type millimeter-wave radar sensor. In this paper, the performance of the 96 GHz millimeter-wave radar sensor for FOD detection is evaluated at an airport runway, referencing the international standard. Six different types of FOD samples, as specified in EUROCAE ED-235, are evaluated. These include a tire fragment, a light, a chunk of concrete, an M10 bolt and nut, a fuel cap and a piece of metal. All dimensions of the FOD samples are reduced by almost 50% compared those described in the document. The results confirm a detection probability for all FOD samples exceeding 95%.

articleTitle: Phase Retrieval for Fourier THz Imaging with Physics-Informed Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: With the continuous progress of terahertz (THz) generating and sensing technology, THz imaging is promising for a wide application range. However, 3D scene reconstruction at THz bands faces with challenges due to the difficulty of accurate phase data recording. In this paper, we demonstrate a phase retrieval method for THz Fourier imaging based on a deep learning (DL) algorithm. This scheme incorporates Fraunhofer diffraction as the physical origin of Fourier imaging as prior knowledge. The classification and reconstruction tasks are achieved based on the dataset transplanted from MNIST. The process is composed of two steps. The supervised DL based on the prepared data for classification, and phase reconstruction and the unsupervised DL network (PhysenNet) performing de-noising. The developed DL method achieves 94% accuracy for the classification task and 0.03 mean square error for the reconstruction task, which means that complex and easily-disturbed heterodyne detection can be replaced to a certain extent.

articleTitle: Design of 20 Gbps bidirectional full-duplex real-time communication system on 220 GHz band
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: With the rapid growth of communication demand, the terahertz communication system has attracted more and more attention. The current terahertz communication system is difficult to realize long-distance bidirectional communication due to limited power and strong crosstalk. In this paper, a terahertz bidirectional real-time communication system is proposed, which can solve the problem of limited distance and interactive communication by using the duplex of terahertz amplifiers and terahertz frequencies. After simulation and extrapolation, the system can support up to 400 m 20 Gbps upstream and downstream fullduplex real-time communication.

articleTitle: Modified Waveguide Flange Mechanical Design for Compactness of THz Sources
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A modified waveguide flange is designed and implemented for compact integration of sub-millimeter-wave components. The proposed modified waveguide flange is fully compatible with the standard traditionally used millimeter-wave (mmW) and sub-millimeter-wave (sub-mmW) UG-387/UM flange, allowing a significant miniaturization of high frequency multipliers and their integration with antennas and other standard market RF components. The presented flange has been used at ACST to develop high power and full-band THz sources and compact sources, covering from 330GHz to 900GHz. This modification is expected to allow future development of sources up to 1.5 THz. This new proposed flange allows the minimization of internal propagation losses, and it adds compactness and flexibility for different applications in the THz range.

articleTitle: Preliminary Results of a 65-nm CMOS Free-running Oscillator Emitter With Tunable Radiation from 280 GHz to 292 GHz
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We report on a submillimeter-wave radiating source integrated in 65-nm CMOS technology. The source is based on a free-running differential oscillator which radiates the second harmonic of the oscillation frequency through an on-chip integrated folded-slot antenna. The chip was wire-bonded and combined with a silicon lens for backside radiation. Preliminary measurements yield tunable radiation frequency from 280.1 GHz to 291.6 GHz, with peak radiated power of -8.2 dBm for one of the measured samples. Great repeatability is observed between different samples in terms of the oscillation frequency.

articleTitle: Quantum Feature Extraction for THz Multi-Layer Imaging
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A learning-based THz multi-layer imaging has been recently used for contactless three-dimensional (3D) positioning and encoding. We show a proof-of-concept demonstration of an emerging quantum machine learning (QML) framework to deal with depth variation, shadow effect, and double-sided content recognition, through an experimental validation.

articleTitle: Sailing on Far Infrared and Submillimeter Waves Plasma Diagnostics, towards THz-TDS and beyond
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In the preface of their iconic book [1] M.A. Heald and C.B. Wharton summarize the concept of plasma diagnostics, as the instrumentation "to make unperturbed measurements of plasma parameters". The term diagnostics has medical origin, having been acquired from the studies of the effect of nuclear radiation by the Atomic Energy Commission (AEC) when the Sherwood Program for controlled nuclear fusion research was launched. This paper will give an overview of plasma diagnostics and plasma heating systems in the Far Infrared Radiation (FIR) and submillimeter waves range (100-2000 GHz) for magnetically confined plasmas in tokamaks [2]. Then the novel addition to the diagnostics landscape coming from Terahertz Time Domain Spectroscopy (THz-TDS) applications will be discussed.

articleTitle: Thickness Gauging of Waterproof Textiles using Fast THz-TDS
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Thickness gauging of high-tech textiles and their coatings is challenging as fabrics are structured, flexible materials and coatings can penetrate the surfaces during application. We present terahertz thickness measurements of waterproof yet breathable textiles consisting of microporous polypropylene film laminated to polyester fabric. Fast measurements using a terahertz time-domain spectrometer based on electronically controlled optical sampling highlight the potential for non-destructive, contact-free inline quality control of textiles.

articleTitle: 600 – 900 GHz Frequency Sources with up to 4 mW Output Power based on Flip-Chip Schottky Barrier Diodes Technology
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We report a set of three submm-wave sources able to provide > 1 mW typical output power in the 600-900 GHz frequency range. These sources are based on active multiplication chains (AMC), using ACST high power discrete Schottky diode technology. Peak power levels up to 4, 3 and 2 mW are achieved in the 600-700, 700-800 and 800-900 GHz frequency range respectively. These 600-900 GHz sources are based on three base sources covering the 200-300 GHz with an additional tripler stage at the end. All frequency multipliers in these sources are using flip-chip Schottky diodes approach, and no power combining technics are used. Equivalent performance to full MMIC Schottky multipliers is achieved using our discrete diode-based multipliers.

articleTitle: Super-Resolution Terahertz Imaging with Plasmonic Focal-Plane Arrays
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present a terahertz focal-plane array comprised of $\sim 0.3$ million plasmonic nanoantennas, which can simultaneously provide spatial, ultrafast temporal, spectral, amplitude, and phase information of imaged objects, for the first time. Taking advantage of the multi-spectral nature of the amplitude and phase data, the combination of this focal-plane array with a convolutional deep neural network enables super-resolved image reconstruction of objects with subwavelength feature sizes and thickness variations, achieving an effective pixel count larger than 1 kilo pixels.

articleTitle: The Response of Split-Well Direct-Phonon THz Quantum-Cascade Laser Structures to Changes in Doping
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We have studied the effect of doping on the temperature performance of a split-well (SW) direct-phonon (DP) terahertz (THz) quantum-cascade laser (QCL) scheme supporting a clean three-level system. We expected to obtain a similar improvement in the temperature performance to that observed in resonant-phonon (RP) schemes after increasing the carrier concentration from $3 \times 10^{10} cm ^{-2} to 6 \times 10^{10}, cm^{-2}$ To our surprise, in the devices we checked, the results show the contrary. However, we observed a significant increase in gain broadening and a reduction in the dephasing time as the doping and temperature increased. We attribute these effects to enhanced ionized-impurity scattering (IIS). The observation and study of effects related to dephasing included in our experimental work have previously only been possible via simulation.

articleTitle: Progress of the Methods for Optimum of Quasi-Optical Mode Converters at KIT
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The paper reports the progress of the methods for the synthesis of Quasi-Optical (QO) mode converters at KIT in the period from 2018 until today. Typically, the QO mode converter consists a waveguide launcher and a mirror system. The first progress done is the development of the spectrum reconstruction method for smoothing the launcher wall. The second is the improvement of the method for the design of quasi-parabolic mirrors. The third progress considers the synthesis of a Denisov-type launcher for the conversion of co- and counter-rotating modes.

articleTitle: Analysis of THz Scattering of Compacted Granular Materials using THz-TDS
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Scattering of terahertz radiation in compacts is of great interest due to its potential to non-destructively assess various structural elements such as particle size and defects in compacts. In this study, we isolate the scattering contributions to the loss coefficient of borosilicate glass microspheres suspended in a polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) compact measured by terahertz time-domain spectroscopy. The particle size and concentration of microspheres in the compacts were varied to resolve their effect on terahertz scattering.

articleTitle: A 220GHz Mono-pulse Beam Adaptive Self-Tracking Antenna for Long Distance Communication Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Due to the demand of terahertz communication for high-precision beam tracking technologies, a high-precision beam adaptive acquisition and self-tracking antenna for terahertz communication is proposed in this paper. It works at the 220GHz frequency band, which is composed of mono-pulse sum-difference network feeds, a reflector, and a two-axis high-precision servo system. The measured results show that the gain of the antenna is better than 50dBi, the beam width is 0.18°, and the zero-depth of the difference beam is better than 35dB. A kilometer-level airborne communication experiment verified the performance of the system.

articleTitle: Application of high frequency gyrotron to pulsed ESR measurement
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Gyrotron is a high-power radiation source in the millimeter and submillimeter wave region, which is suitable for the radiation source of a high frequency (high magnetic field) short-pulsed ESR system. Pulsed ESR spectroscopy system was developed using the high-power millimeter wave of gyrotron. The FID signal of stable radicals of BDPA diluted with polystyrene was successfully observed. Higher sensitivity of measurement was achieved by averaging. It became possible to measure a smaller amount of sample, and it was possible to show its usefulness from the measurement of a small sample.

articleTitle: Terahertz Oscillator using Rectangular-Cavity Resonator and Large-Area RTD with Heat Dissipation Structure
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We fabricated and demonstrated a terahertz oscillator using rectangular-cavity resonator and large-area resonant tunneling diode (RTD) with heat dissipation structure. We utilized a new RTD layer structure in which the bottom conductive layer with low-thermal conductive n<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>-InGaAs, which disturbed heat dissipation to the substrate and caused heat destruction, was replaced by high-thermal conductive<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n+</sup>-InP layer. A high output power of (~200) $\mu \ W$ was obtained at 530 GHz without heat destruction. The experimental results well agreed with the theoretical calculation.

articleTitle: THz Heterodyne System Using Novel Mixer and Local Oscillator Devices
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We demonstrated a broadband THz heterodyne receiver for astrophysics using Hot-Electron Bolometer (HEB) mixers based on high-T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">C</inf> superconducting MgB<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and Quantum Cascade Laser (QCL) as local oscillator (LO). This detector will advance the state-of-the-art by allowing an operation at elevated temperature $(\sim 20\mathrm{K})$ and providing the intermediate frequency (IF) bandwidth of about 10 GHz. Such a bandwidth is required for high-resolution spectroscopy of interstellar molecular clouds at frequencies 3-5 THz and is not currently available in NbN based HEB mixers. A lab receiver system is being developed to prototype the payload for application on balloons and SmallSats.

articleTitle: Integrated Graphene Patch Antenna for Communications at THz Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Graphene is an attractive material for communications in the THz range due to its ability to support surface plasmon polaritons. This enables a graphene antenna to be smaller in size than its metallic counterpart. In addition, the possibility to control the graphene conductivity during operation by an applied bias leads to the tunability of the resonant frequency of graphene antennas. Graphene-based antennas integrated into transceivers working at THz frequencies may lead to faster and more efficient devices. In this work, we design and simulate a graphene patch antenna that can be integrated into transceivers by through-substrate vias. The tuning of the resonant frequency is also studied by simulations.

articleTitle: Complex refractive index determination of PTFE, TPX and polypropylene windows for TeraHertz broadband spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We perform TeraHertz characterization of three low-loss polymer candidates, i.e. polytetrafluoroethylene, polymethylpentene, and polypropylene, to choose the material with the proper opto-mechanical properties for aerosol and gas broadband spectroscopy cell windows. Samples are analyzed with the TeraHertz time domain spectroscopy technique. Then, the time-traces are fitted with theoretical models and the real and imaginary parts of their complex refractive indices are extracted using the Fit@TDS algorithm developed by Photonic TeraHertz team members.

articleTitle: Classification of Terahertz Reflection Spectra using Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A successful implementation of terahertz screening systems requires a development of reliable and efficient identification algorithms. Dimensionality reduction methods are applied to lower the dimensionality of multivariate data while retaining most of the information. Here, we focus on Principal component analysis (PCA) and linear discriminant analysis (LDA) for analysis and classification of terahertz reflection spectra. The complete data set consists of more than 5000 reflection spectra of six active materials. We found that LDA is better for grouping the spectra resulting in highly accurate classification of terahertz spectra. Furthermore, we compare the classification of referenced and non-referenced reflection spectra eligible for real-world applications of terahertz spectroscopy.

articleTitle: Terahertz Meta-surface Sensor with Various Refractive Indexes Based on EIT-like Effect
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A terahertz meta-surface sensor with various refractive indexes based on electromagnetically induced transparency-like (EIT-like) is designed in this paper. The meta-surface unit is composed of a square ring and a circular ring, performing a significant transmission peak at 0.822 THz. After simulation analysis and data fitting, it is calculated that the detection sensitivity for refractive index is about 200 GHz/RIU. The results show that the meta-surface based on EIT-like designed in this paper have high sensitivity to different refractive index covers, which provides a certain reference for the research of metamaterial refractive index sensor in the future.

articleTitle: Terahertz Scanner for Improved Wood Sorting from Bulky Waste
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Wood waste has a potential to be reused or burned in energy production facilities. Improved sorting of wood waste saves resources and can reduce CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions. Therefore, we develop a terahertz scanner as one of the imaging system elements for an intelligent wood sorting system.Besides the imaging scheme, we present measurement results of relevant wood and bulky waste samples. Starting from initial investigations by means of raster scans, conveyor belt experiments with a W-band sparse array scanner at feed motions of 10 cm/s were carried out. The goal for the later demonstrator is scanning speed of more than 1 m/s.

articleTitle: New Type of Pulsed High-Power sub-THz Source Based on Helical-Type Gyro-TWTs
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A new type of microwave source for the generation of high-power ultra-short coherent pulses at 263 GHz is presented. The source is based on the idea of passive mode-locking of two microwave tubes as it was first proposed in [1]. While passive mode-locking is well-established in laser physics, this idea is new for microwave electron tubes and was first experimentally demonstrated in [2]. As electron tubes, two helical gyro-TWTs are used that are coupled by a quasi-optical feedback system. The configuration proposed in this publication extends the original setup to enable the operation of the passive mode-locked oscillator in the hard excitation regime and to allow in addition the operation of the coupled helical gyro-TWTs as two-stage amplifier and as frequency-tunable, phase-locked backward wave oscillators. The performed simulation show an expected output power above 500 W and pulse widths below 0.1 ns for an operation as passive mode-locked oscillator.

articleTitle: Ultrafast Helicity-Dependent Magnetic Switching by Optical Phonons Driven at Resonance
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Using narrow-band mid- to- far-infrared circularly-polarized optical pulses, we demonstrate that magnetization can be switched all-optically in magnetic nanostructures mounted on fused-silica and sapphire substrates. The helicity-dependent magnetic switching scales in efficiency with optical phonons characteristic of the substrate. We explain the switching in terms of a transient magnetic field originating from resonantly-driven circularly-polarized lattice vibrations in the substrate.

articleTitle: Epitaxial growth of InGaSb/AlInGaSb THz-QCL structures
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We proposed InGaSb-well-based THz-QCLs to improve laser performance such as the maximum operation temperature. For realization of the InGaSb-well-based THz-QCLs, we performed molecular beam epitaxy (MBE) growth of InGaSb/AlInGaSb layers on a GaSb substrate and succeeded in growing the InGaSb/AlInGaSb QCL structure with a low threading dislocation density.

articleTitle: Convolutional Neural Network Approach to THz Reflection Alignment
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A major obstacle to non-contact measurement of in-vivo skin samples is the alignment sensitivity of reflected THz pulses. Movement of human skin on the relevant length scales of $10 \mu \mathrm{m}$ is faster than the movement capabilities of current state of the art medical robots: this means accurate non-contact alignment when imaging human skin is currently impossible with mechanical means. Presented here is a promising neutral network approach to correct the pulse from a misaligned terahertz system. This low-cost alternative to mechanical alignment correction will contribute to the development of in-vivo biomedical applications of THz imaging.

articleTitle: Using Ultrafast Photocurrents to Manipulate Electronic Symmetry in the Weyl Semimetal TaAs
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Topological semimetals are sensitive to a breaking and restoring of symmetry, which affect both bulk and surface electronic states. Using terahertz emission and second harmonic generation spectroscopy as sensitive probes for symmetry change, we observe an all-electronic mechanism of photoinduced symmetry breaking rooted in photocurrent generation.

articleTitle: Terahertz diagnostic tool for sub-relativistic electron beams
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We report on the development of a terahertz-driven electron beam deflector, based on a rectangular dielectric-lined waveguide (DLW), and the development of a simulation framework to probe the dynamics and analyse the experimental results. We show how such a terahertz (THz) deflector provides a valuable diagnostics tool for ultrafast electron bunches.

articleTitle: Electrical Control of Mode-Locked Resonant Tunneling Diode Terahertz Oscillators
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We experimentally demonstrated electrical control of the repetition frequency and offset frequency of mode-locked resonant tunneling diode (RTD) terahertz oscillators by bias voltage modulation. These results will pave the way for the realization of stabilized terahertz frequency comb using RTD oscillators that operate at room-temperature.

articleTitle: Terahertz thin-film attenuator with 35 dB power attenuation
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present a THz thin-film attenuator with 35 dB power attenuation suitable to evaluate the linearity of a time-domain spectroscopy system.

articleTitle: An Improved Algorithm for Fringe Jump Corrections with Three-classification Unwrapping for Far-infrared Interferometer
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Line-averaged plasma electron density can be calculated by comparing the phase difference between probing signal and reference signal from the far-infrared interferometer. In the process, fringe jumps could result in incorrect data in reconstruction. In order to process the line-averaged plasma electron density signals on the Experimental Advanced Superconducting Tokamak (EAST), a new phase unwrapping algorithm by means of classification is proposed to extract density information from the phase difference, which can avoid and recover the fringe jumps in the whole process. The results showed that the improved algorithm has the advantages of real-time, high resolution, and high accuracy.

articleTitle: A Meander Trace Inserted Metamaterial Perfect Absorber for a Sub-Terahertz CMOS Image Sensor Pixel On-Chip Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A unit cell of meander trace inserted metamaterial perfect absorber (MMPA) based on electric-inductive-capacitive (ELC) resonator structure for a sub-terahertz (THz) CMOS Image Sensor Pixel’s antenna and that of 10 GHz version on a FR4 with the same topology were simulated, fabricated, and evaluated. Our MMPA was found to give 19.3 % lower resonant frequency than the conventional MMPA and 59.2 % smaller in length than the typical microstrip patch antenna while keeping a high absorption rate even with a lossy substrate, suggesting that the proposed antenna is suitable for sub-THz CMOS Image Sensors.

articleTitle: Oil shales’ THz anisotropy and imaging
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Oil shales are sedimentary rocks that could be used as seal rocks, waste storage and unconventional hydrocarbon sources. Obtaining their petrophysical characteristics is necessary to assess whether they are worth exploiting. Therefore, given that anisotropy is linked to petrophysical properties, their characterization is of great importance. Hence, we propose here to study the terahertz anisotropy of an oil shale. This last is partly related to the organic matter content, which is link to the oil yield. Moreover, we made two Terahertz images of the same sample, obtained by changing the polarization of the electric field by 90° between them. Differences show new and complementary information about the sample.

articleTitle: Resonant Terahertz Field-effect Transistors for Spectroscopic Sensing Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present a system concept which can enable spectroscopic sensing applications over a broad frequency range and with high speeds. To address spectral sensitivity at distinct frequency lines, we use antenna-coupled terahertz field-effect transistors (TeraFETs) with resonant patch antennas in combination with a broadband pulsed terahertz source with fast pulse repetition rates of 100 MHz. To enhance the spectral sensitivity at the selected frequencies, we combine the TeraFETs with resonant filters based on frequency selective surface (FSS) structures in thin metal layers. We demonstrate possible applications of spectroscopic sensing such as material identification via spectral fingerprints or water vapor monitoring.

articleTitle: Polyethylene’s Temperature Dependent Terahertz Spectrum
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The terahertz spectra of polyethylene have been observed over a wide temperature range, 6-300 K. A prominent mode has been identified and characterised at 79.6 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> at 6 K. Strong redshifting of 6.2 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> and broadening is observed upon heating to 300 K. A weak secondary mode was also observed at 6 K, but this mode quickly disappears as temperature increases. The intensity of the 79.6 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> mode is also observed to decrease dramatically upon heating from 6–300 K, reducing to two-fifths of its original intensity. The spectrum at all other terahertz frequencies is approximately temperature independent.

articleTitle: A 3-D printed Platform for a Photonic Terahertz Spectrometer to Measure a Photonic Crystal Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this work, we demonstrate a 3-D printed platform using cyclic olefin copolymer to measure a ceramic photonic crystal waveguide. An operating range from 150 GHz to 200 GHz was achieved with highly efficient coupling from a terahertz spectrometer into the platform and the sample. The measurement results agree with simulation results.

articleTitle: Sensing moisture patterns using terahertz spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We report on a novel and comprehensive method to determine leaf wetness by using machine learning algorithms applied on transmission THz time-domain data of a vast set of moisture patterns. More generally, our approach opens ways to determine properties of materials with a complex structure for which a model-based signal processing approach is not feasible.

articleTitle: Discussion on evaluation of terahertz frequency low absorbers using THz-TDS spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Difficulties exist in the evaluation of low absorbers by terahertz spectroscopy. In particular, there is a lack of substantial reports in the literature on quartz, which is expected to be a low-absorption optical material for high-power terahertz wave applications. For the refractive index, there are no detailed reports of birefringence at terahertz frequencies, and for the absorption coefficient, there is variation in past literature values. Therefore, in this study, experimental and analytical methods were investigated to discuss the optical parameters of quartz crystal in detail.

articleTitle: 3D Printed Terahertz Filter as a Broadband Frequency Reference
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A simple broadband terahertz transmission filter with strong absorption lines and medium broadband attenuation is introduced. The filter is 3D printed using a low-loss cyclic olefin copolymer (COC) filament and characterized with a time-domain and a frequency-domain terahertz spectroscopy system.

articleTitle: 13.5-mJ THz Radiation from Lithium Niobates
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Free space highly-efficient strong-field THz radiation with a single-pulse energy up to 13.5 mJ and an 800 nmto-THz conversion efficiency of 1.2% is experimentally achieved in large-size lithium niobate crystals driven by 1.2 J Ti:sapphire femtosecond laser pulses.

articleTitle: A Compound Noise Reduction Algorithm For Terahertz Imaging
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Terahertz transmission imaging has unique advantages such as non-destructive testing compared with other transmission imaging methods. However, due to the low power of terahertz laser and the obvious diffraction effect of imaging, there is usually a lot of white noise in the system in transmission imaging. Since the system uses a high-density polyethylene lens, there will be additive noise such as Newton's rings in the image. In this paper, an improved mean filtering composite denoising algorithm is used to reduce the noise of the image with a high information entropy, which solves the problem of additive noise and white noise in terahertz transmission imaging. To achieve the purpose of improving visual effects, eliminating noise interference and highlighting the imaging subject. And provide research basis for terahertz imaging image analysis, target detection and feature extraction.

articleTitle: Ultra-Sensitive Sensing of Bacteria With Terahertz Spoof Surface Plasmon Polariton Resonators
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Biosensors are key components for the early detection of diseases. As such, a higher sensitivity allows for an earlier detection or even detection before symptoms form, as most pathogens and biomarkers have extremely small concentrations. Here we present an ultra-sensitive biosensor based on the scattering of terahertz waves in a spoof surface plasmon polariton resonator on bacteria. While the strongly bound wave and the high-quality factor of the resonator allow a sensitivity in the order of single bacteria, a high selectivity – the other key feature of a good biosensor – is provided by a surface functionalization with aptamers.

articleTitle: Silicon THz Topological Photonics for 6G communications
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The global digitalization and the recent rise of artificial intelligence-based data-driven applications have directed their vectors towards terabits per second (Tbps) communication links. The existing 5G communication architect cannot fulfill this demand due to bandwidth scarcity, which has stimulated innovative technologies with a vision of 6G communication. Terahertz (THz) technologies have been identified as a critical candidate for the emerging 6G communication with the potential to provide ubiquitous connectivity and remove the barrier between physical, digital, and biological worlds. Nonetheless, the existing THz on-chip communication devices suffer from scattering loss, bending loss, limited data speed, and lack of active tunability. Here, I will describe a new class of active on-chip THz topological devices consisting of broadband single channel 160 Gbit/s communication link and ultrahigh-Q (Q ~ 106) cavities built on Silicon Valley Photonic Crystal. Silicon topological photonics will pave the path for augmentation of CMOS-compatible terahertz technologies, vital for accelerating the development of 6G communications that would empower societies with real-time terabits per second wireless connectivity for network sensing, holographic communication, cognitive internet of everything, and massive digital cloning of the physical and the biological world.

articleTitle: A 130GHz Two-Stage Common-Base Power Amplifier in 250nm InP
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A two-stage millimeter-wave power amplifier (PA) in 250nm InP HBT technology is presented in this paper. Common-base topology is used for the driver stage and the output stage of the PA. The PA has a small-signal gain of 15.3 dB at 130 GHz and the small-signal 3-dB bandwidth is 16 GHz. The PA achieves 17.4 dBm saturated output power (P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sat</inf>), 17.1 dBm output 1-dB compression point (OP1dB), and 23.2% peak power-added efficiency (PAE) at 130 GHz.

articleTitle: Ultrafast spintronic THz emitters and their optical damage limit
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Optical damage threshold of the ultrafast spintronic THz emitters has been studied. For a given metallic spintronic heterostructure, the THz generation efficiency is related to the wavelength-dependent optical absorption. The mean value of the optical damage limit of most of the above THz emitters is found to be $\sim 60$ GW/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> at 800 nm exaction with 100 fs pulse at 1 kHz repetition rate. Nearly four-fold enhanced optical damage limit is observed for 1550 nm excitation as compared to the 800 nm excitation, though, the THz characteristics remain the same for both.

articleTitle: Ultra-High Mobility and Temperature-Dependent Carrier Dynamics in Narrow-Gap Hg1-x Cdx Te Films
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Mercury cadmium telluride (MCT) is a well-established semiconductor alloy with a widely tunable band gap in the infrared. However, there have been no comprehensive studies on its ultrafast THz photoconductivity dynamics. We report on ultra-high carrier mobilities ($6 \times 10^{\mathbf{5}} \mathrm{cm}^{\mathrm{2}}$/Vs) and long lifetimes in long-wave infrared MCT films as measured by time-resolved terahertz spectroscopy (TRTS). A crossover to negative terahertz photoconductivity at higher frequencies is also observed. Our results suggest that TRTS could find industrial application as a non-contact probe of MCT films for infrared photodetectors and imaging arrays.

articleTitle: W-Band Demonstration of Dynamic, High-Gain Beam Steering with a Scanning Lens Phased Array
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We report the measured results of a sparse, 4x1 scanning lens phased array prototype at W-band that is capable of beam steering a directive (>30 dBi) beam towards ±20° with sidelobe levels around -10 dB. The array elements are high-aperture-efficiency resonant leaky-wave lens antennas with a feed that suppresses the spurious TM0 mode over a wide bandwidth by using a circular waveguide in a ground plane surrounded by annular corrugations. The scanning lens phased array relies on simultaneous electrical and mechanical phase shifting to steer the beams. We use 15 GHz IQ-mixers followed by x6 multipliers to achieve electronic amplitude and phase control at W-band and a piezo-electric motor for mechanical phase shifting, which allows us to scan this array up to 20°. Measurements at 90 GHz of the lens array are in excellent agreement with simulations. More measurement results will be presented at the conference.

articleTitle: Pulse Response of Asymmetric Dual-Grating-Gate HEMT Plasmonic THz Detector
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We investigate the pulse response of an InP-based asymmetric dual-grating-gate high-electron-mobility transistor (A-DGG HEMT) as a plasmonic terahertz detector. We show that a long tail appearing in the output photovoltage waveform is attributed to the electron tunneling from the channel layer to trapping levels in the InAlAs barrier/carrier-supply/spacer layers.

articleTitle: THz spectroscopy techniques for water gradient quantification
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Understanding depth dependent hydration, or gradients, is important for a wide range of applications from paper manufacturing to biological tissue imaging. However, in situ characterization, especially in a non-destructive, reflective measurement is difficult in practice. Moreover, uncontrolled sample drying, water migration, and surface warping create significant challenges towards experimental testing. In this work we show a simple scenario with a standard cleanroom wipe of around $350 \mu \mathrm{m}$ thickness being exposed to water and left for complete drying, while its reflectivity together with changing mass data were recorded. The reflectivity was measured using VNA-based quasioptical system. High dynamic range, frequency domain measurements show a non-trivial frequency dependence on reflectivity that cannot be explained by aqueous dispersion alone. Further, the measurements reveal complicated drying dynamics where broadband reflectionless behavior was observed even when the sample was still $\sim 50$% water by mass. These investigations are an important step towards model model-free based analysis of spectra that should provide direct extraction of water at depth.

articleTitle: Extraordinary Transmission of Bull’s Eye Structure Observed by Up-Conversion-Based THz-Wave Frequency-Domain Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Using optical up-conversion-based THz-wave frequency-domain spectroscopy, we observed the extraordinary transmission of a bull’s eye structure fabricated by a micromachining technique. The fabricated bull’s eye structure, which consisted of a circular aperture of 100-$\mu$m diameter and concentric periodic grooves of 200-$\mu$m periodicity and 20-$\mu$m depth, showed the surface plasmon-enhanced transmission peak at 1.48 THz and the subwavelength-scale confinement of the transmitted THz-wave beam.

articleTitle: Optimizing the Radiation Pattern of a MEMS-Based Reflectarray Using a Genetic Algorithm for Beam Steering Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this work, we consider the criteria for a good radiation pattern and employ a genetic algorithm (GA) to conFigure a MEMS-based reflectarray accordingly. We propose and numerically compare several fitness functions for three different single-objective optimization problems: maximizing the directivity in a specific direction, minimizing the sidelobe level, and steering a null in the direction of an interferer as the main beam stays fixed. As a proof of concept, we carry out a radiation pattern measurement of a static reflectarray. Its measured broadband characteristics as well as its main beam and sidelobes at the design frequency agree with the calculated results based on the proposed mathematical model.

articleTitle: Spatiotemporal Measurement of THz Near-Fields Using Electro-Optic Sampling
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Terahertz generation by optical rectification in LiNbO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> is a promising technique for generating intense THz radiation for particle acceleration and beam manipulation. A better understanding of the THz near-field properties is necessary for the optimization of THz generation efficiency, transport, and coupling. We demonstrate a technique for spatial and temporal characterization of single cycle strong field THz pulses in the near-field of a LiNbO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> source using electro-optic sampling. Using this technique, we have reconstructed the full temporal 3D THz near-field close to the LiNbO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> emission face.

articleTitle: Observation of fundamental mode oscillations in Gyrotron FU CW GVII
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: An experiment in fundamental oscillation mode was conducted using Gyrotron FU CW GVII designed to oscillate in the second harmonic. It was observed that 11 fundamental wave modes oscillated in the frequency range of 115 to 205 GHz. Gaussian beams converted by a mode converter, designed for the co-rotating second harmonic TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">65</inf> mode, were emitted from the gyrotron window. It was demonstrated that this gyrotron can output Gaussian beams in a wide frequency range. A Vlasov launcher converts to a Gaussian beam even for the oscillation of a counter-rotating mode.

articleTitle: Optimization of Si CMOS TeraFETs for 300 GHz band operation
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present an equation for the cutoff frequency accounting for the parasitic fringing capacitances and the gate series resistance. Numerical simulations validate this analytical result. Our analysis shows these gate width dependent parasitics significantly reduce the 20 nm CMOS cutoff frequency for width exceeding 2 mm and even more strongly impact the terahertz (THz) response.

articleTitle: Efficient Waveguide Feeds for Low-Profile Submm-wave Lens Antennas
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A small volume and low-mass THz spectroscopy instrument, integrated in a CubeSat platform, enables an accessible and low-cost pathway to earth science. Low-profile lens antennas emerge as a suitable candidate to realize a high gain, 50 dB, over a wide bandwidth, from 450 GHz to 550 GHz. To achieve a high aperture efficiency with a large numerical aperture lens, an advanced waveguide feed is required. In this work a concentric corrugated waveguide feed and multi-layer leaky-wave feed are presented and benchmarked against an open-ended circular waveguide feed. All three feeds are fabricated and will be evaluated in combination with a 7.4 cm diameter silicon lens. It is shown that the two feeds result in a 65% aperture efficiency, i.e. a 13% improvement with respect to the open-ended waveguide.

articleTitle: 125 GHz wireless transmission of 10 GBaud/s Nyquist-QPSK signal using p-i-n broadband transmitter and FMB envelope detector
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This study experimentally demonstrated a simple, low-cost terahertz wireless communication network that is fully compatible with radio-over-fiber technology. In this experiment, quadrature phase-shift keying (QPSK) modulation, 8-quadrature amplitude modulation(8-QAM), and 16-QAM formats are utilized to send orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) signals over 30 – 150 cm wireless link distances. Here, a broadband p-i-n photodiode upconverts the signals to 125 GHz frequency on the transmitter side, and a fermi-level managed barrier (FMB) diode down-converts the received sub-THz waves on the receiver side. The results indicate that 20 Gbps data rate under 7% FEC limit condition can be successfully transmitted over a 30 cm wireless link distance.

articleTitle: A novel algorithm for refractive index determination using photomixing terahertz continuous-wave spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The pronounced efficiency in terahertz generation and detection and rapid frequency tunning ability make continuous wave (THz-CW) spectroscopy based on photomixing be preferred by industry application. However, its spectral utilization on solid products is hampered by complex and time-consuming data processing methods such as cosine fitting and Hilbert transformation. This study proposed a method that can extract the refractive index of solid samples from THz-CW data rapidly and accurately. The refractive index determination is based on the acquisition of the phase difference between the sample signal and the reference signal. Our method starts with locating the extreme points of the reference signal as the zero-phase points. The phase delay of the sample signal at determined zero-phase points is then calculated as the arccosine function of the ratio between the actual photocurrent and the estimated extreme value. The estimated extreme values are obtained by interpolating the neighboring measured extreme of the original signal. The phase difference extracted by this method has a 2$\pi$ wrapping issue. Therefore, a highly robust unwrapping algorithm is designed based on global linearity evaluation. Five PTFE samples with different thicknesses were measured for exemplification. The effectiveness and robustness of our method are verified by the reproducibility of refractive index determination results from different samples and different experiment configurations.

articleTitle: Extraction of Spectral Information From Terahertz Reflectometry Data
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Despite the significance of the terahertz band spectroscopy and its technological potential, the practical applications are mostly limited to the transmission measurement due to the intrinsic difficulties of the reflection measurement caused by the interference of the multiple reflections and the complex beam path geometry. In this study, a simple pre-process of the time-domain signals has been exploited to extract spectral information from terahertz reflectometry measurements leading to a significant reduction of the reflection fringes. The baseline concept of this approach is isolating the second reflection from the top surface conditions by removing the influence of the first reflection from the reference and the sample signals.

articleTitle: Control and Optimization of Patch-Antenna-Coupled THz Detector Performance using Superstrate Dielectric and Silicon Lens
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present the study on performance optimization and resonant frequency modification of terahertz detectors with the use of hyper-hemispherical silicon superstrate lenses. A series of detectors from 580 GHz to 2 THz which employ a monolithically integrated patch-antenna-coupled field-effect-transistor were fabricated in a commercial 65nm CMOS process of TSMC (Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company). We demonstrate that the resonance frequency with state-of-the-art optical performance can be efficiently controlled by the selection of a superstrate layer in the frequency range which exceeds 100 GHz. This technique can be employed for post-fabrication tailoring of detector resonance frequencies to target spectral lines.

articleTitle: Broadband Terahertz Wavefront Engineering Based on Topology Optimization of Refractive Index in Non-Dielectric Structures
