The interaction circuit consist of three stages: prebunched stage, linear stage and curved nonlinear stage. 3DPIC code are employed to analysis the performance of the circuit. The tube could generate a saturated power of 350 kW at 20.6 GHz, corresponding to a saturated gain of 58.45 dB and a maximum efficiency of 31.5 %.

articleTitle: Multipolar Terahertz Antennas
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Continuous-wave photonics-based THz sources present limited output power due to the restricted input optical power accepted by photomixers. Here, we investigate multipolar antenna design to increase the available THz output power by increasing the number of photomixers. Simulations of 4 to 8 dipole arms antennas are conducted, showing an improvement of antenna gain in comparison to standard dipole antennas, additionally to a potential increase of the THz power for photomixing applications.

articleTitle: 3D Printed Terahertz Antiresonant Fibers for Controllable Guiding Properties
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We study, fabricate and characterize the properties of hollow antiresonant (AR) terahertz waveguides ideal for terahertz transmission. We model and measure transmission loss as the antiresonant tube thickness is varied from 0.45 to 0.55 mm with constant fiber dimensions. The experimental results confirm that the 3D printed AR waveguide can guide terahertz wave with low loss and illustrate spectral features near the resonant frequencies. The aim of this work is to develop a low-loss, low cost and simple terahertz waveguides with transmission behavior adjusted by a single parameters, the cladding tube thickness.

articleTitle: Broadband THz Absorber Layers for Microbolometer Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The potential for wide-range THz imaging applications can be significantly enhanced with the implementation of cost-effective IR microbolometer technologies. For real-time broadband THz imaging purposes, thin films based on a titanium alloy, TiAlV, is investigated as the potential THz absorber layer in a microbolometer structure. Fabricated TiAlV thin films are evaluated in terms of their thickness, sheet resistance, and THz absorbance to assess their use in the microfabrication of a single pixel detector. Owing to its much lower conductivity compared to other metals and compatibility to microfabrication methods, by tailoring the sheet resistance with control in layer thickness, significant enhancement in THz absorbance is observed over a wide frequency range.

articleTitle: Designing coupled metal slot antennas for detecting micron-sized 2D material in terahertz regime
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The metallic meta-surface which enables measurements of micron-sized two-dimensional (2D) materials with millimeter-wavelength terahertz wave is introduced to overcome diffraction limit. We induce strong light (terahertz wave)-matter (15-$\mu$ m-sized graphite) interaction by using a slot antenna making electric-field confinement and enhancement of electromagnetic waves. When micron-sized graphite partially covers the slot antenna, the resonance transmissions are significantly reduced. This result implies that strong coupling between terahertz wave and metallic graphite is accomplished through the slot antennas, which can be expanded toward various 2D materials in the regime of millimeter-wavelength.

articleTitle: Resonant thermal terahertz metasurface-based emitters on n-GaAs/GaAs
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Thermal metamaterial GaAs-based emitters operating in THz range were developed and investigated. Structures of desired parameters were simulated using 3D finite difference time domain method, and produced with a square geometry metasurface on the top structured by UV laser lithography. Depending on the metacell geometrical parameters the emission spectra of the heated samples (up to $400^{\circ}\mathrm{C})$ revealed resonant emission features in the range from 0.7 THz to 1.2 THz and the bandwidth of 0.29 THz. The demonstrated principle of using n-GaAs instead of metal bottom layer and unintentionally doped GaAs as dielectric spacer paves the way for thermal emitters compatible with III-V semiconductor system-based THz optoelectronics technology.

articleTitle: Temperature-dependent low-frequency vibrational spectra of sodium magnesium chlorophyllin
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Terahertz time-domain spectroscopy has been used to investigate the vibrational spectra of polycrystalline sodium magnesium chlorophyllin - one of the natural derivatives of chlorophyll - over the temperature range 88 K–298 K. A number of well-resolved absorption peaks were observed in the frequency range 0.2–2.5 THz, which are interpreted as originating from mixed character of intramolecular and intermolecular vibration modes. As the temperature is increased, the observed absorption features resolve into broader peaks. The peak centered at 1.83 THz shifts towards higher frequencies, indicating that for this feature, significant intermolecular anharmonicity exist.

articleTitle: Laser-Induced Periodic Surface Structures on Ge2Sb2Te5 Irradiated by Terahertz Free-Electron Laser Vortex Beam
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Laser-induced ablation of Ge2Sb2Te2 using terahertz vortex beam was investigated. Intense terahertz pulses from a free-electron laser were made to pass through a Tsurupica spiral phase plate to generate the vortex beam. Laser-induced periodic surface structures (LIPSS) were formed with a period quarter of the wavelength and an orientation parallel to the beam polarization. Due to the singularity of the vortex beam, LIPSS formation was not observed at the center of the irradiated spot.

articleTitle: Design of Periodic Dielectric Loaded Circuit Based on AlN-SiC for the W band TE02 mode Gyro-TWT
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A study of a periodic dielectric loaded circuit based on AlN-SiC for a W band TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">02</inf> mode gyro-TWT has been presented. The designed interaction circuit consists of AlN-SiC dielectric rings and copper rings. By applying this, the suppressions of the oscillation modes for the W-band TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">02</inf> mode gyro-TWT has been achieved. The simulation results indicate that the output power is above 140kW with the bandwidth of 8GHz, the gain is above 35dB. In additional, the component will be applied in a sample tube of the W band TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">02</inf> mode gyro-TWT.

articleTitle: Towards Terahertz Wireless Authentication with Unique Aperture Fingerprints using Leaky-Wave Antennas
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We introduce a fundamentally new approach to wireless authentication and fingerprinting based on the unique spectral footprints induced by the geometry of the leakage aperture in the leaky THz waveguides transmitters.

articleTitle: Optical Single-Shot Object Recognition in the Terahertz Spectral Domain
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Imaging in the terahertz spectral region is costly and complex. Machine learning yields tools that allow the recognition of objects more efficiently than plain imaging. We present a single-shot optical machine learning approach for detecting objects in the terahertz spectral region by using a single pixel detector paired with a terahertz spatial light modulator.

articleTitle: Antiferromagnetic Resonance Spectroscopy of NiO in the Terahertz Region
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Nickel oxide (NiO) is widely known as a typical easy-plane-type antiferromagnet with a Néel temperature of T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N</inf>=525 K. Despite its simple cubic structure, the magnetic structure has not been fully understood yet. Indeed, antiferromagnetic resonance (AFMR) modes observed so far are not consistent with the standard two-sublattice model. In this study, a frequency-domain terahertz (THz) spectroscopy technique using continuously tunable photomixers was applied to a single-crystalline NiO, and magnetic field dependence of the AFMR mode at 1 THz was obtained for three different field orientations for the first time.

articleTitle: Simulation of Selective Excitation of Dark Plasmon Modes in Single Metal Rods by Focused Terahertz Radial Beams
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Numerical simulations in the terahertz region are made to study the near-field enhancement associated with plasmon resonances of a gold single rod illuminated by linearly and radially polarized light. We demonstrate that bright and dark modes are selectively excited dependent on the vector beam mode and rod orientation relative to the incident light. These findings show that terahertz cylindrical vector beams have potential applications for selective excitation in plasmonic micro structures.

articleTitle: Alignment of Terahertz Transmission Setups with Free-Space Laser Photoconductive Switches
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A systematic procedure for ensuring perfect alignment of Photoconductive Antennas (PCA) in transmittance measure setups with free-space laser PCA gap feeding and mechanical adjust of silicon substrate lenses is presented. The method is especially suited to research studies for characterization of PCA geometries. An example of measured spatio-temporal beam pattern is shown.

articleTitle: A Leaky Enhanced Photo-Conductive Connected Array for Broadband Generation of THz Power
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Photoconductive antennas are devices that provide power up to THz frequencies at a relatively low cost. However, the power radiated by each antenna is typically quite low and arrays have been proposed to increase it. In this paper we present the design of a leaky enhanced array architecture that surpasses the state of the art as it operates efficiently for frequencies up to 1THz, without excessive complications in the manufacturing. This architecture is compared with a ‘standard’ array, showing a broader bandwidth and a higher emitted detected signal.

articleTitle: A Terahertz Continuous Phase Shifter Based on Varactor Diodes
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Terahertz phase shifter is a key research direction of terahertz technology, which still suffers from the problems of small phase shift range and large insertion loss. We propose a terahertz continuous phase shifter based on a 3dB directional coupler and the varactor diodes, which can achieve continuous phase shift up to 175.5° with an insertion loss of less than 6dB by controlling the capacitance.

articleTitle: A compact and continuously operating CO₂ pumped HCOOH dual laser
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A compact terahertz continuous wave (CW) CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> pumped formic acid (HCOOH) dual laser has been developed for higher time resolution and long continuous operation, with active power and intermediate frequency (IF) control. The output power of more than 20 mW on 0.69 THz line is obtained by using a 1.5 m long dual-waveguide with an inner diameter of 38 mm. The air supply system of the laser is designed for continuous air intake, so that the laser system can operate continuously and stably for at least 24 hours. Two high precision ($1~{\mu }\mathrm{m}$) moving frames are used to control the output power and IF of the dual laser. The whole dual laser system has been successfully operated, with output power exceeding 20 mW and IF stable at around 1 MHz in more than 24 hours.

articleTitle: Directivity Measurement Method for Metasurface Antennas by an Alternative to Terahertz Compact Oscillators
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Metasurface antennas with high directivity are essential in compact terahertz oscillators for 6G wireless communications. However, compact terahertz oscillators have yet to be commercialized and cannot be accessed when they are required to measure the directivity of metasurface antennas. Here, we show a directivity measurement method for metasurface antennas by an alternative to terahertz compact oscillators employing a commonly-available frequency-multiplied source and an iris diaphragm. Measurements show that the metasurface antenna integrated with an iris diaphragm enhances the directivity of a single iris diaphragm 2.5 times. The proposed directivity measurement method by an alternative to terahertz compact oscillators would be a welcome contribution to developing terahertz components for the standardization of 6G wireless communications.

articleTitle: A Novel Terahertz Integrated Sensor Based on Metamaterial and Embedded Microfluidic Channels
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: THz metamaterial microfluidic sensors, which can be utilized for the detection of liquid specimen, have attracted much attention in biosensing applications. In this paper, a novel microfluidic channel embedded THz metamaterial sensor is proposed and characterized. Unlike the reported THz metamaterial microfluidic sensors, our concept combines the microfluidic channel with substrate, by designing micro-channels in PDMS substrate. It could be easily fabricated by standard photolithography technique. We also compare and contrast the transmission and reflection performance of different SRR metamaterials. The simulation results show that the two-gap SRR pattern with 120° spacing angle exhibits highest sensitivity, FOM and Q-factor.

articleTitle: Point-to-Point Transmission of In-Plane Terahertz Beams between Conducting Plates for Integrated Sensing Platform
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Terahertz waves can be used for sensing with high spatio-temporal resolution along with rich spectral information. However, conventional experimental setups of terahertz sensing based on free-space optics are bulky and not readily integrable to a compact and portable setup. In this study, we propose a method to implement in-plane point-to-point transmission of wide terahertz beams. Specifically, we convert a point excitation into a 2D collimated beam, which is again focused onto a point by using a symmetrically arranged pair of dielectric-free Luneburg lenses defined inside two conducting plates. The hollow space allows a large space for samples to interact with the terahertz beam. Thus, it can reconcile the space limitation of the setup flexibility of sample replacement. We have experimentally characterized the transmittance and confirmed that $\boldsymbol{S} _{21}$ over a length of 195 mm is about -25 dB from 260 GHz to 300 GHz, which is enhanced by approximately 10 dB than without the lenses.

articleTitle: Strong coupling regime between THz metamaterial and Tamm cavity
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: New resonator schemes are high desired to improve coupling strength between THz photons and quantum matter. Here, we report on an original THz system based on a LC metamaterial in strong coupling regime with a THz Tamm cavity. We demonstrate a splitting of the THz resonance in two peaks with quality factors as high as 35, which is promising for THz quantum optics.

articleTitle: A Terahertz Corrugated Horn Array Based on Silicon Platelets
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A terahertz corrugated horn array is widely used in array receiver systems and is suitable to be made by stacked metal sheets. In this paper, we introduce the development of a broadband 2 × 2 terahertz corrugated horn array fabricated by silicon micromachining technology. The horn array is made up of 16 metalized silicon platelets with a total weight of only 4.2 grams. The measured gain of each horn element is around 16 dBi at 240 GHz with a low cross-polarization level, and the bandwidth is greater than 100 GHz with a return loss better than -15 dB.

articleTitle: Integrated, broadband, arbitrary-ratio power division based on air-silicon effective mediums
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: All-silicon substrateless waveguides offer exceptionally low-loss and low-dispersion for integrated terahertz systems. On this platform, we present a scheme for realising broadband arbitrary ratio power division. Effective medium techniques are employed to generate power division with ratios from 50%/50% to 95%/5% across the 220–330 GHz band with average efficiency above 88%.

articleTitle: Near-field analysis of the thermally excited evanescent waves on GaN
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: local phenomena of materials including electron motions and lattice vibrations generate ultra-small thermally excited evanescent waves in the long-wavelength infrared range (8-20 μm). To perform a thorough analysis of the evanescent waves, we have developed passive-type scanning near-field optical spectroscopy (SNOS) without using external illuminations. It enables the passive spectral analysis of the thermally excited evanescent waves with a spatial and wavelength resolution of 200 nm and 150 nm, respectively. Here, we performed a near-field measurement of GaN which has a surface phonon polariton resonance at a wavelength of 14.1 μm. We have experimentally verified a long decay length at 14.1 μm, indicating that it enables detecting unique signals due to the surface phenomena.

articleTitle: Finite Rate of Innovation Theory Applied to Terahertz Signal Processing
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Methods based on finite rate of innovation have been demonstrated to perform better than the relevant standard methods at other frequencies and for other imaging modalities. We apply this theory to terahertz imaging, outlining some of the necessary steps for specializing the method to best suit terahertz signals. To demonstrate the effectiveness of our method we apply it to simulated terahertz signals, comparing the amplitudes and time locations used to create the simulated signal with those extracted through our method from the simulated signal. The close agreement between the amplitudes and time locations of the modelled reflections illustrates the impressive accuracy of results produced from our method.

articleTitle: Dispersion compensated ring lasers for terahertz frequency comb and ultrafast terahertz detection
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We report frequency combs formation in THz QCL ring cavities with spectral bandwidth of $\sim 400$ GHz. In addition to the frequency comb operation sech<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>-shaped spectra are observed in RF-injected ring lasers and dispersion compensated double ring cavities, hinting at the existence of soliton regimes in the QCL. The device is also used below threshold to detect commercial THz frequency combs. High harmonics of the comb beatnote could be measured optically up to 67 GHz (670<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> harmonic).

articleTitle: Three-dimensional printed achromatic λ/4 waveplate for the terahertz frequency range
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A design of a three-dimensional printed achromatic $\lambda$/4 waveplate based on form-birefringence targeting the lower terahertz (THz) frequency range is proposed. For the waveplate a stratified structure is employed which gives rise to form-birefringence. Furthermore, experimental results in the frequency range from 75 GHz to 110 GHz show that the proposed waveplate causes a $\pi$/2 phase shift of incident linearly polarized light with a deviation from optimal behaviour not exceeding 5% for the entire range.

articleTitle: Terahertz Microfluidics for attomole- and picoliter-level sensing
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present a compact terahertz (THz) microfluidic chip based on a nonlinear optical crystal with a small number of meta-atoms for accelerating the research on THz microfluidics. The chip operates based on near-field interactions among a solution sample that flows in a microchannel, meta-atoms, and a highly dense point THz source that occurs in the process of optical rectification at the irradiation spots of femtosecond pulse laser beam. To date, we have achieved attomole-level sensing using a picoliter-order volume of various solutions in a sub-wavelength effective sensing area. Details of the chip, sensing examples, and future THz microfluidics are discussed.

articleTitle: Low frequency THz spectrum of 4-hexylbenzoic acid measured at room temperature
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The terahertz spectrum of 4-hexylbenzoic acid is reported for the first time in the low frequency range. The FTIR measurements revealed that this material is characterized by 7 absorption peaks in the considered frequency range at room temperature. A good correspondence was obtained between the experiment and the theoretical model. This work increases the scope of using FTIR technique in determining the low frequency THz spectra of materials.

articleTitle: Coherent detection of broadband terahertz pulses using liquid water
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Here, we report a terahertz (THz) coherent detection scheme based on liquid water. The sensitivity is 1 order of magnitude higher than that of the air-based method under comparable detection conditions. The scheme is quite sensitive to the energy and polarizations of the control second harmonic (CSH) and THz field strength, which brings a direct route for optimization and sensitivity enhancement of THz detection.

articleTitle: Wideband guided-mode resonance filters with low-loss material
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We report an all-dielectric single-layer guided-mode resonance filter (GMRF) operating in the wideband terahertz (THz) region. To obtain strong resonance in this region, a dielectric material must have a low refractive index and low absorption at wideband THz frequencies, and a high tensile strength (TS) is needed. Cyclic olefin copolymer (COC) films have a lower refractive index and lower absorption than polyethylene terephthalate (PET) films and a higher TS than polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) films. Thus, COC is a suitable dielectric material for wideband THz designs. The reported GMRF operates in the range of 0.576-2.759 THz, which agrees well with rigorous coupled-wave analysis (RCWA) simulation results.

articleTitle: Electric Potential Mapping of All-Solid-State Lithium Ion Batteries using A Terahertz Chemical Microscope
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A terahertz (THz) chemical microscope has been developed to measure the electric potential distribution of liquid phase lithium ion batteries (LIBs) during charging and discharging. A LIB was fabricated on a sensing plate, which consists of SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and Si films on a sapphire substrate, to generate THz pulses by a laser irradiation. Since the amplitude of THz is proportional to the electric potential on the sensing plate, the electric potential distribution of the lithium ion battery on the sensing plate could be visualized. In this study, the electric potential distribution across a conventional all-solid-state LIB was measured by immobilizing the LIB on the sensing plate using epoxy resin. The distribution of the electric potentials of the battery was clearly visualized by the TCM. This result indicates that the TCM could be one of useful tools for the development high performance batteries.

articleTitle: Ultra-Compact and Low-Power Planetary Instruments at Terahertz Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In recent years, space agencies across the globe have been actively looking into ultra-compact instruments to fly on small satellite platforms to have multiple flight missions with innovative way of getting science data. The idea is to use CubeSats – which are shoe-box size satellites – and SmallSats as useable platforms to supplement main missions as well as using them for standalone scientific missions. The size of the CubeSats are referred in the unit of `U’, where one `U’ is a cube with 10 cm x 10 cm x 10 cm. A small 6U CubeSat will have approximately 2U space available for low-power, low-mass, yet highly capable scientific payload (the rest of the space is used for solar cells for power generation, star tracker for guidance, attitude control, and other electronics). These CubeSat/SmallSats based flights enable advancing proof of concept instruments to higher technology readiness level (TRL) by flying them in relevant environment and allow to have multiple targeted flights with scientific data returns.Developing ultra-compact scientific payloads for these novel platforms poses a host of challenges. First, the instrument needs to be highly compact due to the lack of available space. Second, it has to be ultra-low power due to the severe restrictions on DC power availability. And finally, one has to be innovative in the design of antennas as traditional high gain reflector antennas (for scientific payload as well as for data communication) are not practical. Design and development of large aperture deployable antennas and other innovative structures are gaining a lot of attention in this regard.We have been developing high resolution spectrometers, radiometers, and radars at millimeter-wave and terahertz frequencies on CubeSat and SmallSat platforms for astrophysics, planetary science, and Earth science applications. We are also developing millimeter-wave communications systems on CubeSat platform to provide communication link during entry-descent-landing (EDL) phase of Mars and other planetary missions. In this presentation, we will present an overview of the state of the instrumentation development for CubeSat platforms and the design and implementation challenges. Innovative packaging solutions, novel antenna technology, and low-power backend solutions will also be presented. We will show that CubeSats and SmallSats will play a key role in future scientific missions to space and also they will find increasing applications in commercial communication and other endeavors.The research described herein was carried out at the Jet Propulsion Laboratory, California Institute of Technology, Pasadena, California, USA, under contract with National Aeronautics and Space Administration.

articleTitle: MIMO Antennas for Radiative Near-Field Links: A Comparative Study at 300 GHz
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This paper presents a comparative study of different Multiple Input Multiple Output (MIMO) array architectures to realize high-capacity Point-to-Point (PtP) wireless links for potential use in future 6G backhauling applications. This study focuses on the 220-320 GHz band, defined by the new IEEE 802.15.3d standard. Both phased array and focal plane array architectures are studied, considering the link to operate in the radiative near-field. The theoretically achievable capacities are presented based on the channel matrix estimated in the radiative near-field and the application of Shannon’s capacity formula. It is found that capacities well above Tbps rates can theoretically be realized, even without the use of interference cancellation techniques.

articleTitle: Highly efficient THz transient four-wave mixing in doped semiconductors
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present a quantitative study of the efficiency of degenerate THz transient four-wave mixing in germanium doped by shallow impurities using the Dutch free electron laser FELIX. We derive the third order nonlinear sheet susceptibility and find values at low temperature that exceed those of any other material and wavelength range reported to date.

articleTitle: Terahertz four-wire waveguides for broadband signal processing and multiplexing
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this work, we introduce a versatile metal-wire waveguide geometry, namely a four-wire waveguide, which is capable of sustaining two independent and orthogonally polarized fundamental modes, thus acting as a broadband polarization-division multiplexer. By integrating multiscale-structured grooves into the wires of such a waveguide, we demonstrate the independent manipulation of polarization-division terahertz signals.

articleTitle: Temperature-Dependent Dielectric Properties of Human Bone Constituents at THz Frequencies: Contrast Mechanisms and Bound Water Dynamics
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: THz time domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS) was used to investigate the dielectric properties of constituents of human bone. We report experimental values for refractive index and absorption coefficient for four major anhydrous constituents of bone: Collagen, Hydroxyapatite, Calcite and Amorphous calcium phosphate. We varied the sample temperature in order to explore the physical mechanisms underpinning the THz dielectric function of these constituents. Experimental data were well described using the Debye model for collagen, or the Lorentz model for mineral compounds, respectively. A fitting procedure based on Particle Swarm Optimization was implemented in order to extract the fitting parameters such as relaxation times and oscillator strengths.

articleTitle: Recent Development of a 105/140GHz MW-level Gyrotron at IAE
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A 105/140 GHz MW-level gyrotron has been developed aiming for fusion application at IAE from 2020. The gyrotron employed a triode MIG, a cylindrical cavity working under a TE18, 7 mode for 105GHz and a TE24, 9 mode for 140GHz. A built-in quasi-optical mode converter, a single-stage depressed collector and a boron nitride single-disk window were adopted. In the recent test of this year, the dual-frequency gyrotron achieved test results of 520 kW at 105 GHz and 320 kW at 140 GHz under 1-Hz 10-ms continuous pulse-burst operations, and 300 kW/600ms, 450 kW/250ms at 105 GHz.

articleTitle: Terahertz spectroscopic evidence of correlation driven optical transparency in CaVO3
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Transparent conducting materials are emerging materials due to their immense application in optoelectronic and photovoltaic industries. So, finding various methods to achieve the elusive togetherness of conductivity and transparency is also increasing. Transparent conducting transition metal oxides unfold a new class of materials used as transparent conductors. So, we have done low energy carrier dynamic of transparent conducting CaVO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> thin film using terahertz (THz) time-domain and time-resolved spectroscopy. THz optical conductivity reveals the system is in the borderline of metal to insulator transition, and ultrafast optical relaxation is through electron-phonon thermalization. Overall, extracted parameter suggests that CaVO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> can be a suitable alternative to existing transparent conductors.

articleTitle: A Switchable Terahertz Wave Modulator Based on VO2
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a dynamic THz modulator combining metamaterial with vanadium dioxide (VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>). The phase transformation characteristics of VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> enable the device to realize the reconstruction of transmission and reflection spatial morphology in two frequency bands, and both have a high polarization conversion efficiency of orthogonal polarization. At the same time, both the phase gradient distribution of transmission and reflection state include 360° by changing the structural parameters of the top structure. Based on this unit structure, we design a switchable THz beam modulator based on VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, which can achieve 54° deflection of the reflective beam at 140GHz when VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> is in a metallic state and 32° refraction of the transmitted beam at 220GHz when VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> is in the dielectric state.

articleTitle: Detection of strong light-matter interaction and near-field mapping on a single resonator with a thermal transducer
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A thin layer of a mid-IR transparent polymer is inserted inside a metallic nano-resonator, where a photonic mode and an intersubband transition are strongly coupled. Acting as a non-perturbative transducer, and without essentially modifying the optical response, the polymer allows the detection of absorbed optical power in the form of thermal expansion due to heat dissipation. This innovative approach permits to identify - at the nano-resonator level - the typical anti crossing characteristic of the polaritonic system, and to perform direct imaging of the electromagnetic fields buried within the optical cavity.

articleTitle: Investigating phonon dynamics across the magnetic transition in multiferroic YCrO₃
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We investigated phonon dynamics of multiferroic YCrO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> using infrared (IR) spectroscopy, supported by first-principles simulations across the antiferromagnetic (AFM) transition temperature ($T _{N}$) ~ 138 K. Magnetic field and temperature-dependent measurements of phonon energies ($\omega$) and linewidth ($\Gamma$) across $T _{{N}}$ allow us to narrow down the anomalous T dependence due to magnetoelastic coupling and exclude magnon-phonon coupling and magnetostriction effects as governing mechanisms.

articleTitle: Linear cross-polarization conversion in a planar near-field coupled terahertz metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this article, we have demonstrated broadband terahertz cross-polarization conversion in a planar coupled metamaterial structure through simulation and experiments. The proposed metamaterial geometry contains a cut resonator and four split-ring resonators (SRRs) as a unit cell. The proposed metamaterial design is capable of showing maximum cross-polarization conversion of up to 39%. Broadband polarization conversion occurs in our metamaterial configuration due to the significant near-field coupling between the different resonant modes of the resonators. Our study could be used to construct broadband terahertz photonic devices.

articleTitle: Planarized tapered waveguides for high-temperature THz quantum cascade laser frequency combs
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present a novel planarized double metal waveguide platform for high-performance THz quantum cascade laser frequency combs. The waveguides are embedded in a low-loss polymer (BCB) and have an extended top metallization, resulting in lower waveguide losses and improved RF and thermal properties. A further performance improvement is observed for waveguides with a tapered profile due to nonlinearity-enhancing effects. These free-running devices produce strong single RF beatnotes up to almost −30 dBm at 90 K, nearly three orders of magnitude stronger than for ridge devices. The improved comb performance is maintained for higher operating temperatures, with a 200 GHz comb bandwidth and a single RF beatnote above −60 dBm at a heat sink temperature of 115 K.

articleTitle: Development of a corrugated horn at 2-THz band for a hot electron bolometer mixer
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We are developing a waveguide-type hot electron bolometer mixer (HEBM) at 2-THz band for high-speed wireless communications (Beyond 5G) or atmospheric/astronomical observations. We are developing an HEBM with a diagonal horn and are also developing an HEBM with a corrugated horn at 2- THz band to improve the beam pattern performance. A corrugated horn has a good axisymmetric beam and polarization characteristics over wide band, although machining of a small corrugation structure is difficult. The width of the teeth was designed to be 15 μm凹/20 μm凸 with a depth of 37.5 μm. The corrugated horn consists of a 120 number of the teeth, 20 number of tapered teeth with a deepest depth of 75 μm, and a circular to rectangular transition. The total length of the horn is 6.1 mm. A simulation result of the horn shows low reflection loss and low-side lobe level. We have fabricated a sample horn and confirmed the teeth structure were well machined by measuring with a nondestructive inspection using X-ray. The size of the teeth was measured using X-ray and a laser microscope.

articleTitle: High Gradient mm-Wave Accelerating Structure Design
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We report on the design of a multi-cell mm-wave accelerator structure operating near 100 GHz. This frequency regime enables not only a high gradient due to higher breakdown thresholds, but also reduced fill times which decreases pulsed heating and allows for higher repetition rates. These advantages make mm-wave accelerators an attractive solution to applications requiring high gradients or ultra-compact structures. The cavity geometry and distributed RF coupling network for the reported linac design have been optimized using ANSYS-HFSS and SLAC's parallel electromagnetic code suite ACE3P, with simulated accelerating gradients reaching 169 MeV/m with 100 kW per cell.

articleTitle: Experimental Study of Electron Impact Ionization between a Relativistic Electron Bunch and a ZnTe Crystal
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We utilized electro-optic (EO) sampling to measure the electric field induced by a 35-MeV picosecond electron bunch propagating inside a ZnTe crystal. We injected electron bunches into the crystal and probed the irradiation effect. We found that the electron bunch positively charges up the crystal via impact ionizations through the collision between the fast electrons and bounded electrons inside the crystal, and the ionization saturates during 10 ps.

articleTitle: Fast and sensitive THz detector based on optomechanical resonator
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We demonstrate an optomechanical THz meta-atom device consisting of a THz resonator and an oscillating mechanical nanobeam. This device efficiently interacts with THz radiation and shows mechanical responses in oscillation amplitudes with a responsivity of 4 nm/$\mu$W, and thus can be employed as sensitive THz detectors operating at room temperature. We further implement phase lock loop (PLL) measurements and show that the device can respond at high speeds, with a harmonic bandwidth on the order of 1 MHz. Moreover, in this optomechanical system, Duffing nonlinearities can be easily observed.

articleTitle: Efficient THz Time-Stamping of Ultrafast Electron Probes
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We demonstrate a preliminary measurement of THz streaking of ultrafast electron bunches generated from an rf photoeinjector using an efficient THz deflector structure. We show that the structure can achieve upward of 1.5 MV/cm of peak deflecting THz fields subsequently improving the timing resolution of ultrafast electron diffraction measurements.

articleTitle: A study of phased-array effect in THz radiation pattern from the semiconductor surface
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The primary cause of the THz radiation from semiconductors is the optically created oscillating dipoles and their orientations. Therefore, the optical excitation angles of the incident femtosecond laser and THz detection vary due to the radiation patterns of dipoles considering Snell’s law and the phased-array effect. We investigated this phased-array effect using finite-difference time-domain simulations for angular dependence at focus and non-focus conditions of the laser beam spot. The angular dependence simulation results at focus conditions show a point-source dipole radiation pattern and a pronounced directivity for high frequencies at non-focus conditions. This study provides a better understanding of the THz radiation pattern from semiconductors.

articleTitle: Extraction of device parameters of a metal-insulator-semiconductor by terahertz emission spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this study, we focus on the terahertz radiation from a Si metal–oxide–semiconductor (MOS) structure and formulate the mechanism of THz radiation to semi-quantitatively evaluate the MOS devices. A simplified model, which can effectively explain the dependence of THz emission amplitudes on external bias voltages for both n- and p-type Si MOS structures, is derived from Poisson’s equation with considering external effects, including the flat-band voltage, hot carrier diffusion, and quick recombination through interface states due to photocarrier field acceleration. The results reveal the possibility on estimating the surface parameters, such as surface potential and dielectric layer.

articleTitle: Enhanced selectivity based on molecular imprinting for aqueous glucose detection with terahertz waves
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We report a strategy towards highly selective and sensitive terahertz detection of aqueous glucose via molecular imprinting polymers synthesized on Au nanoparticles. In this process, Au nanoparticles are encapsulated by MIPs with glucose-specific “cavities”. These “cavities” can selectively adsorb a large amount of glucose molecules, through which, both sensitivity and selectivity can be enhanced compared to the traditional terahertz spectroscopy.

articleTitle: Employing M1 direct calibration/de-embedding approaches for large signal model validation at mm-wave frequencies
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this contribution, we employ direct calibration/de-embedding approaches to validate the large signal device model of state-of-the-art HBTs and CMOS technologies operating in the mm-wave frequency band WR6. The capability of placing the first tier calibration reference plane in close proximity to the DUT allows the large signal metric to be directly compared with foundry models.

articleTitle: System-on-Chip approach millimeter-wave imaging development for fusion plasma diagnostics
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Millimeter-wave “System-on-Chip” technology has been employed in chip heterodyne diagnostics systems for fusion plasma measurements, including radiometers, reflectometers, interferometers, etc. The SoC technology has brought a dramatic advance in microwave imaging instruments. We are currently developing wide bandgap GaN chips, which support long-term fusion plasma parameter measurements in radiation harsh environments.

articleTitle: Crystal Quality Evaluation of N-(4-methoxybenzylidene) aniline by Terahertz Laser Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Terahertz (THz) laser spectroscopy with high frequency resolution was applied for crystal quality evaluation. N-(4-methoxybenzylidene) aniline crystals with different quality was prepared by recrystallization with melting method with different crystal growth parameter such as cooling rate. The validity of the crystal quality evaluation by THz spectroscopy was confirmed by comparing peak intensity, peak frequency and FWHM of the THz spectra and XRD patterns for the same sample.

articleTitle: Beam Pattern characterization of Sierpinski Fractal Photoconductive Antennas
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Far field results for the beam pattern of fractal photoconductive antennas (PCAs) based on the Sierpinski triangle, measured through a collimated aperture raster scan technique with fixed transmit and receive free-space laser-fed PCAs are presented. The fractal behavior has been compared to simulations, with excellent agreement.

articleTitle: Metrological-grade terahertz frequency combs
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Metrological-grade frequency comb (FC) synthesizers are the ideal sources for quantum applications. At terahertz (THz) frequencies, electrically pumped quantum cascade lasers (QCLs) have shown quantum-limited frequency noise operation, phase/frequency absolute referencing and self-starting FC operation, albeit over a rather restricted dynamic range. Here, we conceive a technological approach to achieve FC operation over the entire available gain bandwidth and across almost the whole lasing regime at THz frequencies, by increasing the mirror losses of its Fabry-Perot cavity through coating the back facet with an epitaxially-grown multilayer graphene film.

articleTitle: Uncovering Protein Structural Dynamics with Terahertz Light
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The long-range structural vibrations of biomacromolecules (molecular weight $\gt 5$ kDa), are matched to biological thermal energies. This intriguing overlap raises the question if, like sequence and structure, these dynamics are also evolutionarily optimized for robust and efficient biochemistry. The vibrations for such massive systems are necessarily complex. The structural vibrations involve displacements of entire subdomains, are numerous and closely spaced in energy, leading to dense spectra. The spectra are further complicated by the energy overlap with collective excitations of the biological water necessary for in vivo structure and biological relevance. Compounded with these effects, while a single spectrum corresponds to a single structure, biomacromolecular structure thermally samples small configurational changes in time, leading to variation in the vibrational spectra. These effects all lead to the smooth featureless spectra seen by investigators for macroscopic samples. In this talk I will provide an overview of terahertz biomolecular studies and discuss the fundamental issue of isolating vibrational excitations based on specific structural displacements. An example of a technique to provides this isolation is anisotropic terahertz microspectroscopy (ATM). Using ATM we have found that indeed there are biases in the directionality of vibrational displacements which change with ligand binding and photoexcitation. In particular photoexcitation measurements of orange carotenoid protein (OCP) demonstrate that intermediate states of the photo cycle coincide with changes in the directionality of vibrations, suggesting these reorganizations of the dynamics may assist with access to intermediate state structures. Finally, I will discuss the challenges of current instrumentation, computational tools and sample preparation that need to be addressed to more fully realize the potential of THz in the understanding of the role of picosecond structural dynamics in biology.

articleTitle: Discovery of Coulomb-Drag Instability of Graphene Dirac Plasmons
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Quasi-ballistic electrons injected from the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{n}^{+}$</tex> region into the gated n-region of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{n}^{+}\text{-}\mathrm{i}\text{-}\mathrm{n}\text{-}\mathrm{n}^{+}$</tex> graphene FET (GFET) strongly drag the quasi-equilibrium electrons in the n-region. We found that this Coulomb drag can substantially influence the current-voltage characteristics leading to instability of graphene Dirac plasmons and resulting in coherent oscillations/ amplification in the terahertz range.

articleTitle: Development of a cryogenic far-infrared post-dispersed polarising Fourier transform spectrometer
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The sensitivity of state-of-the-art superconducting far-infrared (FIR) detectors is such that wideband spectroscopic observations will require techniques to reduce the spectral bandwidth of a detector to limit the photon noise from an astronomical source. The leading instrument concept features grating spectrometers to post-disperse the light that has been modulated by a polarising Fourier transform spectrometer (FTS) onto a detector array, thereby reducing the photon noise on each detector. While the principles of this method are understood, to date an integrated system has not been realized in the laboratory. We present the development of a fully cryogenic post-dispersed polarising FTS (PDPFTS). To assess the data processing challenges posed by this hybrid spectrometer realistic astronomical spectra are generated by combining line emission from a tunable THz photomixer source with continuum emission from a variable blackbody source.

articleTitle: Mid-Infrared Saturable Absorbers with Ultra-Low Saturation Intensities
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We report on an ultra-low threshold saturable absorber operating in the mid-infrared spectral region (λ ~ 9 μm). The device relies on intersubband transitions in semiconductor quantum wells embedded in metallic microcavities. It operates in the strong light-matter coupling regime. The absorption change stems from the collapse of the polaritons resonances upon bleaching of the transition. We have developed an analytical formalism based on temporal coupled mode theory to model the device non-linear behavior. Using a commercial TEC-cooled quantum cascade laser as source, we demonstrate saturation with a peak pumping power of 150 mW (corresponding to an intensity on the sample of 10 kW.cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup>).

articleTitle: Rotating Quadrupole Undulators Formed By Magnetized Helices
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: To create a rotating quadrupole field a system of two magnetized helices is proposed. The simplest shape of undulator trajectories in such a field is provided when electrons are injected into a quasi-homogeneous region of the azimuthal component. Such systems can be used to implement high-power FEL-like sources of coherent radiation from short electron bunches.

articleTitle: Shielding Effectiveness Measurement of Small Enclosures with Multiple Probes
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The SE of small enclosures depends on the receive probe position inside of enclosure. It is not easy to move the receive antenna throughout the small enclosure to obtain the largest field. This paper describes how to overcome it using the SE measurement system with multiple electro-optical probes.

articleTitle: THz emission spectroscopy of interlayer phonons in MoSe2
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Terahertz (THz) time-domain emission spectroscopy was performed on layered 2H-MoSe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. The THz emission shows coherent phonon signals in addition to the usual single cycle THz pulse. Fourier analysis of the highly damped oscillatory response shows low frequency peaks below 1 THz (33 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> which we attribute to infrared active interlayer shear and breathing modes.

articleTitle: Features of a new THz/XUV endstation after FLASH2020+
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The FLASH2020 + upgrade project will include a new semi-permanent endstation for the FLASH1 THz beamline at DESY [1]. The FLASH THz-XUV pump probe facility provides XUV and THz pulses with low timing jitter. Combining these photon beams for pump-probe experiments alongside with an externally synchronized near-infrared (NIR) femtosecond laser system will promote research in various scientific fields. The endstation is capable of offering both, transmission- and reflection geometries combined with additional features such as a cryo-magnet and a cryogenic system at the sample position. Diagnostics of the photon beams near the sample position will also be available with novel tools under development.

articleTitle: Terahertz Beam Shaping: Gaussian to Flat-top Beam Conversion Through Tri-layer Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A flat-top beam is preferred to a normal Gaussian beam for various imaging applications since it provides more uniform illumination over a scene. In this paper, we present a highly efficient tri-layer metasurface lens for terahertz beam shaping, namely Gaussian to flat-top beam conversion. This metasurface includes linear polarization conversion, and a full 2 $\pi$ phase tunability range can be covered by varying the geometry of anisotropic resonators. The required phase profile of the metasurface lens is obtained through the Gerchberg–Saxton (GS) algorithm. Full-wave simulations and analytical results confirm that the incident Gaussian beam is transformed to a flat-top beam.

articleTitle: Far infrared imaging spectrometers for the next generation astronomical instruments
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Advances in far infrared astronomy have been, and will be, defined by instrument capabilities. Especially relevant is the development of imaging spectrometers for the wavelength range of 0.03-3 mm, which are not available at all at this moment. We will discuss recent advances in this field: First, we discuss the development of miniature on-chip spectrometers, that can operate in a 0.09-1 THz by using lossless superconducting circuits to create miniature spectrometers. For higher frequencies this is not possible due to material limitations, moreover instruments have to be operated in space due to the opacity of the atmosphere. Recent proposals for new missions focus on space-based observatories with optics cooled down to 4K, which offer unprecedented spectral imaging speeds, but require large arrays of extremely sensitive detectors. In the second part of this paper we will discuss the development of microwave Kinetic Inductance detectors with a sensitivity of NEP. 3.1.10-20 W/ãHz, sufficient for these applications.

articleTitle: Low-Frequency Vibrations and Magnetization of [C(NH2)3] [MII(HCOO)3] Metal-Organic Perovskites
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Seven metal-organic perovskites of [C(NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>] [M<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">II</sup>(HCOO)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>] with M= Mg, Ni, Co, Mn, Zn, Cu, and Cd were synthesized and investigated with terahertz time-domain spectroscopy as well as solid-state density functional theory. The similarity in structures resulted in similar spectral signatures but the relative peak positions and relative intensities varied with the metal atoms. The computational results revealed that the two main spectral features originate from similar lattice vibrations, except for the Cd material which has a slightly different structure. The influence of the electronic configuration of the metal d-orbitals on the spectral features was closely investigated.

articleTitle: Si COMS field-effect transistors as THz detectors: Imaging and sensing above 2 THz, 3D Fourier imaging and s-SNOM near-field microscopy
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Antenna-coupled field-effect transistors (TeraFETs) continue to establish themselves as reliable and versatile detectors of electromagnetic radiation for the entire THz frequency range. In this keynote presentation, we report about the state-of-the art of such detectors, and about the exploration of various applications of them as power detectors and heterodyne mixers.

articleTitle: A sub-Harmonic Abstraction Oscillator-based THz Reference Signal Generator in CMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This abstract presents a sub-harmonic abstraction oscillator-based sub-THz reference signal generator in a 22-nm FDSOI technology. The reference signal generation is a bottleneck in the THz sensing field, especially with the solid-state circuit method. The sub-harmonics abstraction with the dual-tank method achieves a 25 mW DC power consumption with a 0.15 THz output frequency, and its output power achieves −23 dBm, with could drive the next amplifier stage as a THz reference generation.

articleTitle: Terahertz Scanning Tunneling Spectroscopy of Graphene Nanoribbons on the Atomic Scale
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Ultrafast terahertz spectroscopy is an important tool for exploring new materials, yet unravelling some phenomena requires ultrafast experiments with atomic resolution such as terahertz scanning tunneling microscopy (THz-STM). Here, we advance THz-STM as a diagnostic technique for materials science by demonstrating terahertz scanning tunneling spectroscopy (THz-STS) with atomic spatial resolution and introduce an algorithm for extracting the underlying differential conductance from THz-STS measurements in both steady-state and pump-probe scenarios.

articleTitle: Thickness dependent Terahertz Spectroscopy of (100) Vanadium doped β-Ga2O3
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We investigate the thickness-dependent polarization-resolved optical properties of (100) β-Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> using Terahertz polarization-resolved spectroscopy. Further, we observe thickness-dependent transmission dips which are in C4 symmetry.

articleTitle: THz spectroscopy to probe long-range electrodynamic interactions between proteins
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We have recently experimentally demonstrated, for the first time, the activation of long-range attractive electrodynamic forces between proteins by means of THz spectroscopies, supported by fluorescence cross correlation spectroscopy and numerical simulations. Our experimental work provides a proof of principle of out-of-equilibrium collective oscillations activation of dipole-dipole electrodynamic intermolecular forces. It paves the way for exploring the potential role of electrodynamic intermolecular forces in living matter.

articleTitle: Photoinduced Phase Change in SnSe Probed by Ultrafast Multi-THz Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We use time-resolved multi-terahertz spectroscopy to measure the transient reflectivity and extract the optical conductivity of SnSe after femtosecond optical excitation. Polaron-like photoconductivity features are observed. The change in conductivity spectra and dynamics are strongly dependent on excitation density. Thresholded behavior depending on pump fluence supports a non-thermal change of state after ultrafast excitation of the electronic subsystem.

articleTitle: GaAs pHEMT Damage under High Power MMW Injection
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this paper, the damage effect on GaAs pHEMT of high-power millimeter wave (MMW) is studied based on TCAD. The results show that the heat generated in device decreases with the increasing of frequency. However, the current is obviously higher under MMW injection than that under low frequency microwave injection. In addition, pHEMT shows different nonlinear characteristics under different frequency bands.

articleTitle: Dielectric phase hologram with compact dual-reflector feed for submillimeter-wave imaging applications
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A dielectric phase hologram integrated with a dual-reflector feed for frequency-diverse submillimeter-wave imaging applications is proposed. The structure is based on Cassegrain optics and consists of a dielectric material with reflective surface coatings acting as primary and secondary reflectors. The hologram integrated into the dielectric aperture surrounding the secondary reflector has a quasi-random surface relief to create complex field patterns in the region of interest at 220-330 GHz.

articleTitle: Dual-function tunable metamaterial devices based on vanadium dioxide
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This article is based on vanadium dioxide to build a terahertz metamaterial device that can be exchanged in two functions: tunable and switchable between transmission and absorption.

articleTitle: Measurement of the Maximum Detectable Range of a THz-TDS System Driven by a Mode-Locked Laser Diode with a Divergent Beam
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We measure the maximum detectable distance and frequency range of an ultra-high repetition rate terahertz time-domain spectroscopy system in reflection geometry with conductive and dielectric samples, respectively. All measurements are performed without lenses or mirrors and thus with a divergent beam. We show that frequencies up to 600 GHz are detectable at a range of 1.2 meters. The measurements are in agreement with the expected theoretical values. This enables short-range radar imaging.

articleTitle: Solving Unsolved problems in IR and THz Near-field Nanoscopy with Rapid Simulation and Hybrid Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this work, we propose time-efficient schemes in the simulation, calculation, and understanding of tip-sample interaction in the near field, especially in the field of scattering-type scanning near-field microscope. Using rapid simulation methods, we can solve scientific problems with extended tip geometry, complex sample topography, and uniaxial or biaxial sample anisotropies, recreating tip dependent near-field spectral and images with high spatial resolution. Using machine learning, we explore the most accurate means to extract dielectric function from near-field spectra, and vice versa. Our methods shed light on the understanding of the contrast mechanism in s-SNOM imaging and spectroscopy, while also representing a valuable platform for future quantitative analysis of the experimental observations.

articleTitle: First Outdoor Measurements of a Submillimeter-Wave Differential Absorption Radar
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A differential absorption radar tuned near the 557 GHz water vapor absorption resonance is being developed as an instrument concept to measure absolute humidity out to distances of a few km from a lander or rover on the surface of Mars. Full instrument testing is difficult because Earth’s atmosphere is too absorptive near 557 GHz to measure radar backscattering at significant ranges. Therefore, alternative methods for testing critical functions of the radar are being evaluated, including outdoor measurements of the radar tuned to a more transmissive band near 360 GHz.

articleTitle: Terahertz Dispersion Compensator based on Subwavelength Fiber Grating
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate a compact terahertz subwavelength low-loss polymer grating for dual-polarization. Our grating supports large negative group velocity dispersion (over -188 ps/mm/THz) in a very short length of 43 mm, which can be exploited for dispersion compensation of terahertz links.

articleTitle: New opportunities open by advances in table-top high-power broadband THz sources
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Terahertz Time Domain Spectroscopy (THz-TDS) has become a ubiquitous tool in many scientific fields and is also increasingly deployed in industrial settings. While these systems become more and more mature, efficient lab-based THz generation techniques combining broad bandwidth and high dynamic range (e.g., as provided by sources with high THz average power and correspondingly high repetition rate) remain rare. Whereas many generation and detection techniques have seen continuous performance progress in the last few years driven by different application fields, the average power of practical sources remains low. A promising yet poorly explored route is simply to increase the average power of the driving lasers using state-of-the-art, high-average power ultrafast Yb-gain based lasers providing multi-100-W to kilowatt average-power levels as excitation sources, which are increasingly available both in laboratory setting and commercially. This new excitation regime for THz generation in various schemes has become an active area of research in the last few years, and current results have allowed to reach power levels in the THz domain in the multi-ten to multi-hundred milliwatts in different repetition rate regions – which was previously restricted to accelerator THz sources. This progress opens the door to a multiplicity of new and old research areas to be re-visited.

articleTitle: Experimental result on transmission line for solid-state 400 MHz DNP-NMR spectrometer
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this paper, a test result of transmission line used for solid-state 400 MHz dynamic nuclear polarization enhanced nuclear magnetic resonance spectrometer is presented. The transmission line, which is made up of corrugated waveguide about 3 meters, transmits the Gaussian like wave beam radiated from quasi-optical mode converter into the probe of spectrometer. The result shows that a wave beam with scalar Gaussian mode content about 99% is received at the end the transmission line.

articleTitle: Shared mirror resonator design for easy frequency tuning of THz lasers
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We demonstrate novel resonator design for THz lasers based on stimulated polariton scattering (SPS). Frequency tuning of SPS lasers requires adjustable crossing angle between the non-collinear fields at fundamental and Stokes wavelengths, which is especially challenging in surface emitting geometries. Our shared mirror resonator design utilizes a mirror shared between fundamental and Stokes cavities to automatically fix their overlap region within a SPS crystal. Robust and repeatable tuning is achieved by rotation of a single mirror.

articleTitle: Design of a W-band and F-band Broadband Meta-surface Output Window
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: To improve the working bandwidth of the output window for the TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> mode gyrotron traveling wave tube, a metasurface dielectric window is designed in this paper. The metasurface layer and the middle layers adopt the same dielectric material, so the equivalent dielectric constant of the matching layer can be easily changed by adjusting the height and inner and outer radius of the hollow cylinder structure and the distance between them to meet excellent matching. Simulation results show that the bandwidth of the output window reaches 66.5 GHz in W-band and F-band, the transmission parameter S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf> over -0.06dB.

articleTitle: THz irradiation reduces the DNA damage marker γH2AX in human cells: THz wave enhances DNA damage repair?
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Continuous-wave THz radiation (0.10 THz and 0.28 THz) was irradiated to HeLa cells treated by bleomycin (BLM), and the induction/repair of DNA damage was observed by visualizing γH2AX. The signal intensity of γH2AX was decreased during and after the BLM treatment when 0.28 THz wave (250 mW/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) was irradiated to the sample, suggesting that the THz wave enhances DNA damage repair. This phenomenon was not reproduced by 0.10 THz continuous-wave irradiation (200 mW/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>), suggesting the irradiation effect’s frequency dependence. Also, we performed a thermal control experiment by heating the sample to 42°C and observed the increase of γH2AX signals, indicating that the 0.28 THz irradiation affects DNA damage repair in a temperature-independent manner.

articleTitle: Removal of Artifacts in THz Imaging with a Synthetic Aperture
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Terahertz time-domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS) measurements from synthetic aperture radar (SAR) type measurements enable high resolution imaging. However, the reconstructed images show artifacts and noise. In this work, the benefit of considering the antenna pattern to reduce artifacts is demonstrated. Additionally, the limitations of focused transmission measurements are shown by measuring the beam profile in the focused and in the divergent part of a transmission terahertz path.

articleTitle: A Quantum Cascade Laser Microscope for Time-resolved Study of Membrane Proteins
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We have developed a confocal laser microscope operating in the wavelength range between 5.8 and 6.3 $\mu$m with a parallel confocal visible-light illumination channel for the study of light-sensitive membrane proteins. The measured diffraction-limited lateral resolution is 19 $\mu$m. Differences in the amide-I and II bands of proteins of the order of $10^{-5}$ can be detected with 30 ms time resolution using cryogen-free HgCdTe detectors and lock-in amplification at the QCL repetition rate. The microscope is suitable to study rhodopsins with a slow photocycle of several seconds.

articleTitle: Terahertz spectroscopy for non-destructive investigation of crystalline Nifedipine in tablets made from smartFilms®
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The crystallinity of Nifedipine (NIF) in tablets made from smartFilms<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup> was investigated by THz TDS. NIF remains amorphous for loadings of up to 5 w% and partly recrystallizes for higher loadings. The capability of smartFilms to stabilize the amorphous state of NIF can be improved by the addition of Polyvinylpyrrolidone.

articleTitle: Studying Photocurrents in α-Sn/Ge QW By Terahertz Time-Resolved Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Generation of a terahertz radiation in $\alpha$-Sn / Ge quantum wells by ultrashort laser pulses is studied. Existence of the $\alpha$-Sn at room temperature is shown by Raman spectroscopy. Cardinal differences were found in the parameters of THz pulses generated in samples with quantum wells widths of 4 nm, 6 nm sign and in nanostructures with quantum wells widths of 8.5 nm, 10 nm. The observed changes in the polarization dependences of the electric field of the THz radiation generated in $\alpha$-Sn/Ge nanostructures with changes in the width of quantum well going from 6 nm to 8.5 nm are associated with the transition from a normal band structure to an inverted one in these nanostructures.

articleTitle: Full-Wave Solver for Radiation from Thermal Sources
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The thermal emission from finite-size bodies is directly investigated without resorting to reciprocity. Specifically, an integral equation representing the electromagnetic field distribution on a conductive body under investigation is proposed. The source of the electromagnetic field is classic as it is an extension of Johnson noise sources to volumetric problems. The solution of the integral equation allows one to study the radiometric properties for geometries that are smaller than the investigated wavelengths, and in observation points, both in the near and in the far-field. The limits of validity of the formulation are clarified.

articleTitle: Terahertz Multiplexers Based on Valley Photonic Crystals
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We developed a low-loss, low-group-delay-dispersion, backscattering-free, scalable (de)multiplexer based on topological valley photonic crystals (VPCs) to realize full-duplex ultrahigh-capacity communication systems in the terahertz region. We designed low-pass filters whose cutoff frequency can be arbitrarily changed by adjusting the filter parameters of VPCs. A three-channel (de)multiplexer (triplexer) was fabricated using a cascaded filter and demonstrated its operation; we successfully conducted communications experiments under error-free conditions using on–off keying modulation.
