abstract: Coherent emission of the surface plasmon phonon polaritons in GaN surface relief gratings with the filling factors of 75 %, 50 %, and 25 % was investigated experimentally and theoretically. Finding an optimal grating filling factor of 25 % allowed us to observe the excitation of higher order modes and to increase the quality factor of polariton emission by up to 5.8 times demonstrating new approaches for polariton-based components in infrared and terahertz spectrum range.

articleTitle: Terahertz imaging of optically modulated graphene layers
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Terahertz (THz) imaging in combination with optical graphene modulation can serve as a versatilite technique for contactless characterization and discrimination of graphene layers. Maximum modulation depth of 45 % has been reached for double-layer graphene. This technique increased the contrast up to 16 % for single-layer graphene and 23 % for double-layer graphene under laser illumination.

articleTitle: Monolithically Integrated Silicon Photodiodes For Terahertz Electronic-Photonic Integrated Systems
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Aiming towards broadband scalable terahertz (THz) electronic-photonic integrated systems, a monolithically integrable silicon photodiode is investigated. The photosensitive charge transport mechanism along with bias dependent broadband THz characteristics are experimentally and theoretically investigated. An electrical equivalent circuit model explains the bias dependent variation in the intrinsic device parameters and simultaneously provides control to tune the impedance to achieve desired optimal matching in THz integrated circuits. An average THz rectification responsivity of 3 kV/W is measured across the 1-40 GHz, 110-170 GHz and 220-325 GHz frequency range.

articleTitle: High-resolution absorption spectroscopy with a phase-locked quantumcascade laser
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We report on high-resolution spectroscopy using a quantum-cascade laser (QCL) with an emission of 3.3 THz, which is locked to a mm-wave reference signal using a harmonic Schottkydiode mixer.

articleTitle: Classification of Mental State from Sub-THz Reflections from the Skin
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: By applying machine learning techniques on sub-THz reflectance measurements from the palms of 21 subjects, this work presents preliminary evidence that the reflected electromagnetic (EM) signal is inherently different during stress and relaxation periods. Furthermore, the obtained results demonstrate that this difference can be determined from a 30second-long measurement with an accuracy of 92% for binary classification between relaxation and stress and an accuracy of 88% for multiclass classification between relaxation, mental stress, and physical stress.

articleTitle: Efficient cooling of spintronic THz emitter in reflection geometry
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present THz generation in a Spintronic THz emitter (STE) in reflection geometry, excited by a high-power (7 W after chopping), high-repetition rate (up to 400 kHz) industrial Yb-based fiber laser at 1030 nm, temporally compressed to sub-30-fs. Our data shows that the backward cooling geometry allows for higher THz power and higher conversion efficiency from the STE. Additionally, we explore multiple repetition rates and pump diameters and give guidelines for optimized operation of these emitters in the μJ pulse energy regime.

articleTitle: Bias-free Terahertz Generation through Graded-composition InGaAs Photoconductive Structures
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present a bias-free photoconductive terahertz emitter that utilizes the deep built-in electric field in a graded-composition InGaAs structure to generate terahertz radiation at $\sim 1550$ nm optical pump wavelength. A plasmonic nanoantenna array is employed to confine photo-generated carriers in regions with the highest built-in electric field. We demonstrate record-high-power pulsed terahertz generation compared to other photoconductive emitters operating in the 1550 nm optical wavelength range, with power levels exceeding 860μW.

articleTitle: Terahertz hologram for homogenous illumination
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Terahertz devices are constantly being developed, both taking into account generation and detection of terahertz radiation. It enables creating more and more complex optical systems, which further forces development of passive optical elements. Here, terahertz hologram forming uniform illumination at a particular plane are proposed. The structures form the radiation to illuminate the square area of the examined sample. Few different approaches utilizing hologram as thin and lightweight option for such elements. Structures have been designed using iterative approach, their performance was numerically simulated, then they were manufactured using 3D printing technique and finally experimentally verified.

articleTitle: Third Harmonic Generation in Ge:Ga pumped by FLARE
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We observe third-harmonic generation (THG) in gallium-doped germanium (Ge:Ga) upon pumping with picosecond sub-THz (0.6-0.7 THz) pulses from the THz free-electron laser FLARE with a peak electric field strength of up to 4 kV/cm (30kW/cm2). The measurements are performed at cryogenic temperatures where the majority of holes are bound to the acceptor dopants. The dependence of the THG on the pump intensity exhibits a threshold-free power-law behavior with an exponent close to 3 as expected.

articleTitle: Interferometric Correction of Delay Errors in an Ultra-High Repetition Rate Terahertz Time-Domain Spectroscopy System
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A compact and economical terahertz time-domain spectroscopy system can be constructed by using a monolithic mode-locked laser diode (MLLD) as the light source and by employing an off-the-shelf optical delay unit (ODU). The sub-picosecond pulses emitted by the MLLD promise a system bandwidth of up to 2 THz. However, mechanical inaccuracy and wobble of the ODU often cause the delay axis of the detected terahertz signal to be non-linear. In this work, we show how the optical signal from the MLLD can be used in a Mach-Zehnder interferometer to generate a low-frequency reference signal that allows us to correct the delay axis with femtosecond-accuracy.

articleTitle: Design of a 0.6THz Compact Sum-Difference Network
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this paper, a 0.6THz (Terahertz) compact sum-difference network structure is proposed and designed. The calculated results show that the VSWR (voltage standing wave ratio) is below 1.35 in the range from 605GHz to 645GHz and the corresponding transmission coefficient from four input ports to the sum port is around -2.5dB with the consideration of conductive loss. The phase difference between four input ports and sum port, elevation-difference port, azimuth-difference port are also satisfied with in-phase/anti-phase. In addition, the results of far radiation field about this structure present that the null depth is superior to -50dB at 625GHz.

articleTitle: Broadband Mode Division Multiplexer Based on Terahertz Spoof Surface Plasmon Polaritons
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this paper, a broadband mode converter based on terahertz spoof surface plasmon polaritons is demonstrated. The incident surface waves in the TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> mode are converted to the TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> mode within the frequency range of 0.55–0.75 THz. Furthermore, a broadband mode division multiplexer is proposed, which simultaneously supports the TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>, TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> and TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> modes. The length of the whole device is about 14 times of the wavelength. For the first time to our knowledge, a mode division multiplexer based on terahertz spoof surface plasmon polariton is reported.

articleTitle: Disentangling Complex Current Pathways in Metallic Nanostructures by Terahertz Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We demonstrate a sensitive contactless characterization method based on terahertz (THz) time-domain spectroscopy to analyze the current pathways in nano-metallic devices. Our analysis of the THz conductivity spectra of a nano-metallic Ru/Co bilayer, supported by a resistor-network model, allows for the determination of the complex-valued electronic transparency coefficients both of the metallic bilayer and the internal nanointerface. Hence, the contributions of the internal current pathways and the current splitting at the interface have been quantified.

articleTitle: Multi-THz Pump Bandwidth Activation of Ultrafast Anharmonic Vibrational Coupling
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We use first-principles calculations to model multi-THz excitation and ultrafast coherent energy flow between vibrational degrees of freedom in gas-phase fluorobenzene. To accomplish this, we compute anharmonic coupling constants and use coupled equations of motion to model the ultrafast dynamics. We determined the role of anharmonic coupling as well as the symmetry of the vibrational modes in intramolecular energy transfer. The results from this modeling are guiding measurements of anharmonic coupling in fluorobenzene with a new multi-THz pump, femtosecond stimulated Raman scattering (FSRS) probe experimental setup.

articleTitle: Exploiting nano-iron binding with aptamers for the specific sensing of cancer biomarkers in the terahertz frequencies
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The quantitative measurement of cancer biomarkers based on aptamer-protein binding plays an important role in early cancer diagnosis. Conventional aptamer-based optical biosensing utilizes gold nanoparticles for aptamer modification. The use of iron nanoparticles can simplify the detection procedure due to its magnetic response. Here, we explore the use of ferrotetroxide nanoparticles for the modification of MUC-1-targeting aptamers. Mixtures with aptamer concentration ranging from 0 nM to 1000 nM were measured on a previously reported metamaterial structure. The results suggest that ferrotetroxide nanoparticles can successfully bind with aptamers with enhanced sensitivity in the terahertz frequencies.

articleTitle: Terahertz heterodyne spectroscopy of radio-frequency-driven frequency combs without moving parts based on telecommunication technology
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present heterodyne spectroscopy measurements up to 0.76 THz of a frequency comb generated by a terahertz emitter driven by a near-infrared source. This source consists of a narrowband (< 100 Hz), continuous wave, 1550.12-nm, telecommunication-wavelength laser and a high-precision radio-frequency signal generator, which drives a Mach-Zehnder interferometer to produce a wideband, near-infrared frequency comb with a mode spacing and repetition rate of 10 GHz. We synchronized this source to external reference sources and evaluated its potential as a replacement for conventional, mode-locked, cavity-based laser sources in terahertz frequency combs.

articleTitle: The study of the terahertz absorption spectrum of G-Quadruplex
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The secondary structures of nucleic acids are crucial to the regulation of genomic activities, and could potentially serve as a marker for some cancers. Question remains whether such structures could have distinct absorption features in the terahertz range, including a 1.6 THz peak absorption previously reported in methylated DNA. In this study, we examine the terahertz absorption spectrum of G-quadruplex (G4), a key secondary DNA structure that has been closely linked to cancer. The results show that in its most basic form, made up of self-assembled guanosine monophosphate (GMP), there are no distinct features. This result provides a reference for our ongoing investigation on other secondary structures of nucleic acids, and suggests that abnormal population of G4, as found in some cancers, may not be detectable via terahertz absorption spectroscopy.

articleTitle: Circular polarization immunity of the cyclotron resonance photoconductivity in two-dimensional electron systems
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Two-dimensional electron systems (2DES) subjected to a perpendicular magnetic field absorb electromagnetic radiation via cyclotron resonance (CR). Here we report a qualitative deviation from this well-known behavior. Our measurements in large-sized 2DES based on GaAs and HgTe reveal that the CR-enhanced photoconductivity becomes insensitive to the radiation helicity, showing almost the same signal amplitude for both CR active and inactive polarities of B, when the temperature T is lowered to that of liquid helium or below. Strikingly, the simultaneously measured CR in the transmission demonstrates a conventional strong helicity dependence for all T. In contrast similar photoconductivity measurements in graphene show no anomalies indicating an ordinary helicity-sensitivity in the whole investigated temperature range.

articleTitle: Broadband Lossless Matching Layer for Lens Arrays at THz Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present the design, fabrication and characterization of a broadband lossless matching layer for shallow lens arrays. The matching layer we propose is based on silicon pyramids fabricated on top of the lens array by means of laser ablation. This matching layer has the advantage that it covers over an octave of bandwidth. We have compared the performance of this matching layer with the commonly used parylene-C matching layer at the center of the targetted band, 500 GHz. The matching layer based on the silicon pyramids has 1.6 dB higher transmission.

articleTitle: Superconductor-insulator transition in a NbN film under in-plane magnetic field
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The complex conductivity of an ultrathin superconducting NbN film was investigated by terahertz time-domain spectroscopy under an in-plane magnetic field. Simultaneous use of Maxwell-Garnett effective medium theory and the model of optical conductivity by Herman and Hlubina [Phys. Rev. B 96, 014509 (2017)] assuming linear dependence of pair-breaking scattering rate on the magnetic field proved to correctly reproduce the terahertz spectra obtained experimentally in a magnetic field of up to 7 T.

articleTitle: Design of a ring-focus dual reflector objective for standoff sensing of spherical targets in the 220 – 330 GHz band
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A dual reflector objective design is explored in WR3.4 for sensing of spherical targets. The secondary mirror shadow enables coaxial integration of topical systems without additional obscuration of the submillimeter wave beam. The system is designed with geometrical optics and evaluated with physical optics. The power coupling efficiency between the source electric field and back scattered field from a spherical target is >0.4 across the frequency of interest.

articleTitle: Design of a Quasi-Optical Mode Converter for a 50GHz High Power Gyrotron
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Quasi-optical mode converters are usually used in gyrotrons to separate the spent electron beam from the outgoing power and convert the operating mode into a fundamental Gaussian wave beam. Using the cylindrical wave decomposition and a synthesis method, this paper designs a 50GHz/TE$_{\mathbf{93}}$ quasi-optical mode converter. According to the results, the conversion efficiency is 97.6%. And the vector Gaussian mode purity of the output beam is 99.8%. This quasi-optical mode converter will be used in a 50GHz high power gyrotron.

articleTitle: Determining the THz and Infrared Spectral Properties of Single Crystals and Thin Crystalline Films from First Principles
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present recent developments to the software packaged PDielec that can be used to post-process solid-state DFT calculations to determine the THz spectra of single crystals and thin crystalline films, including effects of crystalline orientation, beam incidence angle and beam polarisation, allowing the full interpretation of complex THz spectra. We use the explosive Cyclotrimethylenetrinitramine (RDX) as a previously well studied example.

articleTitle: Signal-to-noise ratio improvement of low-temperature passive near-field optical microscope using a tip-height modulation method
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We have recently developed a low-temperature scattering-type scanning near-field optical microscope (s-SNOM). The system mainly contains a highly sensitive long-wavelength infrared confocal microscope and a crystal tuning fork-based atomic force microscope. In this work, a sample-height modulation is replaced by a tip-height modulation. The acquisition time is reduced from 10 s to 3 s after improving the signal-to-noise ratio of the near-field signal. We carry out the near-field detection on a self-Joule heated NiCr wire deposited on SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. The resource of the near-field signals has been analyzed as the thermally excited evanescent wave due to fluctuating electrons.

articleTitle: Non-labeling Detection by Terahertz Surface Plasmon Resonance of Topological Insulator Bi2(Se, Te)3
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Terahertz (THz) wave, corresponding to intermolecular binding energy, is the key to realizing a non-labeling bio-medical sensor. To use topological insulators for THz surface plasmon resonance, we aim to enhance the sensitivity by a selective resonant excitation effect of the specific chemical binding and surface plasmon at the THz band. Here, we report the THz-SPR of Bi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Se<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Te, which has fewer lattice defects than Bi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Se<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>. Bi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Se<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Te was processed in a micro ribbon array to enhance SPR in the THz range. The avidin-biotin specific binding was observed due to the enhancement of THz-SPR with Bi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Se<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Te.

articleTitle: Integrated Microprobes for Terahertz Near-Field Time-Domain Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Despite the large range of promising applications for Terahertz technology, its real deployment has been limited by bulky equipment, mechanical disturbance, high power consumption, and low flexibility systems. Here, we present the design of a THz platform based on photonic integrated devices and photoconductive antennas that can reduce the footprint of all discrete optics in THz spectroscopy systems by two orders of magnitude. The integrated platform aims to contribute to the technological bridge that will take the THz spectrum from bulky systems to on-chip platforms.

articleTitle: Terahertz Near-Field Microscopy of Metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this work, near-field imaging of terahertz (THz)-frequency spoof surface plasmons (SSPs) supported by a variety of metal/dielectric metamaterial structures is reported. Our s-SNOM technique demonstrates deep sub-wavelength mapping of the field distribution associated with in-plane resonator modes in plasmonic dipole antennas and split ring resonator structures, as well as SSPs propagating on planar waveguide structures. Experimental results are compared with finite-element simulations and show excellent agreement. Furthermore, all-electronic coherent THz-s-SNOM has been employed to resolve the amplitude and phase images of localized plasmons in dipole antenna structures.

articleTitle: Equipment optimization for time-domain THz single-pixel imaging
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Developing a fast and robust THz time-domain imaging system that is low cost is essential for future commercial uses of such systems. Single-pixel imaging techniques are compatible with THz time-domain detectors and the combination of being a movement-free imaging system with undersampling capabilities gives them the potential of having fast acquisition rates. However, most undersampling algorithms have been designed for visible light imaging technology which is very different from THz technology. Here, we optimize the equipment and algorithms used for time-domain THz single-pixel imaging.

articleTitle: 1.5 MW, 140 GHz Gyrotron for W7-X - development status and experimental results -
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: For the upgrade of the Electron Cyclotron Resonance Heating (ECRH) system of the stellarator Wendelstein 7-X (W7-X), a 1.5 MW, 140 GHz continuous-wave (CW) gyrotron is under development. In order to provide a first experimental verification of the scientific microwave and electron beam optics design of the gyrotron at pulse lengths of a few milliseconds (ms), Karlsruhe Intitule of Technology (KIT) has developed and tested successfully a short-pulse pre-prototype gyrotron. The tube was stably operated at up to 1.6 MW output power. The status of the project as well as the results achieved during the first experimental campaign, are presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Active CEP control of terahertz pulses using artificial microstructure
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Despite rapid progress in metamaterials, the carrier-envelope phase (CEP) control for terahertz (THz) pulse is still challenging due to its broadband feature. Here, we demonstrate a THz CEP shifter, which consists of different stereo-metamaterial (stereo-MM) arrays. The performance of the CEP shifter is characterized by using a THz-TDS system. Simulation and experimental results show that the CEP of the THz pulse can be ideally adjusted by the proposed CEP shifter, which can be shifted as high as 2$\pi$.

articleTitle: Accurate modulation of graphene metamaterials with no-electrode through free electrons
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: 2D material graphene has a wide range of applications in terahertz, most graphene modulation is performed with electrodes for gate voltage modulation or high-power laser pulse modulation. Here, we construct a self-developed system based on scanning electron microscopy (SEM) combined with terahertz time-domain spectroscopy (TDS) to experimentally demonstrate the tuning of a no-electrode graphene metamaterial modulation. Because the electron beam radius and position of the SEM is highly controllable, it can be adjusted precisely. This is of seminal importance for the development of terahertz graphene terahertz devices.

articleTitle: Demonstration of a W-band Kilowatt-level Continuous Wave Sheet Beam Traveling Wave Tube Interaction Circuit Design
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The power capacity and thermal density of millimeter-wave and terahertz devices directly limit the ability to operate in continuous waves. Based on the proposed high-power slow-wave structure, a kW-level W-band sheet beam traveling-wave tube (SB-TWT) is demonstrated. PIC simulation shows that the maximum power is 1600W, and corresponding electronic efficiency is ~ 20%. The 3-dB bandwidth is 17 GHz from 85 GHz to 102 GHz. Thermal analysis shows that its power capacity is sufficient to support the continuous wave operation at an electronic transmission rate of not less than 93%.

articleTitle: Coherent Control of Single-Molecule Switching Reactions with Sub-Cycle Atomic Forces
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We introduce sub-cycle atomic-scale forces provided by near fields of a lightwave-driven scanning probe tip. Exerting these ultrafast forces to key atoms of a single-molecule switch allows us to coherently steer a select structural rotation that modulates the switching statistics by up to 39%.

articleTitle: High-Power Cavity-Type RTD THz Oscillators Integrated with Impedance-Matched Slot Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We proposed and fabricated high-power cavity-type RTD THz oscillators integrated with impedance-matched slot antenna. By changing the load admittance with the slot length, the impedance matching condition can be satisfied. A high-power oscillation of 131 μW was obtained at 730 GHz with a 3.5 μm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> RTD. The experimental results reasonably agreed with theoretical calculation.

articleTitle: Cooled Bolometer Design for High-Sensitivity THz Passive Imaging
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Detectors with a Minimum Detectable Power (MDP) under the picowatt range are required for Terahertz passive imaging. A cooled bolometer using a high-impedance surface associated with a metal dipole to ensure a broadband absorption centered at 425 GHz is presented as a solution. A lateral PiN diode is sensing temperature modifications in the bolometer operating at liquid-nitrogen temperature. Diode prototypes were fabricated on Silicon-On-Insulator 8” wafers with a 50 nm active silicon layer. Their experimental thermal resolution as low as 0.2 mK at 81 K leads to an estimated MDP of the future bolometer reaching 2.45 pW at 25 frames per second.

articleTitle: The Role of Terahertz Dynamics in Solid-state Protein Formulations
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Utilizing four different model substances, the effect of size on the dynamics of one-component lyophilized (freeze-dried) products was studied with terahertz time-domain spectroscopy and differential scanning calorimetry. While sucrose exhibited the well-known behavior of increasing absorption with temperature observed in small organic molecular systems, the polypeptide bacitracin and the two globular proteins lysozyme and human serum albumin (HSA) showed a more complex temperature dependence. Further analysis was performed on the extrapolated vibrational density of states and the boson peak that showed that localized onset of motions influences the spectrum widely without necessarily leading to an alteration of the rate of absorption change at a single frequency far below room temperature.

articleTitle: Terahertz Time-domain Spectroscopy System Using Sub-Bandgap Excitation of Photo-conductive Antenna Made with Low-Temperature Grown Gallium Arsenide
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Terahertz time domain spectroscopy system is constructed using photoconductive emitter and detector antennas operated with sub-bandgap excitations of low-temperature grown gallium arsenide. The system characteristics are investigated using femtosecond lasers with emission wavelengths at 1 $\mu \mathrm{m}$ and 1.5 $\mu \mathrm{m}$. The same level of dynamic range with the 800-nm above bandgap excitation was obtained with the 1.5-$\mu \mathrm{m}$ sub-bandgap excitation, while a lower dynamic range was obtained with the 1-$\mu \mathrm{m}$ subbandgap excitation.

articleTitle: Thermal Design of Mirror System for Quasi-optical Mode Converters in 170 GHz Mega-watts Gyrotrons
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Using water cooling method to dissipate heat of mirror system for quasi-optical mode converters in 1MW,170GHz gyrotrons. In the long pulse state, the power loss caused by the Gaussian beam on each mirror is 2000W, which is the heat source of the mirrors. The simulation results indicate that the maximum temperature of the mirrors in working condition is about 434K and the total deformations of the mirror surfaces are below 0.1mm. Empirically, the total deformations meet the transmission requirements of mirror surface precision.

articleTitle: THz TDS of Nifedipine in Tablets Made from Cellulose Powder
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Nifedipine (NIF) dissolved in acetone was applied onto tablets made from microcrystalline cellulose (MCC) powder. After the solvent evaporated, the crystallinity of NIF loaded into the tablets was examined by terahertz (THz) time-domain spectroscopy (TDS), which revealed that NIF remained amorphous. The content of NIF in tablets was subsequently increased by repeating the loading process, which led to a partial recrystallization of NIF. The results suggest that cellulose pressed into tablets can maintain pharmaceuticals amorphous in a similar way as paper films (i.e., smartFilms<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup>).

articleTitle: Emulating a broadband frequency sweep for Terahertz thin-film imaging
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Conventional continuous-wave Terahertz imaging and thickness resolution systems often rely on the Fabry-Pérot resonances generated in the sample being imaged. As the samples become thinner, larger frequency sweeps are necessary for their visualisation. In this work, we demonstrate a post-processing technique employing zero-padding of a smaller frequency sweep between frequency intervals as low as 10 GHz up to intervals of 200 GHz, conducted between 0.6-0.8 THz, to emulate the thickness resolution generally achieved by orders of magnitude larger frequency ranges.

articleTitle: Microbolometer Pixel Based on Vertical CNT Membrane for Broadband Absorption at Room Temperature
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A design for a unique microbolometer pixel based on a vertically aligned carbon nanotube (CNT) membrane is introduced for a broadband absorption range. The new platform technology was fabricated and characterized for the infrared (IR) region that shows a fast response >1000 Hz and a temperature coefficient of resistance (TCR) of about 0.28%/°C with a high thermal stability for applications at temperatures even beyond 200 °C. With a conservative calculation of the absorbed laser power, a responsivity of 1 mA/W was already achieved. The structure has the potential for a high integration density with a pitch dimension down to $2\times 2 ~\mu$m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Investigation and optimized design of 0.22THz Microstrip Bandpass Filter based on suspension structure
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We designed a 220GHz hairpin microstrip bandpass filter based on suspension structure. In addition, the influence of the silver paste on the quartz substrate during the actual processing is fully considered. Finally, a 220GHz bandpass filter with bandwidth up to 20G, insert loss less than 2dB and return loss better than 20dB is obtained.

articleTitle: Superconducting on-chip tunable mm-wave resonator
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present a design of a tunable on-chip resonator that can benchmark the nonlinear kinetic inductance (KI) properties of various superconducting thin films in the W-band (75-110 GHz), for quantum device applications. Our design uses a quarter-wavelength microstrip resonator with ground plane cutout for transmission measurements, WR10 input & output ports, DC bias line and radial-stub notch filters to suppress RF leakage into the bias lines. Our resonator design procedure uses simulations with perfect electric conductors as an initial reference case, which will be later replaced by finite-impedance material to include the effect of sheet inductance.

articleTitle: Highly superlinear terahertz photoconductance in GaAs quantum point contacts in the deep tunneling regime
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We report on the highly superlinear intensity dependence of the photosignal from quantum point contacts. In our experiments, the devices were made of GaAs quantum wells operating in the deep tunneling regime ($G_{dark} \lt 2e^{2}/h$). With low-power, continuous-wave terahertz laser radiation, the photoconductance increased exponentially with intensity and enlarged by nearly four orders of magnitude with as little as 1000 mW/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. This effect occurred only for a radiation electric field aligned with the source-drain direction. We attribute this intense effect to the local diffraction of the incident field, modifying the height of the tunnel barrier. Further, we showed that a magnetic field suppresses the photoresponse, especially under conditions of cyclotron resonance.

articleTitle: High-sensitive multi-stage terahertz wave parametric up-conversion detection based on KTiOPO4 crystal
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A highly sensitive multi-stage terahertz (THz) wave parametric up-conversion detector based on KTiOPO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> (KTP) crystal pumped by 1064nm laser (10 ns, 10Hz) was demonstrated in this paper. The up-conversion signal was amplified in two KTP crystals based on non-collinear and collinear phase matching respectively to improve detection sensitivity. The detectable THz frequency range was 4.30-4.47 THz and 4.81-4.95 THz. The minimum detectable energy of 244pJ was realized with dynamic range of 36dB at 4.45THz, which was an order of magnitude higher than that of commercial Golay cell. Compared with LiNbO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> crystal, the parametric up-conversion detection based on KTP crystal can realize high frequency range (>3 THz) THz wave detection.

articleTitle: The in-plane photoelectric effect: A new quantum mechanism of detecting terahertz radiation in a two-dimensional electron system
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We report on the discovery of a new quantum phenomenon in a 2D electron gas (2DEG) that enables efficient THz detection [1]. In this effect, electrons absorb THz photons and jump on an artificially created, electrically tunable potential step within the plane of a degenerate 2DEG. The effect is realized in a dual-gate FET-type device with two antenna-shaped gates on top of a semiconductor heterostructure. The device demonstrates a strong photoresponse, which cannot be explained by heretofore known mechanisms and which is an order of magnitude larger than expected from classical plasmonic mixing. We show that the observed photoresponse can be explained by a quantum mechanism that we call the in-plane photoelectric effect. Our theory predicts that this new mechanism is ideally suited for detection of radiation across the entire THz gap.

articleTitle: 300 GHz frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radar system for detecting rocks’ lithological changes
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Remote sensing of lithological changes is of high interest in industrial domains such as geotechnics and mineral exploration. Usually, applied methods are based in acoustics or ground penetrating radars working at HF/VHF frequencies. Their limitations are due to the trade-off between spatial resolution and rock penetration. Currently, frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW) at frequencies higher than 60 GHz are more accessible and available at reasonable prices. However, their feasibility for measuring lithological changes has not been studied yet. Therefore, in this work we have proposed to make measurements with a 300 GHz FMCW radar to detect the interfaces between two limestone of similar refractive indices. As a result, they were successfully detected even after 2 cm rocks’ penetration.

articleTitle: The Gain Analysis of the 345 GHz Traveling-Wave Amplifier with Nonuniform Grating
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The preliminary analysis of operation of the 345 GHz sectioned traveling-wave amplifier with the three-stage nonuniform grating has been presented. The design is based on both the simulation and the experimental results obtained for the W-band amplifier earlier. The THz amplifier is designed for the operation with the nonrelativistic sheet electron beams and the oversized beam-wave system. The result of calculations, carried out with the use of the large-signal theory, demonstrated the power gain up to 23 dB for the frequency region from 335 GHz to 365 GHz in the proposed amplifier. The output power of at least 1 W was predicted for the reasonable level of driving signal, that is less than 50 mW.

articleTitle: Near-field study of THz collective excitations in topological insulators
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Collective excitations at terahertz (THz) frequencies of thin films of Bi2Se3 and Bi2Te2.2Se0.8 topological insulators are investigated by a combination of hyperspectral nano-imaging and detectorless scattering-near-field optical microscopy (s-SNOM). By mapping the THz near-field response, we provide first experimental evidence for the activation of bulk plasmons polaritons and hyperbolic phonon-polaritons coupled with the Dirac-plasmons associated with the topological surface-states. The unveiled low-loss, highly tunable and strongly confined terahertz electromagnetic modes prospect promising application in quantum nano-photonics.

articleTitle: Near-Field Imaging of a TeraHertz deep-subwavelength Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this paper, we present a study on the near-field distribution on a metasurface consisting of deep-subwavelength rectangular apertures. The metasurface is made out of a free-standing stainless steel sheet of thickness 100 microns, by making periodic perforation using LASER milling techniques. We measured the near-field distribution inside the aperture cavity, which shows a resonance in the near-field intensity. This resonance in a near electric field can be leveraged for various applications such as high-resolution sensing and imaging.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic field confinement by bound states in the continuum
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Confining electromagnetic fields as tightly as possible has driven research in optics and photonics. Conventionally, extreme sub-wavelength confinement is possible at the cost of absorption losses in resonant structures. Here, we experimentally show that it is possible to get an extreme confinement of the electromagnetic field in a resonant system without losses. We exploit symmetry protected bound states in the continuum which fully suppress any radiative losses. Using our unique local excitation and detection terahertz microscope we can measure the confinement of the electric field at the surface of our array, revealing an amplitude decay of $\lambda$/38 at 0.39 THz.

articleTitle: Optical conductivity measurement of chemically-doped graphene via terahertz time-domain spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We study optical conductivity of CVD-grown graphene depending on chemical doping conditions using terahertz time-domain spectroscopy. Varying the exposure duration of FeCl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> solution, used for copper etching in the transfer process, allows graphene to have various carrier densities. According to terahertz transmission measurement, we confirm that the terahertz conductivity of graphene tends to increase with the exposure time to the chemical solution. It supports that Fermi level of graphene film can be controlled by chemical doping based on cooper etchants.

articleTitle: Terahertz spectral properties of medical films cross-linked by electron beam
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We investigated the property changes of medical film cross-linked by electron beam (e-beam) irradiation, using THz time-domain spectroscopy (TDS). The cross-linked medical film showed higher refractive indices and absorption coefficients than those of reference film in the THz regime. THz-TDS have a potential for monitoring of cross-linking on the medical film. In addition, the THz-TDS method has potential as a practical nondestructive technique for polymer examination and analysis.

articleTitle: Design Aspects for Sensitive Metasurface-Based THz Biosensing in Aqueous Solutions
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Metasurfaces can improve the sensitivity of THz biomolecule detection significantly. Still, the high absorptive properties of water-based matrices prevent direct measurements under physiologically relevant conditions. In this work, we present a collection of sensor designs focusing on their distinctive geometries and transmission behavior. One major advantage of the proposed structures is their preservation of a resonance feature in the frequency response, even for measurements in water. Consequentially, efficient THz detection of larger and more complex entities such as vesicular structures like exosomes becomes possible.

articleTitle: Subthreshold VO₂ vertical switches for large-bandwidth millimeter-wave and sub-terahertz detection
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Non-linear impedance characteristics of VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> offer solutions to highly sensitive radio-frequency (RF), millimeter-wave (mm-wave), and terahertz (THz) detectors. We demonstrate high-speed broadband sensibility of miniaturized VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> switches by utilizing the nonlinearity close to the abrupt insulator-to-metal transition (IMT). We apply an intensity modulated sub-THz signal to the 2-terminal devices inside a coplanar waveguide (CPW) and detect the down-mixed component at the intermediate frequency (IF). The maximum output IF power selectivity over noise reaches 45 dB with a −3 dB bandwidth of 12 GHz. Its responsivity to sub-THz radiation and high-speed switching makes our design a potential detector for a wide range of high-data-rate wireless applications.

articleTitle: Hyperbolic Lens Antenna in Groove Gap Waveguide Technology at Sub-millimeter waves
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this paper, a flat hyperbolic lens antenna using Groove Gap Waveguide (GGW) technology is designed at 300 GHz. A GGW horn antenna is used to feed the metamaterial lens placed in a parallel plate waveguide (PPW), in order to increase the directivity in the direction of propagation. The combination of both devices, the metalens and the GGW antenna, achieves excellent radiation performance.

articleTitle: High-Sensitivity Terahertz Microfluidic Biosensor Based on Metal Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This paper presents a terahertz microfluidic biosensor based on metal metasurface. The resonant structure of this biosensor is four mutually symmetrical open ring structures. The analyte is placed between the metal resonant structure and the metal mirror, so that the terahertz wave interacts with the analyte fully. Simulation results show that the biosensor has an absorption rate of 99% at 0.4-0.9 THz and a sensitivity of 233GHz/RIU. In addition, the biosensor is polarization insensitive and has potential applications in nondestructive detection of trace materials and biomedicine.

articleTitle: Electron Gun and Beam Dump System for 170GHz, 1MW Gyrotron
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The design simulation of the electron gun and beam dump system are presented in this paper. The both system works for the 170GHz, 1MW gyrotron which has operational mode TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">28,12</inf>. The gun geometry and beam optimization are performed with numerical code EGUN and the optimized result for the both systems are shown.

articleTitle: Portable THz Frequency Standard using Difference-Frequency Generation of Acetylene-Stabilized Telecom Diode Lasers
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We have developed a portable THz frequency standard. It is based on difference-frequency generation (DFG) of two telecom lasers in a uni-traveling-carrier photodiode (UTC-PD). Both lasers were simultaneously stabilized to acetylene $(^{13}\mathrm{C}_{2}\mathrm{H}_{2})$ transitions by modulation transfer spectroscopy using one reference gas cell. The fractional instability of the THz standard at 288GHz was attained to be $1\times ^{10-8}$ over 400s averaging time. This THz standard serves as a new wavelength reference for THz spectroscopy equipments and consequently improves their measurement accuracy.

articleTitle: A Novel Terahertz Metasurface of Electromagnetically Induced Transparency Based on Carbon Nanotube Films
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A study of electromagnetically induced transparency based on carbon nanotube-based terahertz metasurface consisting of an array of two asymmetric split rings has been presented. The theoretical results agree with the simulation results. Moreover, we have investigated the sensing performance of the proposed terahertz metasurface.

articleTitle: Flow Rate Effect on THz-TDS of Thin-film Fluid in Microfluidic Device
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Here we present a compact microfluidic device for thin-film water fluid measurements in reflection THz-TDS. We discuss the variables that need to be considered when utilizing this device in THz-TDS, and we find that different flow rates can cause subtle changes in the THz response.

articleTitle: A 128×128 Low-power Cryogenic Readout Circuit for Ge-based Blocked-impurity-band Detector
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A 128 × 128 low-power cryogenic readout circuit suitable for Ge-based Blocked-impurity-band detector is developed by way of 0.18 μm CMOS technology in this paper. Based on the extraction of parameters and the establishment of the cryogenic temperature model of MOSFET, we focus on the design of the pixel circuit and readout mode. In order to reduce the power consumption, we adopt the rolling mode. The correlated double sampling technology is also used to reduce the channel noise in this design. The designed readout circuit can work at both room temperature and 6K, where the maximum power consumption is 16.37mW, and the working frequency is 20Hz.

articleTitle: Structural Regulation of Fiber Biomaterials by Far-IR Radiation
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In recent years, far-infrared radiation technique has been employed in chemical, biological, and material research fields, and it can give remarkable effects distinct from a simple thermal treatment on various biological substances. Here, we show a latest study on irradiation effects of far-infrared rays from two-kinds of high-power light sources, free-electron laser and gyrotron, on cellulose fiber that is potential for functional biomaterials.

articleTitle: Laterally Emitting Nearly Single-Cycle THz Pulse Generation in Two-Dimensional Aperiodically Poled Lithium Niobate Crystal
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: It is shown that intense, nearly single-cycle THz pulses can be generated in two-dimensional aperiodically poled lithium niobate (2D APPLN) structure formed by placing a multiple-slit shadow mask in front of a large aperture 1D APPLN crystal. The THz wave is emitted perpendicular to the direction of pump pulse propagation, which is favorable for their independent control. The electric field strength in the focus of lens is estimated to be about 0.6 MV/cm at pump pulse intensity of 50 GW/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Characterization of high permittivity and low losses TiO2 sintered material for THz applications
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this work we demonstrate the fabrication and characterization of TiO2 ceramics material with high refractive index and low losses in the 300- 1400 GHz range. The optimized fabrication process, based on Spark Plasma Sintering, allows for the elaboration of high-density materials whose dielectric properties make them good candidates for the design of fully dielectric metamaterials.

articleTitle: Wavelength dependence of plasma-based THz generation in liquids
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This work is intended to take the first step to study the effect of input laser wavelength on the efficiency of liquid-based THz radiation sources. The numerical simulation data indicate a real opportunity to improve the existing sources. However, the resulting gain is not as significant as in the case of the two-color air filament, which points out at the need for further optimization.

articleTitle: A misalignment-insensitive sub-THz data link based on an AI nonlinear equalizer
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this study, we demonstrated a simple, low-cost terahertz wireless communication network and investigated the effect of angle misalignment on bit error rate. The results show that the 3 Gbaud 4QAM-OFDM signals can still be retrieved at short distances (<1 m). We pushed even farther, and by utilizing a neural network, we developed an Artificial intelligence-based nonlinear equalizer, which enhances the system’s robustness to misalignment.

articleTitle: Antenna-coupled MKIDs for an Integral Field Unit at 7.8 THz
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A focal plane array of extended-hemispherical silicon lenses coupled to aluminum coplanar-waveguide (CPW) Microwave Kinetic Inductance Detectors (MKIDs) has been designed to operate at 7.8 THz. Low-dispersive leaky-wave radiation has been used to efficiently illuminate the antireflection-coated lenses. To minimize the radiation loss from the antenna feeding lines at these high frequencies, the CPWs have been miniaturized and placed on a dielectric membrane. A test device has been fabricated and its experimental characterization in terms of sensitivity, optical coupling, and beam patterns is ongoing.

articleTitle: Terahertz Wave Shielding and Absorption Materials Based on Organic Aerogels
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: With the development of terahertz technology, there is a booming demand of THz waves shielding and absorption materials to avoid electromagnetic interference or pollution. The electromagnetic interference shielding effectiveness not only depends on their composition, but also is influenced by their microstructures. Porous structure has special advantage of low density and high electromagnetic wave reflection’s ability. We design and prepare the THz wave shielding and absorption materials based on organic aerogel.

articleTitle: Vector Network Analyser-based Terahertz Solution for High-quality Medical Imaging
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This paper introduces a comparative evaluation between Terahertz (THz) imaging (based on a Vector Network Analyzer (VNA)), and Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT). The use of the VNA is assessed in suppressing the issue of speckle noise introduced in OCT imaging, which hinders clinical interpretation. Depth profiles of the sample (A-Scans) were produced by both systems which, when stacked, build a B-scan image. Each system was visually evaluated by its ability to spatially resolve both along and normal to the beam axis, using a phantom resembling a tooth with a hole, including a lattice structure representing decay. Relative to commonly appreciated x-ray imaging, results show that comparatively VNA-based imaging can be done to greater spatial resolution than with infrared OCT.

articleTitle: Efficient double-side detection in the mid-IR using a QWIP MIM architecture on a transparent substrate
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present a mid-IR ($\lambda \approx$ 8.3 μm) quantum well infrared photodetector (QWIP) fabricated on a transparent substrate, allowing photo detection with illumination from either the front surface or through the substrate. The device is based on a 400 nm-thick GaAs/AlGaAs semiconductor QWIP heterostructure enclosed in a metal-insulator-metal (MIM) optical cavity. For two different excitation configurations - backside illumination through the substrate and frontside direct illumination - we present passive optical characterizations (reflectivity and transmissivity), electric transport measurements and photocurrent generation, showing similar broadband spectral response for the two detector ports and an experimental $T_{\text{blip}}$ of $\approx$ 200K.

articleTitle: 0.22THz Wideband Doubler Based on a Single-chip GaAs Monolithic Integration
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We designed a terahertz wideband doubler with a frequency range of 200 GHz to 240 GHz. This frequency doubler uses six-anode Schottky diodes Integrated on a GaAs substrate. Based on the traditional balanced doubler circuit topology, a special input reduced height waveguide structure is adopted to make the input signal more easily absorbed by the diodes, thereby achieving high efficiency and wideband. The simulation results show that the efficiency is greater than 30% in the output frequency range of 200GHz-240GHz, pumped with 200mW, and the peak efficiency at 235GHz is 37%.

articleTitle: Reagent identification using terahertz spectroscopic imaging with machine learning
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We achieved to detect reagent distribution with high accuracy and high-speed by combining machine learning and terahertz spectroscopic imaging using the multi-wavelength terahertz wave parametric generator. 3200 pixel identification image could be acquired in a few minutes without any post-processing.

articleTitle: Helical Micro-Undulators For XFELs
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Short-period undulators formed by four alternating longitudinally and radially magnetized rare-earth helices can create a high transverse field near the axis. Such undulators can provide a larger average oscillatory electron velocity than Halbach planar undulators and, in addition, the confinement of particles along both transverse coordinates. Hybrid undulators formed by two longitudinally pre-magnetized rare-earth and steel helices are easier to implement. Both types of micro-undulators seem promising for the creation of compact XFELs.

articleTitle: Field- and frequency-dependent disassembly of polymerized and chemically stabilized microtubules by intense THz pulses
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Non-thermal biological effects of terahertz (THz) radiation have been reported in cellular- and tissue-level systems, however the fundamental interactions with biomolecular structures underlying these effects remains unclear. Microtubules (MTs) are cytoskeletal protein complexes that regulate the mitotic and morphologic characteristics of cells, and are a promising potential target underlying THz-induced functional changes observed at higher levels of biological organization. It is shown that extended exposure to intense THz pulses induces significant structural modifications to polymerized MTs in vitro. Results suggest potential therapeutic applications of THz radiation by inhibiting mitotic activity of diseased tissue.

articleTitle: Propagation-invariant channels on terahertz metasurfaces with hyperbolic dispersion
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We report the implementation of split-ring resonator (SRR) metasurfaces with hyperbolic dispersion that allow spoof surface-plasmon polaritons (SSPPs) to propagate on diffraction-free in-plane paths. We use these propagation-invariant channels to sustain a confined propagation of terahertz SSPPs within the metasurface. By changing the location of the SRR-gap, the propagation angle of the SSPP can be tuned, additionally allowing for arbitrary in-plane routing.

articleTitle: A flexible high-repetition-rate source of sub-half-cycle terahertz pulses based on spatially indirect interband transitions
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present a flexible and scalable source of strong phase-locked THz pulses based on shift currents in type-II-aligned epitaxial semiconductor heterostructures. The THz waveforms are extremely asymmetric and exhibit only 0.45 optical cycles within the FWHM of their intensity envelope, peak fields above 1.1 kV cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> and spectral components up to the mid-infrared, at a repetition rate of 4 MHz. Our detailed quantum mechanical analysis reveals a novel emission process, where local charging dynamics pulls spatially separated electrons and holes back together, resulting in emission of almost unipolar THz waveforms.

articleTitle: Highly Efficient Terahertz Spintronic Emitter Integrated with Optimized Photonic Crystal
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Spintronic terahertz emitters are new to the terahertz source family. They are broad-spectrum and gapless unlike traditional sources involving semiconductors and nonlinear crystals. Moreover, they can emit intense electromagnetic fields strong enough for nonlinear terahertz application, but on the other hand, they can operate with low excitation pulse energy, which makes them quite versatile sources. Unfortunately, spintronic emitters suffer from low conversion efficiency. In this work, we present a spintronic emission enhancement by integrating the emitter with a designed photonic structure. We show experimental results accompanied by simulations demonstrating the efficiency improvement up to almost one order.

articleTitle: Ag-doped cellulose nanofibers for THz wave plates
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The limited availability and environmental issues of materials resources call for the development of biodegradable devices, which also applies to THz devices. Here, we present our work developing THz wave-plates based on cellulose nanofibers and Ag nanomaterials. Emphasis is put on optimizing the wave plate efficiency based on the arrangement and orientation of the nanofibers and the type and concentration of Ag nanoparticles.

articleTitle: High quality factor resonance of metallic terahertz metasurface driven by bound states in the continuum
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A metallic terahertz metasurface based on bound states in the continuous is proposed and the properties of near infinitely resonance quality factor are investigated. The strong limitation of the radiation loss significantly reduces the linewidth of the resonance, and the temporal coupled mode theory is used to verify the generation of this BICs. The research results provide a new solution to realize the high-quality factor resonance, which is sorely desired for developing ultrasensitive terahertz sensor and slow light devices.

articleTitle: Simulation Of Multi-Anode Injection Gun For Megawatt Gyrotron
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this paper, a double-anode Magnetron Injection electron Gun (MIG) has been designed for megawatt level gyrotron. On this basis, a triple-anode magnetron injection electron gun was designed by optimizing the anode structure. Based on electromagnetic simulation analysis, the function that accurately regulating electron injection performance is implemented by adjusting the potential distribution of anodes, and the flow rate of electron beam improved by optimized the structure of the control anode.

articleTitle: Quantification of water states in thin proton exchange membrane manufacturing using terahertz time-domain spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Water states in proton exchange membranes have previously been extracted using terahertz time-domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS) for thick Nafion membranes. In this work, we have developed a parametric based algorithm for data analysis and applied it to thin industrially relevant membranes (13-70μm), processed under different conditions, producing results consistent with conventional gravimetric analysis and prior demonstrations. This therefore opens up opportunities for rapid membrane investigations and understanding.

articleTitle: On the influence of water on THz vibrational spectral features of molecular crystals
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The collective vibrations in molecular crystals can be probed using terahertz spectroscopy, providing unique characteristic spectral fingerprints. However, the association of the spectral features to the crystal conformation, crystal phase and its environment is a difficult task. We present a combined computational-experimental study on the incorporation of water in lactose molecular crystals, and show how simulations can be used to associate spectral features in the THz region to crystal conformations and phases. Furthermore, we also show that water does not play only a perturbative role but fully participates in the emergence of the THz vibrations

articleTitle: Traveling wave photomixers based on low-temperature-grown Gallium Arsenide reaching 50 mA/W under 1550 nm CW illumination
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this work we present an original design of a traveling-wave photomixer (TWP) based on low-temperature-grown GaAs layer (LT-GaAs) optimized for 1550 nm wavelength excitation. The optical wave is absorbed in the LT-GaAs through an integrated silicon nitride-based waveguide. The optical waveguide is centered between two metallic contacts that serves as biasing electrodes and metallic strips of a THz coplanar waveguide. The device exhibited dc photoresponses as high as 50 mA/W.

articleTitle: Structural evolution of amorphous solid water studied by THz spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Time-domain terahertz (THz) spectroscopy is used to monitor the growth, and the structural evolution of amorphous solid water (ASW), during the deposition process at 80 K and subsequent heating. THz absorption spectra with characteristic spectral features were observed, revealing the amorphous nature of vapor-deposited ice film and its crystallization into the stacking disordered ice (ice Isd) at temperatures above 140 K. Detachment of ASW from the substrate followed by its transformation to the water vapor were concluded from an instantaneous jump in delay towards zero and significant change observed in the THz spectra upon the thermal cycling processes.

articleTitle: Parameters Determination and Modeling of Commercial Multi-anodes GaAs Schottky Diodes for Low-cost Terahertz Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Planar Schottky diodes play important roles in THz mixers and multipliers. Accurate parameters extraction and modeling of the diodes have decisive effect in the optimization of these components. In present research, parameters extractions are mostly limited to single-anode or specially-designed diodes. Models for multi-anodes diodes have been investigated using parameters data from diodes manufacturers, which are not always available. Parameter extraction and modeling for unknown commercial multi-anodes diodes remain to be studied. In this paper, the methods for parameters extraction are successfully extended to a commercial four-anodes THz GaAs Schottky diode. Five critical intrinsic parameters and the parasitic parameters up to 220 GHz are investigated. A comprehensive model of the diode is developed. Its accuracy is verified by the good agreement between the simulative and measured S parameters. Our methods provide approaches for systematic studying unknown commercial multi-anodes Schottky diodes.

articleTitle: Characterization Measurements of Sapphire and Diamond based KIDs for Polarimetric Plasma Diagnostics
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this work we present the study and characterization measurements of Kinetic Inductance Detectors prototypes based on NbN thin films on diamond and sapphire substrates. The detectors are polarization sensitive, have multi-pixel design and are meant to be employed as the detecting element in a polarimetric fusion plasma diagnostic system operating at a probing frequency of 1.3 THz.

articleTitle: Infrared correlation nanoscopy with unprecedented spectral coverage
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We introduce a new tunable laser source optimized for IR nanoscopy applications which covers a spectral range of $218 \mu \mathrm{m}$. We demonstrate correlative scattering-type near-field (s-SNOM) and photothermal expansion-based point spectroscopy and imaging. As example system, we study the local chemical composition and the related phase separation in a thin film polymer blend sample, and map IR phonon polaritons in the lower Reststrahlenband in hBN in real space.

articleTitle: Terahertz Frequency Comb Toolbox for Molecular Sensing
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present a toolbox to shape the spectral content of terahertz (THz) frequency combs almost arbitrary. Our method merges the well-established technologies of electro-optic (EO) frequency comb generation in the near-infrared and difference frequency conversion (photomixing) to the THz range. The utilization of multiple EO modulators opens a huge parametric space for the comb spectral design and the fiber integration of the optical system provides robust operation and straight-forward handling.

articleTitle: Investigation of Terahertz Spectra of Electrically Driven Two-Dimensional Plasmons in Grating-Gated AlGaN/GaN Heterostructures
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Terahertz (THz) spectra of electrically driven two-dimensional (2D) plasmons in grating-gated AlGaN/GaN high-electron mobility transistor (HEMT) structure were investigated in emission and transmission geometry at the temperature of 80 K. The 2D plasmon resonances were observed in the frequency range of 1-3 THz. The resonance position and intensity were found to be related to the grating period and the bias voltage applied to the transistor terminals.

articleTitle: Generation of Circularly Polarized Continuous Terahertz Waves Using 650-nm Chaotic Multimode Semiconductor Laser
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We developed a terahertz time-domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS) system with a chaotic continuous wave (CW) light source based on a 650-nm multimode laser diode. We consequently demonstrated that the photoexcitation of a spiral photoconductive antenna by the 650-nm chaotic laser generates CW THz radiation with comb-like sub-THz frequency spectrum, which has very narrow-spaced modes at 0.025-THz intervals. Further investigation confirmed that the CW THz signal is circularly polarized. With this work, we present the feasibility of an economical laser-based measurement system with resolution and features that are highly favorable for evaluating 5G and 6G components as well as for other various applications.

articleTitle: Paint layer delamination mapping before and after consolidation of a 15th century painting using THz-TDI
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this project, a 15th century painting was analyzed using terahertz (THz) time-domain imaging (TDI). THz data was obtained before and after a consolidation intervention to repair delamination on the artwork. An algorithm was developed and applied to the data to detect and map areas where delamination was present on the painting.

articleTitle: Tunable zerogap technologies for terahertz wave manipulations
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We introduce technologies that vary the metallic gap widths in real time and on wafer scale, from subnanometers to several tens of nanometers, for the purpose of manipulating terahertz and microwave propagation with an extinction better than 10,000. Plastic substrates are used and the sample remains robust even after 10,000 bending repetitions.

articleTitle: Selective excitation of LO3 phonon mode of SrTiO3
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A Raman inactive LO3 phonon mode of Strontium Titanate (SrTiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>) has been successfully excited through mode-selective phonon excitation (MSPE) method using a mid-infrared free electron laser (MIR-FEL) at Kyoto University. Hyper-Raman scattering (HRS) spectroscopy was employed to observe and confirm the selective excitation of this target Raman forbidden mode. As preliminary experiments, anti-Stokes HRS of LO3 phonon mode was carried out without FEL irradiation at room temperature and at 5 K. Additionally, by observing the sum frequency generation (SFG) from ZnS Cleartran<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup>, the synchronization of the MIR-FEL and ps-laser pulses was achieved. Finally, selective excitation of the target LO3 phonon mode was demonstrated through anti-Stokes HRS spectroscopy at 5 K. A red shifted phenomenon was recognized since the selectively excited LO3 phonon appeared at 770 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> instead of around 800 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>.

articleTitle: Wideband Molecular Spectroscopy around 250 GHz and 500 GHz with SiGe BiCMOS Transmitters and Receivers
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The millimeter-wave/terahertz frequency range is interesting for a variety of fields. For many applications, a large bandwidth and different frequency bands are required to cover many strong transitions from different molecules. We present results of spectroscopy with a compact transmitter and receiver in SiGe BiCMOS technology covering two frequency bands. Both transmitter and receiver have cross-polarized bowtie-antennas for the two frequency bands. They cover the ranges 222 GHz – 270 GHz and 444 GHz – 540 GHz and can be operated simultaneously. We characterized the transmitter and receiver in laboratory experiments and performed gas spectroscopy with methanol.

articleTitle: Pharmaceutical Cocrystal of Ethenzamide with Gallic Acid: Structural Investigation Based on Terahertz Spectroscopy and DFT Calculation
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The pharmaceutical cocrystal of ethenzamide (ETZ) with gallic acid (GA) was synthesized by the solvent evaporation method. Terahertz (THz) spectroscopy and density functional theory (DFT) were used to explore cocrystal molecular structures and vibrational mode attribution. The THz spectrum showed distinctly different characteristic peaks between the cocrystal and its original components, indicating the formation of the cocrystal. Furthermore, simulations showed that the ETZ-GA cocrystal forms O-H$\cdots$O hydrogen bonds and interacts through the -OH in the GA and oxygen of amide group in the ETZ molecule.

articleTitle: Terahertz wave generation from crossing air-plasmas
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Air-plasma is a convenient method to generate intense terahertz (THz) waves by focusing the dual-color laser pulse on air molecules. Generally, the plasma property is associating to the intensity and frequency of the generated THz waves. Here, we demonstrated the varying intensity of THz wave generation from two crossing-beams of the dual-color laser-induced air-plasmas. When the two crossing beams overlap spatially and temporally, the structure and luminance of the combined plasmas changed greatly.
