In addition, the generated THz waves is not a simple coherent superposition of the two terahertz waves, but the spatial emission property and the maximum output angle is redistributed and redirected. Our results can help to gain more insight on the mechanism of THz wave generation from air-plasma, and offer a new possible modulation method for THz wave generation via controlling the spatial structure and complex dynamics inside the air-plasmas.

articleTitle: Contactless Cost-effective Polarizer for mm-Wave Dielectric Rod Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present a method to control the polarization of guided waves in a mm-wave dielectric rod waveguide. A pair of optical posts is situated on either side of the waveguide, and this markedly raises the cutoff of the undesired mode. The isolation is 20 dB over a frequency span from (55-87) GHz. This can be viewed as a proof-of-concept for reconfigurable, general-purpose polarization control and dispersion engineering in mm-wave and terahertz-range dielectric waveguides.

articleTitle: IEEE 802.11ad Packet Transmission Based on Radio-over-Fiber Technology with Optical SSB modulation in D-band
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This report demonstrates IEEE 802.11ad standard packet transmission in the D-band using a radio-over-fiber technology with an optical single sideband modulation.

articleTitle: Femtosecond Ablation Dynamics Observed with Terahertz Radiation
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Pulse-to-pulse time-domain waveforms of terahertz radiation emitted during laser ablation process were observed using a highly sensitive single-shot terahertz spectrometer using an echelon mirror. We observed the terahertz radiation with the peak electric field strength of 10 V/cm and found that the amplitude and the carrier-envelope phase (CEP) of the emitted terahertz pulses vary with increasing the excitation fluence. Because the changes of the waveforms are observed in the fluence range around the ablation threshold, we conclude that the terahertz radiation reflects the emission dynamics of electrons and ions from the surface. The results suggest that terahertz radiation is an important diagnostic to monitor the initial process of laser ablation.

articleTitle: THz Spectroscopic Characterization of Oil Shales, IRMMW-THz 2022
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Grey to dark-grey samples reported to be oil shales have been analyzed under the THz reflection and transmission spectroscopy. In order to examine the organic and mineral stratification of the oil shales, samples at varying height above the ground level were excavated from stream banks and hilly terrains. The constituent of these aquatic and terrestrial-based oil shales were further correlated to investigate any correspondence or dissimilarities in their composition by examining the refractive index, absorption and optical path length maps of the samples.

articleTitle: Sensitivity and Noise in THz Photoconductive Metasurface Detectors
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Photoconductive antenna THz detectors based on highly absorbing LT-GaAs metasurfaces enable high sensitivity and high signal-to-noise ratio (> 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup>) at optical gate powers as low as 5 $\mu$W. By investigating the dependence of detector performance on optical gate power, we compare several metasurface detectors with standard PCAs and develop a general model for quantifying the sensitivity and optimal gate power for detector operation. We also show that the LT-GaAs metasurface can even enhance sub bandgap absorption, enabling the use of these detectors in telecom wavelength systems.

articleTitle: Terahertz Optical Filtering with Large Area All-Metal and Polymer-Metal Meshes
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Industrial-grade, large area woven wire meshes are investigated using terahertz (THz) time-domain spectroscopy. The experimental results show that the THz optical properties of the bended wire structure of an all-metal mesh are dominated by a surface plasmon resonance, and the polymer-metal mesh acts as an efficient THz linear polarizer with a high polarization extinction ratio.

articleTitle: Terahertz Signature of Magnetoelectric Coupling in Multiferroic Polycrystalline Co4Nb2O9
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Here, we have unraveled the spin-wave excitations in polycrystalline Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>Nb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</inf> (CNO) using terahertz time-domain spectroscopy in the presence and absence of magnetic field. Two resonant modes were observed below Neel’s temperature (T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N</inf>) at 1.7 K. The detailed investigation of these resonant modes was carried out in presence of various magnetic fields. In addition to these zero field-induced modes, two additional magnetic field-induced modes were observed. The optical evidence of the field controlled magnetic excitations along with negative magnetodielectric constant indicates towards the signature of unique magneto-electric coupling in CNO.

articleTitle: Terahertz phase shifter based the fin-line loaded with microstructures nested with VO2
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This paper presents a structure of terahertz phase shifter based the fin-line loaded with microstructures nested with VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. In this structure, the fin-line is used to transmit terahertz waves, and four phase-shifting units nested with VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> are designed on the back of the substrate. With the phase transition characteristic of VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> changed by the pump laser, the on-off state of four phase-shifting units can be well controlled. Finally, within 335GHz-345GHz, the losses of phase-shifting units are less than 2dB, a phase shift of 171.6° can be achieved at 340 GHz, and each phase-shifting unit has a nearly 45° phase shift.

articleTitle: Telecentric f-theta scanning lens design for terahertz imaging systems
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Beam scanning system using f-theta lenses which are telecentric in the image space offers a linear beam displacement with the incident beam deflection angle and a focused beam has a normal incidence angle on the target plane. Therefore, the beam from the source reflects and travels back through the system to the source. The reflection coefficient (S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>) measurement can lead to the inspection of the target plane reflectivity. In this work, a telecentric f-theta lens is designed using ray tracing optimization and later, to verify ray tracing results, physical-optics simulations are performed on the system at 500 GHz. The designed lens has a thickness of 37 mm and shows acceptable f-theta distortion (0.5% for deflection angle of 10° with 22mm beam displacement) and telecentricity.

articleTitle: CCAT-prime Heterodyne Instrument (CHAI) advances
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The CCAT-p Heterodyne Array Instrument (CHAI) is being developed at the I. Physikalisches Institut of the Universität zu Köln. Here we present the proposed architecture of the receiver and the advances made in testing its basic components.

articleTitle: Anisotropic Terahertz Spectroscopy of Single-Crystalline L-Alanine
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The anisotropy of terahertz modes in the amino acid L-alanine have been investigated, revealing the underlying change in dipole moments along principal crystallographic axes. The highly collimated terahertz radiation of the Australian Synchrotron has been polarised with a linear stretch polyethylene polariser and passed though large single crystals cooled to 6.5K to achieve this result. In addition to defining the axis of the dipole moment of the modes, their relative strength has also been compared by rotating the polariser through 90°, transitioning the modes between principal axes.

articleTitle: Can deep models benefit from standard preprocessing of pulsed thermography data?
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: As deep learning-based algorithms keep leading the data segmentation tasks, many efforts are being conducted for their applications in the processing of pulsed thermography sequences. Conventional data preprocessing methods, such as pulsed phase transformation and principal component analysis are still popular in the community as data enhancement methods to improve contrasts and signal-noise ratio in infrared images. In this contribution, the impact of applying two conventional preprocessing methods for pulsed thermography data on the performance and learning computational time of deep learning methods is evaluated. The presented deep learning methods are based on the Encoder-Decoder architectural form, specifically a U-Net and a SegNet. The results show that by applying the conventional transform, the training time for deep learning methods can be significantly reduced. Compared to the results on the original infrared data, the performance on the preprocessed data is kept relatively high, as demonstrated on polyvinyl chloride specimens.

articleTitle: Carrier dynamics in InSe and the impact of terahertz pulses
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We investigate the electron-hole dynamics in few-layer InSe, a van der Waals semiconductor with promising opt-electronic properties. We show that terahertz pulses modulate the spontaneous emission via absorption by photo-excited carriers. We further study the carrier-phonon interaction in the cooling process of the hot carriers, elucidating the roles of acoustic and optical phonons.

articleTitle: Characterization of bound and free water in gelatin hydrogels and their contribution to THz frequency permittivity
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present reflective THz spectroscopic measurements of gelatin hydrogels with different gelatin bases combined with differential scanning calorimetry to quantify the bound water mass fraction of each sample. Samples were synthesized as either planar, optically thick slabs, or thin films lying atop optically thick water volumes. The analysis shows that the THz permittivity of water bound to gelatin molecules and the total bound water mass fraction vary significantly depending on the gelatin base used, the total water mass, and environmental conditions. These results support thorough characterization bound water in gelatin hydrogel phantoms prior to their us as a calibration target.

articleTitle: Polarized Terahertz Wave Resonance Enhanced Transmission of One-dimension Steel Wire Grid
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Terahertz resonance enhanced transmission of one-dimension steel wire grid was experimentally measured using terahertz time-domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS) and simulated with CST Microwave Studio. The results show that the amplitude of multiple peaks in the time-domain waveform and the resonance enhanced transmission is mainly determined by the polarization direction of incident terahertz wave. The multiple resonance transmission frequency is consistent with Fabry-Perot-like cavity resonance. The experimental results are helpful to on-line steel wire grid detection and terahertz imaging.

articleTitle: Ultrafast Terahertz Photocurrents in Semi-metal and semiconductor few monolayer PtSe2
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: PtSe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> is a promising 2D material for the THz range as its bandgap that can be tuned from an indirect semiconductor to a semimetal with the number of atomic layers, unlike other transition metal dichalcogenides. Here we use Terahertz (THz) emission time domain spectroscopy (TDS) to investigate PtSe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> as a function of number of 2D layers. We demonstrate the THz emission from this material for the first time and show that this is a result of second order nonlinear photocurrents in PtSe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, with contributions from photon drag and photogalvanic effects. We also show how the PtSe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> bandstructure dependence on the number of 2D layers radically changes its THz emission properties, rendering PtSe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> a promising material for THz photonics.

articleTitle: A Study of the Usability of Monolithically Integrated Photonic Oscillators for Wireless Millimeter Wave and Terahertz Communication
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this paper, we present a wireless link at 50 GHz, which is driven by two free-running monolithically integrated mode-locked laser diodes (MLLD). The experimental data is validated by a model which is based on two first order auto regressive processes. The modeled power spectrum as well as the probability density function fit very well to the measured data. This allows an assessment of the limitations of the system for future data transmission.

articleTitle: Dual-band Terahertz Complex Amplitude Modulation by Polarization Control via HEMT-Switch 1-bit Coding Microstructure
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: An electronic dual-band and dual-polarization terahertz 1-bit complex amplitude modulation by a resonant shifting of OOK (on-off-keying) on coplanar HEMT (High Electron Mobility Transistor) array is presented. The effects of the dispersion characteristics of different two-dimensional electron gas concentrations on both phase shift and amplitude characteristics are studied. Under a low switching ratio, a 180° reflection phase shift and an average amplitude of -7.5 dB are achieved in the low-frequency band from 0.268 to 0.313 terahertz by modulation in the x-polarization direction, and a 180° reflected phase shift and an average amplitude of -10 dB are achieved in the high-frequency band from 0.420 to 0.433 terahertz by modulation in the y-polarization direction. Considering the current state of the art, the proposed hybrid microstructure is capable of reprogrammable complex amplitude modulation, which provides insight into the realization of full-duplex for high-speed terahertz communications and the reduction of crosstalk between channels to increase the capacity of communication systems.

articleTitle: Influence of Channel Impulse Response Characteristics on Wireless THz-Communications
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: For the analysis of communication systems and channel modeling, it is important to understand, extract and generalize as many properties of the system under test as possible. The channel impulse response can serve as an input for a wide range of investigations and is therefore an important source of information. Knowing the characteristics and behavior of channel impulse responses of THz-systems with its high frequencies and large bandwidths would allow for a focused research based on the most important influence factors. In this paper, a correlation analysis between a variety of metrics based on channel impulse responses from a data center use case and their transmission performance has been conducted in order to identify causal relationships. In this investigation, it could be shown that the symbol duration has an influence on the correlation. A correlation between bit error rate and the amplitudes of key multi-path component as well as the delay spread exists. The consequences of these (partly weak) correlations for applications are still to be established.

articleTitle: Photonic Assisted Beam Steering Enabled by Hybrid Integration of InP-based Antenna Array and Polymer-based Optical Phased Array
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Beam steering is advantageous for continuous-wave terahertz applications in sensing, imaging, and wireless communication. While wide spread in lower frequency bands, in the terahertz region complex emitter and receiver structures are hardly feasible with discrete devices, due to the shorter wavelengths. Therefore, we propose and demonstrate the use of photonic integration: A 1x4 antenna array based on photodiodes is driven by an optical phased array based on polymer. The packaged emitter features increased directivity and enables beam steering across 30 °.

articleTitle: Probing Tl sublattice dynamics in ultralow thermal conductivity TlInTe2
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We investigated the lattice dynamics of TlInTe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> using THz time-domain spectroscopy as a function of temperature across the normal-incommensurate-commensurate transition. Our results indicate electric field screening of the LO mode on cooling and increased phonon anharmonicity in the commensurate phase. Moreover, despite the evidence of diminishing spectral weight of rattling Tl atoms, our measurements directly confirm the rigidity of the underlying InTe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> sublattice. Our data support the scenario proposed for the superionic conductors, where despite the loss of spectral weight of mobile ions, the host lattice remains intact and can transport heat even in the superionic phase.

articleTitle: Rapid s- & p- polarised THz spectroscopy for in-vivo measurements using a handheld scanner
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A compact and easy-to-use terahertz spectrometer is proposed to realize in-situ and fast measurement of both the s- and p- polarizations. A multi-pixel emitter is integrated into a handheld fiber-based terahertz scanner working in a reflection configuration. This self-referenced and mechanical rotation-free ellipsometer will significantly speed up the measurement process and has great potential for use in vivo skin measurements.

articleTitle: A Broadband Meta-Surface Output Window for 220GHz Gyrotron Traveling Wave Tubes
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: To increase the bandwidth of the output window of a mode gyrotron traveling wave tube(gyro-TWT), a meta-surface window is proposed. Compared with traditional multilayer windows, the equivalent permittivity of the matching layer can be changed by adjusting the radius, thickness and spacing of the matching layer cylinders to achieve better matching and thus a wider bandwidth. Through electromagnetic simulation software simulation, the results show that the output window of beryllium oxide meta-surface is lower than -20 dB in the range of 201-288.3 GHz, and the relative bandwidth is 39.68%. The influence of machining error on performance is analyzed.

articleTitle: Dual-plane Terahertz Hologram with Diffractive Optical Elements
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A dual-plane terahertz hologram based on diffractive optical elements is presented. A 2D dielectric array THz hologram with elements comprised of various heights is designed by applying a nonlinear optimization method. The designed hologram masks are fabricated using 3D printing technology. Full-wave FDTD simulations and experimental results demonstrate that the designed hologram can achieve dual-plane imaging, which has the potential to be used in displays and data storage.

articleTitle: Determination of the Vortex Mass in YBaCuO Based on Far-Infrared Magnetic Circular Dichroism
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We demonstrate an experimental method of determining the mass of Abrikosov vortices in a superconductor. For a nearly optimally doped thin $\mathrm{YBa}_2\mathrm{Cu}_3\mathrm{O}_{7-\delta}$ film, we found the value of a diagonal mass amounting to $2.2\times 10^{8}$ electron masses per centimeter $(\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{e}}/\mathrm{cm})$ at $45\mathrm{~K}$ and in the zero-frequency limit, and an even larger off-diagonal mass of $4.9\times 10^{8}\mathrm{~m}_{\mathrm{e}}/\mathrm{cm}$.

articleTitle: Review on CTS Antenna Arrays for Millimeter Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this paper, three state-of-the-art compact parallel-fed continuous transverse stub (CTS) arrays are presented. They operate at various frequency bands ranging from K-band to E-band. Antennas features such as the bandwidth, side-lobe level, and scanning capability are reviewed. Different fabrication technologies are adopted to implement the presented antenna concept such as milling, low-temperature co-fired ceramic (LTCC) and printed circuit board (PCB) technology.

articleTitle: Split-ring resonators imaged by THz s-SNOM
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Split-ring resonators (SRRs) are one of the most common building blocks to design metamaterials operating over a large range of frequencies in the electromagnetic spectrum. Here we acquire s-SNOM images with high signal-to-noise ratio on SRRs by scattering-type scanning near-field optical microscopy (s-SNOM) in the terahertz (THz) domain. By mapping the electric field distribution with subwavelength spatial resolution, we observe clear spatial asymmetries within a single SRR. These effects are more pronounced for the SRRs designed to resonate at the frequency of the probing laser (2.52 THz), compared to the SRRs that do not support a resonant mode at this frequency. This asymmetrical distribution is attributed to combined far-field and near-field multiplication effects, which depend on the position of the probing tip on the micro-resonator.

articleTitle: Design of a low-loss hybrid silicon-organic terahertz field detector
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We propose an innovative design for an integrated, low-loss on-chip terahertz (THz) field detector based on hybrid silicon-organic slot waveguides and THz antennas. We perform a numerical study of the dependency of electro-optic interaction on geometrical parameters to maximize the detector sensitivity. We benchmark it against previously employed plasmonic waveguides which were contended with high plasmonic losses. Our configuration leads to a reduction in the propagation losses of the probe signal by a factor of 5.64, ultimately enabling longer interaction lengths.

articleTitle: Characterization of Multi-Frequency Emission of Far-Infrared Laser with Josephson Junctions in a THz Microscope
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Terahertz (THz) gas lasers produce high output powers and can emit radiation at several lines with different lasing mediums. Often emission of multiple frequencies occurs with one lasing medium, which cannot be spectroscopically resolved with a thermal sensor. Our THz microscope employs a Josephson cantilever as a sensor, which relies on the Josephson effect. Thus, the sensor can record the incident spectrum. Additionally, the sensor can be moved during measurements. Hence, our setup enables the spectroscopic and spatial evaluation of multi-frequency far-infrared laser emission in one measurement. In this work, we present measurements of multiple laser lines, which are simultaneously recorded at frequencies between 1 THz and 1.4 THz.

articleTitle: Real-time subcarrier FMCW radar in the terahertz range based on a resonant-tunneling-diode oscillator: evaluation and demonstration
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We previously reported on real-time distance measurement in the terahertz range using a resonant-tunneling-diode (RTD) oscillator based on the frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW) radar principle. In this new report, we show a significant reduction of the measurement error on fast moving targets achieved by synchronizing subsystems. We also demonstrate the radar in a one-dimensional scanning experiment that produces the two-dimensional image of a field with several targets.

articleTitle: 3D-Printed Metallic Helix Antennas for Orientation Insensitive Polarization-division Multiplexing at Terahertz Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The improvements in 3D-printing increasingly enable their use for Terahertz components. Here we present helical antennas integrated with WR3 rectangular waveguides produced by a 3D metal printer. The constrains in resolution forces the design to deviate from the ideal dimensions for gain, but the flexibility of the production technique allows for the integration of reflector dishes directly on the waveguide, which mitigates these effects. Despite the deviation from traditional helical antenna design rules, the circular polarization is maintained. Hence, this fabrication method delivers orientation insensitive antennas for polarization-division multiplexing.

articleTitle: Dielectric response characterization of in vivo skin areas using a handheld THZ probe
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this work we demonstrate the development and testing of a robust handheld system able to characterize the dielectric properties of in vivo skin on different part of the body, cheeks, temple, forehead, upper arms and volar forearms. This system demonstrates to be robust against misalignments while keeping an acceptable weight comfortable for the operator. This portable system has potential for the diagnosis of dry skin or skin cancer in hospitals, being a valuable tool to complement current methods of diagnosis and detection.

articleTitle: Real-time terahertz imaging system with a HCN laser
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Terahertz (THz) radiation is set to play a key role in a wide range of imaging applications, from security check to medical diagnosis. We demonstrate a real-time terahertz imaging system based on a continuous wave (CW) discharge-pumped hydrogen cyanide (HCN) laser operating at 0.89 THz (337 $\mu$m) with power up to tens of milliwatts. In this work we present the acquisition of a THz-video $(32 \times 32$ pixels at 20 frames-per-second), shown in real-time, using a THz detector operating at room temperature. The results of the experiments reveal that this THz imaging system has the potential to be used for real-time mail inspection and non-destructive inspection.

articleTitle: Doping Study of Terahertz Quantum Cascade Lasers
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The influence of silicon donors on GaAs-based terahertz quantum cascade lasers is theoretically investigated by using a rate equation simulation. Based on a two-well resonant-phonon device structure, seven doping patterns, determined by dopants’ position and distribution, are simulated with 1.0×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup> to 1.0×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup> of sheet doping density at 200K heat-sink temperature. An undoped condition is also examined. Among the doped conditions, even though optical gain is substantial when phonon-wells are homogeneously doped, the maximum gain for the undoped condition is almost three times higher. From these simulation results, a novel doping scheme is proposed to improve device performance.

articleTitle: Millimeter Waves Alter the Genomic Architecture and Transcriptome of Primary Human Fibroblasts
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The current understanding of the biological effects of millimeter waves (MMWs) remains incomplete, and the interaction mechanisms causing these effects are largely unknown. We found that exposure of primary human fibroblasts to MMWs results in modified DNA secondary structure formation, altering the transcriptome and enriching many biological pathways without inducing DNA damage. This establishes the potential for therapeutic application of MMWs to induce targeted modifications to genomic architecture for the purpose of controlling gene expression and specific pathways.

articleTitle: Comparison of Interferometric and Electronic Phase Detection for TDS Systems
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Terahertz time-domain spectroscopy requires a precise knowledge of the phase difference between two pulse trains in order to obtain high-quality terahertz spectra. In terahertz time-domain spectroscopy with systems based on repetition-rate modulation, the phase difference is commonly measured electronically utilizing a detection of the pulse trains’ higher-harmonics’ difference signal via fast photodiodes in combination with a frequency mixer. However, the electronic phase detectors used to conduct these measurements are prone to exhibit both a non-negligible timing jitter and a systematic error. Here, we present the results of our recent attempt to reduce these errors in our own electronic phase detection systems. A more than six-fold timing-jitter reduction from 59.0 fs to 8.6 fs led to a significant increase in both exploitable terahertz bandwidth and signal-to-noise ratio. Additionally, utilizing our interferometrically monitored delay line as a calibration standard, the systematic error could be removed almost entirely and thus, excellent resolution of spectral absorption lines be accomplished.

articleTitle: Study of thermal crosstalk in Avalanche Photodetectors in THz domain
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The Si-Ge avalanche photodetectors coupled with a thin multiplication region can be used for a CMOS compatible high speed optical receiver designs as it has a lower dark current and needs a lower operational voltage. However, the thermal conductance of the chip materials results in thermal crosstalk that significantly degrades the photodetector performance in terms of the Figure of merit parameters like dark current, photocurrent, data transmission, etc. In this work, we illustrate through simulations the deep trench chip design to mitigate the thermal crosstalk effect and therefore improve the photodetector performance in terms of dark current and photocurrent.

articleTitle: 2-bit Terahertz Digitally Coding Metasurface Based on HEMT Switching Microstructure
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this paper, we propose the design of a 2-bit digitally coding metasurface that can efficiently modulate scattered electromagnetic waves and realize different far-field beams. By integrating two independently varying high electron mobility transistors (HEMT) into the metamaterial unit, the metasurface has four phase responses of 0, π/2, π, and 3π/2, corresponding to the four fundamental digital elements “00”, “01”, “10” and “11”. By designing the coding sequence of different arrays of digital elements, the reflected beam can be arbitrarily controlled. This work facilitates the implementation of 3D terahertz beam steering.

articleTitle: Comparison of biomaterials used in contact lenses based on water content analysis with terahertz spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The selection of biomaterials used for contact lens fabrication is crucial to increase the biocompatibility of contact lenses as a means to extend the wearing time and comfort. The assessment of in vitro dehydration of contact lenses made from different materials with terahertz (THz) time-domain spectroscopy and optical coherence tomography (OCT), provides a new index to assess their water content.

articleTitle: Terahertz nano-metamaterials for label-free detection and discrimination of cell
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Terahertz sensing application with metamaterials has been attractive candidate for various analytes. Biomolecule samples especially have been intensively researched with high sensitivity and selectivity using THz metamaterials. Here, we designed nano-gap based metamaterials for highly enhanced absorption cross section of target bio samples. Nano-slot sensing chip was applied to classify various kinds of cells and measure cell density sensitively. Large sized nano-slot sensing chip was fabricated to improve image contrast of brain tissue as well. The results show an excellent potential of highly sensitive label-free biological sample detection and imaging applications.

articleTitle: Topological Dirac semi-metals as novel, optically-switchable, helicity-dependent terahertz sources
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The generation and control of terahertz pulses is vital for realizing the potential of terahertz radiation in several sectors, including 6G communication, security and imaging. In this work, we present the topological Dirac semimetal cadmium arsenide as a novel helicity-dependent terahertz source. We show both broadband (single-cycle) and narrowband (multi-cycle) terahertz pulses upon near-infrared photoexcitation at oblique incidence. By varying the incident angle of the photoexcitation pulse, control of the emission frequency can also be achieved, providing a candidate for a tuneable narrowband terahertz source.

articleTitle: Gyrotron-Alignment Platform with Five Degrees of Freedom
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The proper placement of gyrotron relative to the magnetic field is necessary for optimal gyrotron performance. A gyrotron-alignment platform capable of independent, precise adjustment in five degrees of freedom has been developed. The effectiveness of this platform is experimentally demonstrated by alignment of a 198 GHz gyrotron used for Dynamic Nuclear Polarization.

articleTitle: Ultrafast switch-off of metamaterial polariton modes in a terahertz photonic crystal cavity
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We investigate the non-adiabatic switching dynamics of a bosonic ultrastrong coupling system consisting of a meta-material in a 1D photonic crystal, and report sub-cycle optical control of the coupling between the plasmons and the cavity photons. By switching-off the plasmon mode by a femtosecond laser pulse, we observe ultrafast changes of the coupled system which strongly depend on the arrival time of the laser pulse.

articleTitle: See-through Soil Measurements at 300 GHz
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Over time, terahertz waves (T-waves) have succeeded in gaining a foothold in various areas ranging from localization, imaging, communications, to characterization. Due to several unique properties and abilities of T-wave, groundbreaking applications in real-time continuous monitoring of plant growth and health are conceivable. Nevertheless, a motivation for developing THz medical-style non-invasive imaging systems to diagnose plant health demands prior knowledge of soil attenuation. This paper features preliminary results from seethrough soil experiments conducted with soils of different ages at 275-325 GHz employing a THz-VNA bistatic setup. Proceeding further, the measurements are recorded in three experiment scenarios to acknowledge the pivotal role of soil in maintaining the availability of water and nutrients to the aerial parts of a plant. For this purpose, the soil is moistened with 100, 200, 300, and 400 ml water to record the resulting impact on the plasticity of the soil. This study thus confers that T-wave can see-through soil samples possibly up to ~25 cm thick supported by THz-VNA – state-of-the-art technology.

articleTitle: Semiconducting Amorphous Y-Ba-Cu-O Thin Film Detectors: Fast Room Temperature Thermal Response Up to 40 MHz
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Semiconducting amorphous Y-Ba-Cu-O film based uncooled sensors revealed high performances in the near infrared domain, when submitted to fast incident power variations. These variations led to optical absorption, which, combined with the pyroelectric properties of the film material, induced pyroelectric currents, which were measured in detail up to 40 MHz. Noise equivalent power levels as low as $4.3\times 10^{-10}$W/H$\mathrm{z}^{1/2}$ and detectivity values larger than 1$0^{7}cm\cdot H\mathrm{z}^{1/2}$/W were extracted at 10 MHz modulation frequency, thus paving the way to significant improvements for fast infrared imaging applications.

articleTitle: FM to AM Transition of RF Driven THz QCL fundamental and Harmonic Comb States
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We measure temporal intensity profile by means of Shifted Wave Interference Fourier Transform Spectroscopy of strong RF injected heterogeneous THz QCLs showing a strong AM emission with pulses as short as 6 ps. Additionally, we measure with SWIFTS fundamental as well as harmonic comb states under RF injection which exhibit clear FM emission and its transition to AM as a function of the RF power.

articleTitle: Absorption Properties of Calcium Oxalate in the Far-Infrared Region for Phase Identification in Kidney Stones
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Calcium oxalate is the main constituent of kidney stones, and it exists either in monohydrate or dihydrate form. Herein calcium oxalate dihydrate was investigated by Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy in the far-infrared region. The results reveal a characteristic absorption band around 8.5 THz. This finding could be useful in the phase identification of kidney stones which is valuable in understanding the stone formation mechanism.

articleTitle: Design of a 140GHz quadrature subharmonic mixer based on Schottky diode
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In the context of increasingly tight spectrum resources, mixer, as an indispensable part of communication system, its research is of great significance to the promotion of communication technology. In this paper, the 3D electromagnetic simulation software HFSS and ADS software are combined. Based on the S parameters of 3D model based on HFSS contained in SNP file, ADS is used to represent the transmission characteristics of the circuit, and a subharmonic mixer based on Schottky diode is designed by partial simulation method. The design of quadrature subharmonic mixer is completed by combining subharmonic mixer with power divider. The results show that the conversion loss of the mixer in 130-150 GHZ band is less than 7.23dB.

articleTitle: Improving the Efficiency of LT-GaAs Photoconductive Arrays on Optically Transparent Substrates for High Field THz Generation
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: An improved electrode geometry is developed for LT-GaAs photoconductive antenna arrays fabricated on transparent sapphire substrates to generate high field THz radiation. These improved geometries target more efficient field generation through supporting high biases, higher filling factors and supporting higher transient photocurrents. Each modification to electrode design is characterised for its effect on THz field generation.

articleTitle: Terahertz responsivity of AlGaN/GaN bow-tie diode detectors at the temperatures of 295 K and 80 K
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: terahertz (THz) responsivity of the planar bow-tie (BT) diodes based on AlGaN/GaN high electron mobility transistor (HEMT) structures were investigated at the temperatures of 295 K and 80 K in the frequency range of 150-600 GHz. At 295 K, the zero-bias responsivity of the BT diode was found to be of about 72 mV/W. Biasing the detector by $\pm 1V$ allowed us to increase the responsivity by at least 50 times, while cooling the detectors down to 80 K demonstrated the increase by up to 20 times independently on the frequency of THz beam.

articleTitle: Integrated disk resonator on substrateless dielectric waveguide platform for terahertz switch applications
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present a terahertz single-pole double-throw (SPDT) switch based on an integrated disk resonator for a substrateless dielectric platform made of an all-silicon-based effective medium. The switch operates based on photoexcitation by using visible light focused onto the disk resonator to turn off the resonance, thus removing coupling between two waveguides. The result shows low insertion loss of the proposed switch due to the low dissipation of the platform. The device achieves an extinction ratio of 11 dB and 1.5 GHz of terahertz bandwidth. This terahertz switch can be employed in various terahertz applications including phase shifting and beam steering.

articleTitle: Validating a non-invasive diagnostic for sustained hyperglycemia in humans based on W-band spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)

authors.preferredName: María José De La Cruz Fernández

abstract: Diagnosis of sustained hyperglycemia is a critical factor in diabetes care. HbA1c is the current gold standard indicator assessing fluctuations in medium/long term glycemic state. In this work, W-band spectroscopy is tested for non-invasive monitoring of sustained glycemia by a preliminary validation diagnostic study, using HbA1c indicator as reference. W-band transmission profiles (amplitude) of 30 subjects were longitudinally observed over a period of 7 months. Collected spectral data is studied using supervised longitudinal functional data analysis methods. Results support that it is possible to predict HbA1c value by using W-band transmission profiles, with an excellent linear response (R-squared = 0.97).

articleTitle: Graphene TeraFETs - Effect of gated channel region on THz performance
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We investigate the dependence of the responsivity of antenna-coupled graphene field-effect transistors (graphene TeraFETs) on the transistor’s channel geometry. The graphene TeraFETs are fabricated using a wafer-scale CVD process, and the measurements of the detectors of various geometries are performed at 0.1-1.2 THz. The measured data are compared with existing theoretical predictions and help to improve the accuracy of graphene TeraFET responsivity models.

articleTitle: Compact Multi-Frequency Sub-THz Notch Filters with Rejection within and above the Pass Band
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Sensitive sub-THz diagnostic systems for magnetically confined fusion plasmas need protection from stray radiation produced by high-power Electron Cyclotron Resonance Heating (ECRH) systems which operate in one or more narrow-band frequency lines. These frequencies can be within and sometimes also above the frequency band of the diagnostic system. Notch filters are key components to provide this protection.

articleTitle: Measurement of Time Dependent Reflection, Transmission and Absorption in a Laser Driven Switch for 250 GHz Radiation
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We report experimental testing at 250 GHz of a laser-driven low loss silicon switch. The time-dependent reflection, transmission, and absorption of the wafer were measured and analyzed in both the nanosecond and microsecond time scales. The test results show that absorption plays a major role on both time scales. These results are important in analyzing the performance and output power of a 250 GHz quasi-optical ring resonator. The results should also help to improve the modeling of silicon switch performance on the nanosecond time scale.

articleTitle: High speed response of a Hot Electron Bolometer to a picosecond optical THz source and to a THz QCL comb up to 31GHz
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We have investigated the frequency response of a phonon-cooled Hot Electron Bolometer (HEB) made from an ultrathin superconducting niobium nitride film. We have used short optical pulses and a broadband spectrum analyzer to record the impulse response of the HEB. To interpret the experimental results, we have used numerical calculations based on the two temperature (2T) theoretical model.

articleTitle: Development of a CUSP-Type Electron Gun for a W-Band Helical Gyro-TWT
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: To drive a broadband gyro-TWT with a helically corrugated interaction region, a high-quality axis-encircling electron beam is required. In this publication, a CUSP-type electron gun, capable of generating such a beam, is developed for a 94 GHz helical gyro-TWT. The design was optimized using the electron-beam-optics code ESRAY [1]. The final electron gun is optimized for the generation of an electron beam with a 50 kV beam voltage, 1.5 A current, and a pitch factor of $\alpha=1.0$ with an RMS spread as low as 3.49 %. Additionally, tolerance studies, including the influence of deviations in the emitter position and the surface roughness of the emitter, are performed.

articleTitle: High Intensity Spintronic Terahertz Emitter with ITO and Microsheet Glass Structure
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We demonstrate that an indium tin oxide (ITO) film and microsheet glass layer can be used to increase the intensity of terahertz (THz) radiation from spintronic THz emitters (STEs). In this work, the backward-radiated THz waves of a Pt/Fe bilayer are reflected by an ITO film and subsequently phase-controlled by a microsheet glass to constructively superimpose with forward-radiated THz waves, thereby enhancing the THz emission.

articleTitle: High Doping Concentration and Variable Al Composition THz Quantum Cascade Lasers with 1.39-Watt Operation
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A 1.39 W peak power and 60 mW average power THz QCL is presented by variable Al composition active structure with high doping concentration based on NEGF method design, including the realignment of resonant tunneling and suppression of leakages via high energy confined levels. Re-aligning the resonant tunneling which can be serious degraded due to a band bending from this heavy local doping. With variable quantum well and barrier height, the design owns an improved parameter tuning freedoms, and a saturation of peak gain can be achieved at a relative high doping concentration.

articleTitle: 1030 nm optimized photoconductive receiver excited with >20 mW of THz average power
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present an ErAs:InAlGaAs photoconductive antenna receiver optimized for 1030 nm probe pulses, excited at very high THz average power (24 mW). We measure a dynamic range of 92 dB in a 10 s measurement time. The saturation behavior under high THz average power is studied as well.

articleTitle: Quantitative Gas Spectroscopy in the 220 to 330 GHz Frequency Band Utilizing a Microelectronic Spectrometer
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The development of electronic THz wave rotational absorption spectroscopy for quantitative gas sensing and its experimental validation is reported. The implementation of a THz wave spectrometer operating in the 220 to 330 GHz frequency band using state-of-the-art electronic THz wave radiation sources and detectors is described. The novel system technology for THz wave gas phase spectroscopy is validated by the detection of a broad range of relevant volatile organic compounds, nitrogen compounds, halogenated hydrocarbons, and commercial refrigerants. The sensitivity of the spectrometer meets gas species detection limits set by, e.g. occupational health and safety standards. The large bandwidth (220 to 330 GHz), high frequency resolution (0.5 MHz), and rapid frequency scanning (160 GHz/s) of the spectrometer enables the important analysis of gas mixtures.

articleTitle: Photonic THz near-field imaging: Characterizing high-frequency components from 100 GHz to 4 THz
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present photonic terahertz (THz) near-field, frequency resolved measurements of high-frequency THz emitters from 100 GHz to 4 THz. Up to 528 GHz, we are able to accurately model our measurements with the finite element method for high-frequencies. For higher frequencies, modelling becomes too time consuming, thus stressing importance of measurements. Around 2 THz, we identify unwanted reflections from the air / submount interface.

articleTitle: THz diffractive optics designed with neural networks
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Application of the neural networks to the design of optical elements for the THz spectral range allows to obtain unique, counterintuitive phase delay maps, which can redirect the incident radiation into arbitrarily chosen intensity patterns. In this work, the neural network optimization of three structures is presented – a converging lens, a three-focal-spot lens, and a hologram of a square. The structures have been manufactured using the 3D-printing technique and verified experimentally. Proper functioning of such diffractive elements and high compliance with the numerical simulations has been proved. Proposed diffractive elements can be applied to many areas, including wireless telecommunication or imaging.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Nano-RTD VCO Devices for On-Body THz Nano-Communication Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The constant miniaturization of devices and the insatiable demand for higher bandwidth are driving the development of ultra-compact THz systems. This work proposes a nano-RTD VCO operating at the THz region for on-body nano-communication systems. A semi-analytical tool for evaluating the performance of a transmitter based on the nano-RTD VCO considering different carrier-less modulations is developed. Results show that the device can operate in the H-band (220-325 GHz) while having ultra-low power consumption down to 160 nW at 0.11 Tb/s for reaches up to 25 mm. The device may enable a plethora of applications, including sensing, monitoring, and medical diagnosis.

articleTitle: Wax/PTFE Substrate Lens for Front-side Illumination of TeraFET Detectors
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A composite wax/PTFE lens integrated on the front-side of Si CMOS TeraFET detectors is demonstrated in order to optimize the coupling efficiency of the THz radiation. The wax/PTFE lens is fabricated by first dripping molten wax onto the detector to embed and protect the bonding wires, then pasting a custom-designed hemispherical PTFE lens onto this layer exploiting the adhesive character of the soft wax. The experimental results show a 10-dB injection efficiency enhancement compared with the case without the wax/PTFE lens, and a 20-dB dynamicrange increase in Fourier imaging.

articleTitle: The Performance of Suspended Superconducting NbN Hot Electron Bolometer with Buffer Layer
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We fabricated an antenna coupled NbN hot electron bolometer with vacuum bridge and Nb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf> N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf> buffer successfully and studied direct detection performance at 0.65 THz. This kind of suspended HEB with Nb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf> N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf> buffer can ensure a rather high sensitivity at a relative high environment temperature, which has potential applications in cost savings without disrupting noise performance.

articleTitle: Infrared photoluminescence and absorption of Ge/Si quantum dots with different doping levels
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The influence of Ge/Si quantum dot doping level on the infrared interband photoluminescence is experimentally studied for various temperatures and pumping levels. Indirect and direct in real space optical transitions are identified in the luminescence spectra. Effect of doping on equilibrium and photoinduced absorption spectra is also experimentally studied in mid-and far-infrared (terahertz) spectral ranges for different temperatures. The features in the absorption spectra are explained with the contribution of the optical hole transitions from the ground state to the excited states of quantum dots and to the extended states of the continuous spectrum.

articleTitle: Coupled dual-layer antenna for optimized 250 GHz silicon CMOS detector
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present a novel planar antenna consisting of two coupled slots and impedance transforming elements for the optimized 250 GHz field-effect-transistor-based detector. The device includes a monolithically integrated silicon MOSFET and the antenna structure fabricated using commercial 180nm Si CMOS technology. The employment of a double-layer antenna and a single-finger transistor lets us substantially improve device performance. The enhanced detector exhibits a minimum optical noise equivalent power as low as 15 pW/$\sqrt{Hz}$ at 250 GHz.

articleTitle: Terahertz Planar Goubau Line Components on Thin Suspended Silicon Substrate
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The planar Goubau line is a low-loss planar single-conductor waveguide that holds promise for terahertz applications, where power efficiency is crucial. We present three circuit elements for planar Goubau line: a stopband filter, a matching load, and a power divider, which have been fabricated in a high-resistivity silicon membrane. Simulation results are presented for the matching load and the power divider. The filter’s performance is validated by comparing measurement results with simulations, showing good agreement.

articleTitle: Terahertz Device Design Method Based on Swarm Intelligence Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Efficient design of terahertz devices that meet technical specifications is a prerequisite for building terahertz communication systems for high-capacity communications. The optimal design of conventional terahertz devices requires manual tuning, which makes the whole optimization process extremely difficult due to the complexity challenges such as the high-dimensional optimization space and the high non-linearity between the decision space and the objective space. To address a series of challenges, we propose a design approach that enables the tuning of terahertz devices through autonomous design utilizing artificial intelligence (AI) techniques, thereby reducing the difficulty of device tuning and improving design efficiency. To validate the effectiveness of the algorithm, we apply it to a microstrip waveguide probe transition structure in the terahertz band. The simulation results indicate that the probe structure designed with the algorithm has S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> below −20dB in the output frequency range of 291.6GHz ~ 368.6GHz, with a bandwidth of about 77GHz. in the output frequency range of 311.7GHz ~ 367.7GHz, S11 is below -30dB, with a bandwidth of about 56GHz. among them, S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> at 358GHz reaches −46.3dB, which exceeds the artificial design level and far exceeds the device design requirements.

articleTitle: European 1 MW, 170 GHz CW Gyrotron Prototype for ITER - long-pulse operation at KIT -
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The upgraded EU 1 MW, 170 GHz continuous wave (CW) industrial prototype gyrotron (TH1509U) for Electron Cyclotron Resonance Heating and Current Drive (ECRH&CD) in ITER was tested at the Karlsruhe Institute of Technology (KIT). The gyrotron surpassed the performance of the previous TH1509 tube. In particular, TH1509U delivered (i) 0.9 MW in 180 s pulses (max. pulse length of the KIT test stand) and (ii) more than 1 MW at a pulse length limited to 40 s, due to a problem with the test stand cooling circuit at that time. In addition, it was possible to demonstrate gyrotron operation at (iii) 0.5 MW in 1600 s pulses.

articleTitle: Fiber-coupled THz TDS system with mW-level THz power
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present a fully fiber-coupled THz TDS system with a record emitted THz power of 0.97 mW at 55 mW optical excitation power at the photoconductive emitter. The TDS system utilizes an erbium-doped fiber laser with separate amplifiers for both output arms in combination with rhodium-doped InGaAs-based THz antennas as emitter and receiver. For 1000 averages, a bandwidth of 6.5 THz and a peak dynamic range of 101 dB is achieved.

articleTitle: FDTD Analysis of Cylindrical Waveguides With Both Axial and Azimuthal Corrugations
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Cylindrical waveguides with both axial and azimuthal corrugations can be found in a variety of microwave devices, where they operate mainly as mode converters. In this work, we study the scattering parameters and the mode conversion in a structure consisting of two axial corrugations and an azimuthally corrugated section, by using the in-house FDTD code COCHLEA. General trends, with respect to the dependence of the mode conversion on the geometrical parameters, are obtained, focusing on the possibility to use the structure for improved mode suppression in gyrotron beam tunnels.

articleTitle: Characterization of QCL-Comb emission by Fourier Transform Analysis
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Quantum cascade lasers (QCLs) frequency comb (FC) synthesizers represents the new frontier of miniaturized metrological grade sources, ideal for quantum sensing, metrology, communications and simulations. At terahertz (THz) frequencies, electrically pumped QCLs have shown quantum-limited intrinsic linewidths and can be absolutely referenced to the primary frequency standard. Fourier-transform analysis of comb emission (FACE) enables to asses the level of coherence of any QCL-FC on its entire frequency emission range simultaneously with the possibility to reconstruct its intensity emission profile and instantaneous frequency. Here, we present the novelties in FACE characterization method, proving the metrological nature of a promising new generation of THz QCL-FC.

articleTitle: Silicon RFICs for 100-700 GHz Communication and Radar/Sensor Systems
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The talk will present the latest work at UCSD and at several other universities and research labs on affordable/low-cost silicon RFICs for 100-700 GHz communication and radar/sensor systems. Silicon technology will never result in as low NF as InP PHEMT, or as high transmit power as InP HBTs, but it does offer on-chip high-efficiency planar antennas coupled with low enough NF (5-10 dB) and reasonable radiated power (0.1-50 mW). Therefore, it allows for competitive phased-arrays and point-to-point communication systems at 100-200 GHz, and imaging and radar arrays up to 300 GHz and even 700 GHz. The talk will present state-of-the-art sub-THz and THz systems based on all-silicon platforms (SiGe and CMOS) and discusses the pros and cons of this technology.

articleTitle: High stability of optical beat in laser chaos for THz wave near the threshold level
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Stability of optical beats in a chaotically oscillating laser is confirmed near to laser threshold level using a highly efficient plasmonic photomixer. High stability of it is proofed. The great potential of chaotically oscillating lasers is verified for THz systems.

articleTitle: An investigation of water diffusion in polymers with terahertz time-domain spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Water plays an important role in the degradation of polymers. Diffusion across bulk polymers is commonly investigated by gravimetric and capacitive techniques. Here, the water diffusion in polycarbonate (PC) and poly(methyl methacrylate) (PMMA) is studied by terahertz time-domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS) and gravimetric measurements. Time-resolved measurements of the THz refractive index and absorption coefficients show a good agreement to the gravimetrics and allow the contact-free extraction of the diffusion coefficients.

articleTitle: The Effects of Surfaces and Surface Passivation on the Electrical Properties of Nanowires and Other Nanostructures: Time-Resolved Terahertz Spectroscopy Studies
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The electrical properties of nanomaterials are strongly influenced by their surfaces, which in turn are strongly influenced by device processing and passivation procedures. Optical pump–terahertz probe spectroscopy is ideal for measuring the native properties of these materials, determining the changes induced by device processing, and studying the effectiveness of surface passivation procedures. Here we study the electronic properties of III–V nanowires and other nanomaterials in both their native and encapsulated/integrated states, which is uniquely possible with terahertz spectroscopy.

articleTitle: High-Q Resonances based on quasi-Bound State in the Continuum in Metamaterial for THz Sensing
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A resonator with high Q factors for the terahertz region is proposed, which can excite bound state in the continuum by introducing perturbation to the metamaterial. The sensing performance of designed metamaterial show that the sensitivity and Figure of merit (FoM) can reach 528 GHz/RIU and 939, respectively.

articleTitle: Longitudinally Polarized Terahertz Radiation from Spintronic Emitters
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We report on the generation of a terahertz (THz) beam with a quasi-TEM01 mode by exploiting the interferometric recombination of two linearly polarized emitters in a combined spintronic source. A single-cycle longitudinally polarized field component is realized by tightly focusing the quasi-TEM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf> beam and the scaling of the electric field strength is explored.

articleTitle: Joint Optimization of Complex Amplitude Modulation on HEMT-Meta Array
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Aiming at the laboring issue on reconfigurable metasurfaces, this paper proposes an efficient Matlab-CST joint optimization process for terahertz beam steering on the HEMT-meta array. To improve the beam steering performance, the Matlab program automatically executes optimization process on CST parameter screening for the best reflectance and 1-bit coding phase shift. Furthermore, an automatic CST arraying applies on the HEMT-meta coding array by the Matlab program, which significantly reduces the time-consuming procedure for beam steering verification on the large-sized antenna array. The CST simulation and numerical calculation corroborate the feasibility of the joint optimization, proofing with bandwidth increment from 0.2% to 5.71%, reflection coefficient increment from 4% to 34.1%, and beam steering performance in the 0.3-0.4 THz range. The proposed method significantly improves beam steering metasurfaces’ design efficiency and performance.

articleTitle: Effect of a deformable mirror on THz wave production by laser-created air plasmas
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We numerically simulate THz pulse generation by air photoionization using 2-color laser pulses whose phase fronts are modified by a deformable mirror (DM). By introducing controlled aberrations at the medium entrance, we investigate manipulations of the spatial structure of the filaments generated in gas cell setups. We find that non-axisymmetric aberrations (astigmatism, coma) tend to decrease the generated THz energy. By contrast, spherical aberrations can significantly increase the THz yield. DM effects on THz conical emission and in long-range filamentation are addressed as well.

articleTitle: A Comparison of Continuous-Wave and Pulsed Free Space 2-Port Photonic Vector Network Analyzers for Terahertz Characterization
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Photonic Vector Network Analyzers (PVNA) provide a viable solution to the rising demand for efficient, accurate, and affordable characterization instruments for benchmarking terahertz devices and components. This paper compares continuous-wave and pulsed versions of the free space 2-port PVNA and their aptitudes for THz characterization using a distributed Bragg reflector as an application example.

articleTitle: Design Alternatives for a submm-wave Fabry-Perot Cavity Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This paper discusses different design alternatives for a high gain planar antenna at 240 GHz. The antenna is based on a Fabry-Perot configuration, where two different partial reflection surfaces (PRS) are considered: a free standing metallic plate and a metallized quartz substrate. Similar performance has been found between both alternatives.

articleTitle: A flexible and stretchable 3D-printed terahertz waveguide
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We propose a novel flexible and stretchable terahertz waveguide by 3D printing to guide radiation from terahertz (THz) quantum cascade lasers (QCLs) lasing at the frequency of 2.58 THz. Composite silver nanoparticles and polydimethylsiloxane are coated on the inner surface of the 3Dprinted polycarbonate/rubber substrate tube. The experimental results show that the transmission loss is ~0.22 dB/cm for the waveguide with a 4 mm-bore diameter. Both transmission spectra and output beam profile out from the waveguide demonstrate single-mode characteristics. Importantly, preeminent mechanical stability and stretchability of the 3D-printed terahertz waveguide are verified, which lead to broad applications in stretchable and ultra-flexible terahertz devices.

articleTitle: THz Microscopy of Light Modes Generated with Additive Manufactured Spiral Phase Plates
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Josephson cantilevers are versatile sensors that are used in a THz microscopy setup for the detection of the spectrum and power of microwave and terahertz field distributions. They can be moved three-dimensionally by a positioning system to enable spatial resolution. In this work, we investigate additive manufactured spiral phase plates for the generation of twisted terahertz beams. They are fabricated with a common 3D printer based on the fused filament fabrication process. The terahertz radiation is generated by an optically pumped molecular gas laser and the resulting field distributions are imaged with the THz microscope.

articleTitle: Electrical and noise properties of graphene gate fin-shaped GaN/AlGaN field effect transistors for high frequency electronics
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We report on the fabrication and study of graphene gate GaN/AlGaN fin-shaped field effect transistors. The investigated DC, noise, and sub-sub-THz properties indicate their prospective for transparent high-temperature GaN-based electronics. The dependence of graphene gate properties on the bias adds new functionality to these devices.

articleTitle: THz-Photoconductivity and THz-Conductivity in Metal-Organic Frameworks (MOFs)
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Metal-organic frameworks are a class of emerging materials, with novel, designable, and outstanding properties. Terahertz (THz) spectroscopy is a versatile technique to explore low-energy resonant modes in these materials, and conductivity and photoconductivity. Understanding mechanism and timescales of photoconductivity in metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) is crucial for their applicability in solar energy generation. The subps time resolution of optical pump-THz probe (OPTP) in combination with time-resolved THz spectroscopy (TRTS) provides an unmatched view into the life of a photoelectron within MOFs. In this talk, I will present our experiments studying conductivity and photoconductivity in two MOFs, namely di-Zn(II)-tetrathiafulvalene-tetrabenzoate (Zn<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>TTFTB) and di-Mn(II)-2,5-dimercaptoterephthalate (Mn<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>DSBDC).

articleTitle: Sub-THz Circular Dichroism using Wire Grid Polarizers
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This paper revises the methodology for enabling Circular Dichroism (CD) measurements without the need for rotating transmit or receive horns in a quasi-optical (QO) measurement setup. This is achieved by using a set of wire grid polarizers, obtaining the values of Jones matrices of the sample in order to reconstruct the co-polarized and cross-polarized transmissions through the sample under test (SUT) These transmission values can then be used to create a CD signature for a SUT possessing chiral properties.

articleTitle: 198 GHz Microwaves: From the Gyrotron Output Window to the Unpaired Electron Spins in the DNP NMR Sample
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Versatile instrumentation including a frequency-agile gyrotron as the microwave source, a Martin-Puplett interferometer to modify the microwave polarization, a Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR) spectrometer with cryogenic magic angle spinning, as well as an electron spin detection circuit is presented. The combination of these state-of-the-art technologies allows the recording of high-performance dynamic nuclear polarization spectra, a method used to enhance the sensitivity of NMR experiments via microwave irradiation.

articleTitle: Optical Mode Characterization Using a VNA Phase and Amplitude Measurement Scheme at 104 GHz
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We have developed a modal framework [1], which uses the notion of optical modes, i.e. an unique set of individually coherent orthogonal field distributions, to propagate an incident electric field through an optical system. The framework relies on a transmission matrix and Singular Value Decomposition (SVD), to obtained the mode characteristics: their transmission efficiencies and spatial forms over the input and output surface of the optical system. Here, we present a VNA phase and amplitude measurement scheme used for determining the transmission matrix, and we compare the obtained mode characteristics to our model for a pair of limiting slits at 104 GHz, which show good agreement.

articleTitle: Using Magnetic-Field-Controlled Ferrofluid as a THz Wave Emitter
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We characterize the THz wave emission from ferrofluid under fs-laser pulse excitation. The controllability of the radiation by an external magnetic field is demonstrated. In addition to the magnetic field, the ferrofluid concentration also impacts intrinsically the generated THz wave. The results are contrasted against other established sources with a similar excitation scheme to delineate ferrofluid’s THz radiator capacity.

articleTitle: A Meta-surface Broadband Output Window for Gyro-TWT
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A meta-surface output window for Ka-band TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> mode gyrotron traveling wave tubes (gyro-TWT) is proposed, which can effectively match the dielectric constant perfectly and expand the bandwidth of the output window. The physical mechanism of the output window is investigated by theory and simulation. On the basis of theoretical calculation, the main structural parameters were optimized by high frequency simulation software. When the window operates in TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> mode in Ka-band(26.5GHz-40GHz), the frequency range of the reflection less than -20dB is from 27-40.6GHz and transmission is over 0.11dB. The tolerance analysis are investigated and analyzed, which show that the thickness h$_{1}h_{2}$ and the gap g have less effect on the performance within ± 0.01 mm.

articleTitle: A Practical Co-Design of a Scanning 1D-MIMO Array and Parallel Imaging Algorithm for Security Screening
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
