abstract: A sparse 1D-MIMO array working around 30 GHz is designed and a precise wavenumber algorithm applicable for scanning imaging is tailored and optimized to meet the realistic personnel screening needs. Simulations show that by utilizing wide-beamwidth antennas, a cross-range resolution better than 5 mm can be reached. With a parallel implementation, a fully focused 3D image of size 1 m $\times {2\mathbf{m}} \times 0.4$ m with $576\times 1000\times 70$ voxels can be obtained within 0.6 seconds.

articleTitle: Simulation Study on the Nonstationary Behavior in a Terahertz Gyrotron
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The nonstationary behavior in a TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">02</inf> mode 140-GHz gyrotron has been investigated by 3-D PIC simulation. Simulation results reveal that the gyrotron transitions from stationary state into nonstationary state with the increase of the beam current. Moreover, the axial mode competition is observed when the gyrotron is in a nonstationary state.

articleTitle: Multifunctional Ionic-Gated Graphene Salisbury Mirror Supercapacitor, with Saturable Absorption, Amplitude Modulation and Frequency-Tuning Capabilities in the 2-5 THz Range
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We report an electrolyte-gated single layer graphene super-capacitor, embedded in a polyethylene-on-Au Salisbury mirror optical architecture, working as a THz frequency modulator. The gate-tunable single layer graphene in a quarter wave waveguide ensures 40% optical amplitude modulation depth, and saturable absorption mirror operation, with $\sim 4.5 Wcm^{\mathbf{-2}}$ saturation intensity. By coupling the modulator with a THz quantum cascade laser frequency comb in an external cavity configuration, we also demonstrate fine-tuning of the intermode beatnote frequency, revealing a promising perspective for metrological sources requiring a tight frequency control of the intermode comb frequency

articleTitle: Automatic detection of defects in composite structures by the Dynamic Time Warping method
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The paper presents the results of validation tests of the prepared samples, containing damages and defects that may occur in composite and hybrid structures used in aviation. The research was carried out with the use of a time domain spectroscopy (TDS) scanner. Moreover, an attempt was made to automate the process of analyzing the obtained results, using the method of dynamic time wrapping (DTW). The authors used the DTW method to automatically compare time signals without defects (reference) and signals potentially containing defects, which then allowed to locate the defects in the tested composite plate and to determine the depth of their occurrence.

articleTitle: Terahertz microresonators for silicon material characterisation
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The quality factor of rapidly emerging silicon terahertz microresonator devices is ultimately limited by the intrinsic material absorption. We investigate the significance of the silicon substrate’s resistivity on the quality factor, and determine the material absorption as a function of resistivity. In general, the presented methodology is ideally suited to precisely measure the material absorption of low-loss materials in the THz domain, which is challenging using conventional THz spectroscopy.

articleTitle: Quantum-probe Field Microscope (QFIM) films THz-Nearfield Evolutions
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We demonstrate a novel ultrafast electric field microscopy for sub-wavelength and sub-cycle imaging of nearfield waveforms at THz frequencies. Based on the fluorescence of semiconductor quantum-dots as local field probes, we acquire ultrafast movies of dynamic electric field evolutions inside broadband THz-antennas and of propagating THz-excitations in metallic waveguides using an optical microscope. This flexible scheme allows for local time-domain spectroscopy more than 100x below the diffraction limit and provides field-resolved access to field-driven and strong-field dynamics inside active metamaterials.

articleTitle: THz Imaging System with a Single Resonant Tunneling Diode Transceiver in 300-GHz Band
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: To reduce the cost of terahertz (THz) imaging systems, we propose an active THz imaging system in which both transmitting and receiving are performed using a single resonant tunneling diode (RTD) transceiver. The self-mixing phenomenon of the RTD was used for 2D imaging with a spatial resolution of ~0.8 mm. To increase imaging speed, fast 2D imaging was demonstrated using the beam scanning. The data acquisition time was shortened from 188 to 6 seconds for the imaging area of 60 × 90 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Phase-averaged imaging by controlling the bias voltage of the RTD was proposed to reduce imaging artifacts caused by the interference effect.

articleTitle: A High-order THz Amplitude Modulator Based on Subarray Coding Metamaterial
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this paper, a high-order THz amplitude modulator based on subarray coding strategy is proposed. The HEMT is integrated into the metal microstructure, and the modulation state can be changed by adjusting the voltage to form a 1-bit amplitude modulation unit. Furthermore, we divide and encode the artificial microstructure array to enable joint modulation between subarrays and realize multi-bit high-order amplitude modulation of THz wave through different subarray coding sequences. This work may promote the development of THz quasi-optical modulators, especially high-order amplitude modulation.

articleTitle: Development of Synthetic Diagnostics Platform for Microwave Imaging Diagnostics on EAST
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Microwave imaging diagnostics provide important visualization informations for the study of MHD and turbulence behaviors in tokamaks. In non-ideal conditions it is difficult to interpreting experimental data. With the advancement of computing power, synthetic diagnostics based on the first-principle has been developed and widely used. In this work a synthetic diagnostics platform serving for electron cyclotron emission imaging (ECEI) and microwave imaging reflectometer (MIR) on tokamak has been developed. Benchmarks and cross-validation have been conducted.

articleTitle: Phase-sensitive hyperspectral near-field nanoscope based on self-induced phase locking of terahertz frequency combs
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present a self-mixing intermode-beatnote spectroscopy system, based on a THz quantum cascade laser operating as a frequency comb (FC). The emitted radiation is back-scattered from the tip of a scanning near-field optical-microscope (s-SNOM), which allows to exploit the sensitivity of FC phase-coherence to optical feedback to manipulate the frequency, amplitude and linewidth of the intermode FC beatnote. By stabilizing the phase-locked regimes, we demonstrate, for the first time, a FC based hyper-spectral, THz s-SNOM nanoscope providing coherent detection of multiple phase-locked modes and mapping of the THz near-field response of materials in the 2.29-3.6 THz range, with noise-equivalent-powers of $\sim 400pW/\sqrt{\mathrm{H}}\mathrm{z}$.

articleTitle: Improvements in Windowless Spectroscopy: 3D Printed Nozzles
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present nozzle designs for colliding stream nozzles manufactured from commercially available projection micro-stereolithography that produce highly stable liquid flatjets. Depending on the nozzle geometry, the sheet thickness can be varied between 14 and 43 μm. The sheet thickness is stable over 100 hours and varies by less than 1% of its thickness.

articleTitle: Inhomogeneity Influence on Spintronic Terahertz Emission from Pt/CoFeB/W by Laser Terahertz Emission Microscopy
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The inhomogeneity influence on terahertz (THz) radiation from Pt/CoFeB/W heterostructure has been investigated via scanning the nanofilm surface and recording the THz signals by laser THz emission microscopy driven by femtosecond fiber laser.

articleTitle: Towards terahertz imaging applications at Stonehenge for identification of prehistoric carvings
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Prehistoric carvings on the stone surfaces of Stonehenge may lie undiscovered beneath shrubby layers of lichen. We assess the suitability of terahertz time domain imaging as a subsurface imaging technique for archaeologists to identify carvings obscured by lichen. In a lab setting, we show that lichen at low water content does not completely obscure carvings on stone using terahertz imagery, and that the fainter returns from the stone surface can still be leveraged to give a basic view of the stone topography beneath lichen.

articleTitle: Phase profile optimization of silicon multi-phase zone plate lenses for operation at 585 GHz frequency
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Phase profile of the multi-phase zone plate (MPZP) was optimized for efficient lens operation at 0.585 THz frequency. Different type of the MPZP samples with a focal length of about 13 mm and a focal number of 1 were designed of high-resistivity silicon. The depth and size of initial eight step phase profile were optimized in the most outer subzone areas. Successful optimization of the phase profile allowed us to reduce manufacturing complexity and achieve higher focusing gain values in comparison to respective classical design MPZP.

articleTitle: Three dimensional monolithic integrated miniaturized terahertz frequency doubler based on Z-direction input and XY plane four channel output
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The traditional frequency doubler structure is single input and single output. Its input and output structure is completely distributed on the XY plane. The structure is not compact, which makes the device size larger. According to the development trend of terahertz multi-channel communication system in the future, a three dimensional monolithic integrated miniaturized terahertz frequency doubler based on Z-direction input and XY plane four output is designed in this paper.The electromagnetic wave transmission direction is perpendicular to the substrate. Only two power division structures are used to realize four-way power output. Great innovation is realized in the structure, which makes the frequency multiplier more compact and ensures the consistency of phase and amplitude output from four channels. Finally, in the simulation, under the input of about 500mW, each channel has an output of more than 50mW in the bandwidth of 166GHz ~ 183GHz, with an efficiency of more than 40% and up to 42%.

articleTitle: THz ultra-strong light-matter coupling up to 200K with continuously-graded parabolic quantum wells embedded in microcavities
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: we demonstrate ultra-strong light-matter coupling up to 200K with continuously graded parabolic quantum wells inserted in metallic microcavities at THz frequencies. The harmonic quantization of the wavefunctions protects the intersubband (ISB) transition from Coulomb interactions that allows the measurement of an ISB polariton mode as low as 1.8 THz.

articleTitle: Investigation of Terahertz Radiation Interaction with Space-charge Domains in n-type Gallium Nitride
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Gallium nitride semiconductor was investigated in pulsed electric field, demonstrating interaction of terahertz radiation with space-charge domains propagating with a speed of acoustic waves. The modulation of terahertz optical transmission was investigated in two polarizations, indicating the differences for terahertz radiation polarized along and orthogonally to the electric field.

articleTitle: Low-barrier Schottky detector using nanowire contacts for zero-biased THz applications
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A Low-barrier Schottky detector (LBSD) for zero-biased Terahertz (THz) applications was developed using silver (Ag) metallic nanowires (NWs) with 120 nm diameter as bridge contacts on Indium Gallium Arsenide (InGaAs). A Schottky barrier height as low as 0.21 eV was obtained. This property leads to efficient zero-bias operation with a measured 3 dB roll-off frequency of about 1.2 THz and a noise equivalent power (NEP) of 7 pW/√Hz at 1 THz.

articleTitle: G-band Silicon-filled Waveguide Slot Antenna Array for Highly Integrated Application
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this paper, a G-band silicon-filled waveguide slot antenna array for highly integrated application is presented. The sidewalls are enclosed in gold-metal from all sides. The electromagnetic waves are radiated by slots etched on the top surface of the silicon. The slot array is distributed with unequal spacing to reduce the side lobes level. In addition, considering the fabrication and integrate with terahertz chips, a coplanar waveguide (CPW) to silicon-filled waveguide transition structure is designed. Simulated results demonstrate that a $1 \times 8$ slot array displays very lower side lobe levels, and with the gain of 6 dBi at the frequency of 206.4 GHz. The silicon-based waveguide enables highly integrated terahertz system, since it allows for downscaling the waveguide’s cross section by a factor of about 2.3, compared to an air-filled waveguide.

articleTitle: Mid-infrared Exosome Detection with Plasmonic Nanoantenna Arrays
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Exosomes are nano-sized extracellular vesicles considered as a promising source of cancer biomarkers originating from the parent cells. We develop mid-infrared plasmonic nanoantenna arrays to detect, in the liquid phase, the specific vibrational absorption signal of the protein cargo of exosomes. The unspecific refractive index change is simultaneously detected by the same plasmonic array to monitor the reaction dynamics.

articleTitle: Quasi-optical output for a high gain, broadband W-band amplifier
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The gyrotron-traveling wave amplifier (gyro-TWA), operating in W-band has previously been shown to provide an unsaturated output power of 3.4 kW over a 3-dB bandwidth of 9196.5 GHz in single pulse (350 ns) operation. The output section of the gyro-TWA was critical to maintaining the amplifier stability due to the 37 dB gain from a single gain section. This paper presents the re-design of the gyro-TWA output section suitable for several percent duty cycle and wideband operation over 90-100 GHz. We describe the design of the: wideband smooth output feedhorn, which couples to a fundamental Gaussian mode; the electron beam collector (forming part of the output horn), and the vacuum window. The feedhorn simulations predict a calculated >98% Gaussian efficiency and better than -30 dB return loss. The vacuum window is a multilayer design comprising three window discs: two quartz and one alumina. The predicted return loss is lower than -30 dB over the operating range.

articleTitle: Quantitative Sampling of Atom-Scale Terahertz Waveforms
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Atomic light-matter interaction depends critically on the absolute strength and the precise time evolution of the near field, which may be strongly influenced by quantum-mechanical effects. Yet, quantitatively measuring ultrafast near-field waveforms on atomic scales has remained an open challenge. Using a molecular switch as a local field sensor, we sample the temporal shape and strength of atomically confined light field transients.

articleTitle: Structural and electronic origin of spin-dependent interface resistance in spintronic Fe/Pt THz emitter by first-principles calculations
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Using first-principles methods based on spin density functional theory (SDFT) and multichannel Landauer formalism for spin-transport, we calculated the spin-dependent interface resistance arising from the interface potential barrier due to the shifts in minority (spin-up) and majority (spin-down) conduction bands between Fe and Pt in spintronic Fe/Pt THz emitter. We found that the spin-up interface resistance is lower than that of spin-down in agreement with previous interface reflectivity studies. This direct correlation of spin-transport to structural/electronic properties poses impact on the design of more efficient THz emitters.

articleTitle: Surface conductivity control with graphene sheets stacked between hafnium oxide layers
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Using overlapping graphene sheets and a hafnium oxide layer as an isolator, a graphene capacitor is manufactured. The voltage applied between sheets changes surface conductivity, which can be used for THz modulation or sensing applications. This research aimed to elucidate the basic characteristics of the graphene capacitor to evaluate its possibilities for application.

articleTitle: Using 3D printing and microfabrication techniques of TOPAS for THz lenses and detectors
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Cyclic olefin copolymer (TOPAS) is a polymer transparent for frequencies up to 10 THz. TOPAS can be used for various THz devices and components. This work reports the 3D printing and the microfabrication of THz devices from TOPAS, namely microfluidic devices, lenses, flexible detectors, and freestanding THz filters.

articleTitle: WR-1-Band Packaged Low-Loss Unclad Silicon Waveguide Module
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Hollow metallic waveguides have long been employed as interconnects in terahertz (THz) systems. However, these waveguides are associated with increased ohmic loss at higher frequencies. Herein, we propose a 50-mm-long, compact, packaged low-loss waveguide module using a silicon unclad waveguide with an input/output interface compatible with a standard WR-1 waveguide flange. The superiority of this module was experimentally validated. The results revealed an average total loss of 2 dB across the WR-1 band (0.75–1.1 THz), in contrast to a total loss of 9.3 dB for the 50-mm-long conventional hollow waveguide module.

articleTitle: Nanowire Sensors Facilitate Polarization Sensitive Terahertz Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Polarization sensitive terahertz time-domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS) is an extension to standard THz-TDS, where the main variables used in data analysis not only include the amplitude and phase but also the polarization state of the THz wave. This offers a deep insight into the anisotropy of many materials, and leads to the development of new THz techniques such as THz polarimetry and ellipsometry. Here we present a nanowire sensor technology that allows for practical realization of polarization sensitive THz-TDS systems.

articleTitle: High-Resolution Rotational Fourier-Transform Infrared Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We demonstrate a rotational optical delay line for Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy with simultaneous high time and frequency resolutions. Thanks to the rotational motion, the trade-off between speed and spectral resolution present in rapid-scan FTIRs is alleviated, and enables the use of high-brightness quantum cascade laser frequency combs as light sources. We demonstrate the capabilities of the delay line by resolving low-pressure methane absorption lines and tracking several absorption lines at video frame rates.

articleTitle: Terahertz Generation via Quantum Interference in Quadratic Media
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The quantum-interference terahertz generation mechanism is founded on the wavefunction interference between simultaneous photo-excitation elicited by pump and its coherent second-harmonic. Within the framework of non-centrosymmetric media it can be exploited to augment the optical-to-terahertz conversion limits. In particular, we demonstrate quantum-interference-mediated terahertz generation and control over its interference with simultaneous rectified generation in a quadratic non-centrosymmetric medium. © 2022 The authors

articleTitle: Water States Analysis of Anion Exchange Membranes with Terahertz Time-Domain Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2022 47th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Terahertz time-domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS) has been recently demonstrated to resolve water states inside industrially thin fuel cell membranes. In this work, we apply THz-TDS to anion exchange membranes (AEMs) where detailed water information is crucial to their stability and operational performance. By performing independent ionic conductivity measurement on said membranes, we show a good correlation against the extracted conductivities and resolved bulk water of three AEMs produced with different amination time.
